milestones.title: Milestone and DAG driven development
milestones.problem: Work in this repository was planned in conversation and in task records that describe one session at a time. There was no executable specification of an outcome, no dependency graph between pieces of work, and no way for a fresh worker to ask the repository what to do next. The tool supervises a task; nothing supervised the plan the task belonged to.
milestones.outcome: Every non-trivial change in this repository belongs to a milestone specification and to one dependency-linked issue execution contract, validated as a DAG, with status derived rather than asserted, and projected to GitHub and to the website from that one canonical model.
milestones.current_state: The canonical model, its engine, its CLI, its projections, its doctrines and its tests exist and are exercised by this milestone's own issues. GitHub carried no issues and no milestones before this work.
milestones.desired_state: A fresh worker with no conversation history runs `majordomus plan next`, receives one issue, executes it inside its declared scope, attaches evidence, and the graph recomputes what is ready without anybody editing a status field.
non_scope: A hosted planning backend or database
A second project-management vocabulary; milestones and issues are the only new nouns
Bidirectional GitHub write-back into the canonical files
Estimation, burndown, velocity or any scheduling model
acceptance_criteria: The canonical model parses, rejects unknown keys, and refuses a duplicate id
A dependency cycle, a self-dependency and an unknown dependency are each rejected with a named finding
READY, BLOCKED, ACTIVE, VERIFY, DONE and CANCELLED are derived from recorded facts and stored nowhere
Execution waves are computed from the graph, and overlapping scope inside one wave is reported
The Mermaid DAG is generated from the same graph the CLI reads
GitHub milestones and issues are created and updated from the canonical model, and drift between them is reported
The website renders the roadmap, every milestone, every issue and the DAG from generated data
Every surface agrees: the CLI, the site data and the GitHub projection report the same issue set and the same READY set
Changing one dependency changes every surface
CI refuses a push whose canonical model is invalid or whose generated artifacts are stale
risks: The engine is shell and awk; a graph large enough to make that slow would need a different implementation. Measured, not assumed.
GitHub is a projection. If a human edits a generated issue body, the next sync reports drift rather than silently overwriting it, which means drift can accumulate unattended.

evidence.result: every case in test/cases passed and none failed, each in a disposable repository
1 passed — the CLI, the JSON output, the Mermaid diagram, the GitHub projection and a freshly generated site-data file agree on every set they can be asked about
1 passed — every canonical mutation the case makes moves every surface
every milestone and issue the model held at this commit existed on korczis/prismatic-majordomus with its state matching the derived status; check exited 0 with no drift

milestones.title: A blocking question survives a handover
milestones.problem: An open question is the mechanism for stopping acceptance when work depends on a person. It is attached to the task that opened it, and the gate only reads questions belonging to the active task. Handing over and starting a new task therefore leaves the question unresolved and no longer blocking anything, so the one thing that was supposed to refuse a completed finish refuses nothing. The gap was found by running the documented end-to-end sequence, not by review, and it is published as a planned claim with no implementation and no test.
milestones.outcome: An unresolved question keeps refusing a completed finish after the work moves to a new task, or the alternative is chosen deliberately and the reason is recorded where the next worker will read it.
milestones.current_state: docs/CLAIMS.yaml carries blocker-survives-handover as planned, with implementation and test both '-'. lib/question.sh matches unresolved lines by the active task id; lib/check.sh reads only those. Nothing detects that a handover has orphaned a blocker.
milestones.desired_state: The behaviour is decided between two named alternatives, implemented, proved by a behavioural case, and the claim moves from planned to guaranteed with its implementation and test filled in.
non_scope: A question that blocks across repositories or worktrees
Assigning a question to a person, or notifying anybody
Any change to the finish contract's other lines
acceptance_criteria: A behavioural case demonstrates the current escape, so the gap is executable rather than asserted
The choice between transferring the question and widening the gate is recorded as a decision with what was rejected and why
The chosen behaviour is implemented and a case fails when it is removed
The claim in docs/CLAIMS.yaml moves to guaranteed with a real implementation path and a real test path
The claim detail page states what the behaviour does not cover
risks: Transferring a question with a handover makes it a property of the work rather than of the task, which is right in the common case and wrong when the handover is to a different piece of work. Widening the gate to every unresolved question blocks tasks that never opened one. The decision has to name the case it is choosing to be wrong in.

evidence.result: the case runs the documented sequence and the mutation section reproduces the escape from a probe that narrows the gate back to the active task, so the gap is executable rather than described
the choice, both rejected alternatives with the case each gets wrong, and the two conditions the choice imposed on the implementation

evidence.command: bash test/run.sh 50_blocker_across_handover && bash test/run.sh 25_continuity_lifecycle && bin/majordomus doctor
evidence.result: exit 0, 85s — recorded as this task's verification; an inherited blocker refuses a completed finish, any task can clear it, and the shipped template is not an entry

milestones.title: A durable record names the worker that wrote it
milestones.problem: Every durable record is attributed to the task that is active in the checkout, because decision, checkpoint and question all read .majordomus/state/current.yaml to find out whose work they belong to. Several workers share one checkout, so the record names whoever started a task there rather than whoever ran the command. In one evening three sessions wrote under another session's active task, and one decision had to be dropped by hand after the fact because the premise it recorded belonged to somebody else. Attribution is the one property of a record that cannot be reconstructed later: the conversation that would settle it is gone.
milestones.outcome: A durable record either names the worker that produced it or is refused, and a record written from one session can never arrive attributed to another session's task.
milestones.current_state: Not started. lib/decision.sh, lib/checkpoint.sh and lib/question.sh each resolve the active task from the checkout and write it into the record. Nothing distinguishes two workers sharing that checkout, and nothing reports that it cannot.
milestones.desired_state: Attribution is verifiable from the record alone. Where the tool cannot establish who wrote something, it says so and refuses rather than guessing from what happens to be active.
non_scope: A registry of named workers, personas or agents
Any identity the repository has to maintain, or that outlives the session that used it
Locking a checkout to one worker
acceptance_criteria: A record written while another worker's task is active is attributed correctly or refused by name
The attribution can be checked from the record alone, with no conversation history
No new record type and no registry of workers is introduced
A behavioural case reproduces two workers writing in one checkout
risks: The obvious fix is an identity the tool maintains, which is a registry of named workers by another name and is refused everywhere else in this repository. Whatever is chosen has to be supplied by the session and stored only inside the record it explains.
Refusing to write an unattributable record can lose a decision somebody was trying to make. The refusal has to say what to run instead, in the same breath.

milestones.title: A session is a durable envelope, and knowledge is compiled from what is already canonical
milestones.problem: Continuity today is task-shaped. A task record says what one piece of work is, and checkpoints, handovers, decisions and questions hang off it. Nothing represents the execution episode itself — the worker sat down, touched three tasks, recorded two decisions, closed one issue, and stopped — so the causal question a later worker actually asks is unanswerable from the records: which work happened together, in what order, against which commits, and what did it decide. The second gap is retrieval. `search` is a literal scan over six operational record kinds, which is right for those files and blind to everything else: the claims matrix, the milestone and issue contracts, the policy, the profiles, the prompts and the documents already carry explicit, machine-readable relationships — claim to implementation to test, issue to milestone to dependency, evidence to issue — and no command can traverse one of them. A worker therefore reconstructs both from a conversation, which is the thing that does not survive.
milestones.outcome: A worker with no conversation history can answer what happened, why, what was decided, which evidence supports it, where the canonical source lives, and what to do next — from records and a derived index, with git still the authority over both.
milestones.current_state: There is no session concept: `.majordomus/state/` holds task, checkpoint, handover, decision, question and ledger, and the ledger is the only thing that knows two records were written by the same episode, which it knows only by adjacency in time. There is no index of any kind; docs/CONTINUITY.md states that as a deliberate choice for the record corpus and says nothing about the rest of the repository. docs/DESIGN.md's Clean Extraction Boundary excludes graph semantics absolutely, which forbids even a provenance graph derived from this repository's own files.
milestones.desired_state: A session lifecycle exists with one active session per worktree and immutable closed records that reference authoritative records rather than copying them, and whose whole reference envelope is derived from the ledger instead of accumulated by hand. A knowledge compiler discovers curated sources through git, extracts nodes with identities that survive a rebuild, records edges only where an explicit relationship was observed, keeps a content-hash manifest that makes a no-op sync cheap, and answers read-only queries without mutating anything. `context` can select a bounded slice of it. Both are declared doctrines with validators that doctor and watch dispatch, and the boundary between shared and operational knowledge is a tested property rather than a convention.
non_scope: Any database, embedding, vector store, or similarity ranking
Any model invocation, network call, or generated summary
A second mutable narrative store that copies decisions, questions or checkpoint bodies
Publishing operational records to the website
Renderer-specific knowledge output for any particular note-taking application
Inferring a relationship from prose that does not state it explicitly
acceptance_criteria: A session opens, closes, and its closed record is immutable, temporally ordered, and interpretable against current git through the existing divergence vocabulary
A closed session names the tasks, issues, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and questions of its episode by reference, and copies none of their bodies
Knowledge discovery is driven by git rather than by a filesystem walk, and an untracked file is not a source
A node identity survives a rebuild, and editing one source changes only the nodes derived from it
Every edge carries the file it was observed in; an edge without provenance is a validation failure
A second sync with no source change reports no work and is measurably cheaper than a cold one
Every read-only knowledge and session command leaves `git status` byte-identical
Shared and operational knowledge are separable, and a test proves the shared projection contains no operational record
`context` can carry a bounded knowledge section that is dropped before any immutable fact and is named under EXCLUDED when it is
Each new guarantee is a declared doctrine with a validator that doctor and watch dispatch, a claim, and a behavioural case
docs/CONTINUITY.md and docs/DESIGN.md state the new architecture precisely instead of contradicting it
risks: A knowledge index is a second thing that can be believed. Every mitigation is the same one: the index is a pointer, it carries the source path and hash of what it points at, and it is reported stale rather than silently rebuilt by a query.

A curated source list is a place where something can be forgotten. The alternative — indexing everything git tracks — imports generated files, vendored trees and site output, and was rejected; the cost is that adding a canonical file kind is an explicit edit, and the validator names a declared source class whose discovery returns nothing.

Deriving a session's references from the ledger makes the ledger load-bearing for a second thing. It is already append-only, machine-written and validated by majordomus.ledger-integrity, and the alternative — accumulating references into a mutable session file on every command — puts a write on the hot path of every other command and creates the second store this milestone exists to avoid.

The Clean Extraction Boundary currently forbids graph semantics without qualification. Narrowing it is a deliberate change to a published boundary, and it must be narrowed precisely — a generic provenance graph over this repository's own artifacts — or it stops being a boundary.

milestones.title: Performance is executable evidence, and the hot path does no canonical work twice
milestones.problem: The shell tool is slow enough to be avoided: doctor takes ten seconds and runs on every commit through the pre-commit hook, watch takes the same, knowledge nodes six seconds, plan validate four, the site-data check and a single test case half a minute, and the suite half an hour. Nobody could say which phase paid for it, because nothing measured phases; the two validators that cost two thirds of doctor are loops of one awk process per key over files that were already flattened once. The Rust executable measured at the same time is fast, so the slowness is the shell tool's own.
milestones.outcome: Every public command can be benchmarked from the command registry with cold and warm distributions, the phases and work counters of any run can be printed, the caches and batch reads that remove repeated work preserve every observable result, an accepted baseline lives in the repository and a check refuses a regression by policy, and the pre-commit hook is fast enough that nobody routes around it.
milestones.current_state: MJ_TIMING prints per-validator phases and two work counters (feature/performance-truth 77f5d79). No benchmark command, no baseline, no regression check, no parse cache, no performance doctrine; the numbers above are the measured baseline on this repository.
milestones.desired_state: majordomus bench derives its targets from share/commands.yaml, records p50, p90, p95, p99, min, max, mean and stddev per command and mode, persists local runs under .ai/local/benchmarks/, compares against .ai/repo/benchmarks/baseline.json under the policy's benchmark block, and exits non-zero on a regression. Registry, catalogue, project-model and coverage validators read each flat file once. Flattened YAML is cached under .ai/local/cache/ by content hash. Project rules state the doctrine, docs/PERFORMANCE.md explains it, and CI runs the structural checks.
non_scope: Any change to apps/majordomus-cli, whose measured latency is not the problem
A metrics database, a dashboard, a tracing backend or any telemetry service
Hot reload or filesystem watching
A persistent capability result cache across processes beyond the flatten cache
Benchmarking external services
acceptance_criteria: Every public command in share/commands.yaml is a benchmark target without a second list anywhere
Cold and warm distributions are recorded separately with p50, p95 and p99 and never mixed
A local run is persisted under .ai/local/benchmarks/ and never treated as a baseline
The committed baseline is updated only by an explicit command on a clean tree
bench --check exits non-zero on a regression over the policy thresholds and names the command, the metric, both values and the threshold
Every canonical file is flattened at most once per command, proved by the work counters in a case
A cache hit and a cache miss produce byte-identical command output for every read-only command, proved by a case
doctor on this repository runs under the budget the policy declares, and the pre-commit hook inherits it
The performance rules are project rules under .ai/repo/rules/project, and docs/PERFORMANCE.md is the reference the README points at
risks: A cache is a second thing that can be believed. The flatten cache is keyed by the content hash of the file it caches, so a stale entry cannot be read for a changed file; it can only cost a miss.
Wall-clock thresholds are noisy across machines. The regression policy is conservative and relative, the structural counters are exact, and only the counters gate CI strictly.
Batching reads changes how validators are written. Each rewrite is proved by the case that already exists for the validator, run before and after, plus the counter case.

milestones.title: A change is derived in under a second and judged in minutes, and nothing that could have changed is skipped
milestones.problem: The owner should never wait on the toolchain for a change that touched little. An ordinary derive finishes in under a second. A pull request's required verdict arrives within five minutes. Both are measured and enforced, and the speed comes from not repeating work whose inputs did not move, never from weakening a gate. Proposed in ADR 0185 (A derivation is a typed graph of the generators the executable already plans, keyed by the content of what each node reads, and the full derive stays its oracle); ADR 0186 (A pull request's required verdict is the feedback lane, a gate whose inputs did not change is reused as inputs_unchanged, and the proof lane judges the combined top before it lands); ADR 0187 (Tests are selected by the impact of a change, derived from what each case declares it reads, and a change of unknown impact runs every case) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c208#3, chatgpt-majordomus:c208#24, chatgpt-majordomus:c228#0, chatgpt-majordomus:c292#0.
milestones.outcome: The owner should never wait on the toolchain for a change that touched little. An ordinary derive finishes in under a second. A pull request's required verdict arrives within five minutes. Both are measured and enforced, and the speed comes from not repeating work whose inputs did not move, never from weakening a gate.

milestones.title: A claim that something is enforced, tested or delivered stands only on recorded evidence that would have caught it being false
milestones.problem: The owner wants every rule, guarantee and delivered feature that Majordomus states to be backed by a recorded execution at the revision being shown. For a blocking rule, that execution shows a violation being refused. Every way around a gate (an override, a disabled protection, a proposed decision cited as law) must be visible. Any statement that lacks this evidence reads as not proven on every surface, never as done. Proposed in ADR 0188 (A rule's proof of effect is a recorded refusal of its violation, not the presence of its wiring) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). milestones.title: A derivation computed once is reused by every worktree and by CI, and the incremental path becomes the default on evidence
milestones.problem: A derivation is computed again wherever it is needed. Each linked worktree runs its own derive of a tree another worktree may already have derived, one at a time behind a machine-wide lock held for the whole run, and the CI site job regenerates the site data to compare it. Nothing keeps an output by the key of the inputs that produced it, so a node computed a minute ago in a sibling checkout is computed again. The owner's brief of 2026-10-12 asks for a persistent content-addressed store with verified restore and bounded eviction (campaigns/majordomus-incremental-derive-prompt-pack/05_05_CAS_STORE.md), safe reuse across worktrees (08_08_PARALLEL_WORKTREES.md), reuse in GitHub Actions under the same graph (09_09_CI_GITHUB_CACHE.md) and a guarded rollout to the default (12_12_ROLLOUT_PROVE.md).
milestones.outcome: A node's outputs are kept under its key outside every work tree, restored only after their digests are verified, bounded in size and age, and shared by the worktrees of one machine and by CI runs. The machine lock covers the moment a worktree's files are written and no longer the computation. The incremental path is the default only after the differential case, the measurements and a rollback case exist, and scripts/derive --full remains.
milestones.current_state: Read on 2026-10-13, not re-read when revived on 2026-10-18. No store of derived outputs exists. lib/machine_lock.sh takes one lock per machine for the whole of scripts/derive (rule project.one-derive-at-a-time, case 1018). Worktrees share cargo's intermediate build directory and keep their own artifacts (.cargo/config.toml build-dir, ADR 0139, case 1022). majordomus offload derive queues a full derive on another host (docs/OFFLOAD.md, I2398). .github/workflows/validate.yml caches the Rust build and the npm install, and its site job runs scripts/generate-site-data --check in full. I1409 records that generated content is machine-dependent in places: an abbreviated commit id depends on the local object store and a shallow checkout writes a different changelog.
milestones.desired_state: A store resolved from git's common directory holds, per node key, a manifest and the output bytes. A hit is restored after every digest is checked and a damaged entry is a miss that says so. Two worktrees computing one key compute it once. The store reports its size and is reclaimed by an explicit command under the disk rule. The CI site job restores from a cache keyed by the graph and still compares the committed bytes. scripts/derive runs incrementally by default on the platforms where the evidence exists, and one command returns to the full path.
non_scope: The graph, the keys and the incremental run themselves: milestone a-derive-does-only-the-work-its-inputs-changed.
A remote store service, or sharing entries between machines over the mesh. The offload host keeps a store of its own like any other machine.
Archiving cargo's target directory. The compiler cache is ADR 0139's and the CI Rust cache's.
Restoring an entry written by a pull request's run into a release or Pages publication.
Removing scripts/derive --full or scripts/derive-check.
acceptance_criteria: A restored node's tracked files are byte-identical to a full derive's, and a truncated manifest, a mismatched digest or an entry of an older schema is reported as a miss and regenerated
The store refuses an output path outside the repository root, a path through a symbolic link and a restore over a file no node owns
Two worktrees deriving the same key at once run the producer once, and a holder that is killed does not leave the other waiting past a bound
The store's size is reported by a capability, and entries are removed only by an explicit command that spares entries in use
The CI site job fails on a stale committed artifact whether or not the cache was restored, and a missing cache falls back to generation
With the incremental path as default, scripts/derive --full produces the same bytes, and a case proves the return to the full path
Every duration published about the change names its commit, machine, cache state and sample count
risks: A store shared by every worktree is one more quantity that fills the disk, which ADR 0055 makes a measured quantity reclaimed by predicate. The bound and the reclaim land with the store, not after it.
Machine-dependent content (I1409) makes an entry computed on one machine wrong on another unless the key covers what differs; until it does, reuse stays inside one machine and one CI runner image.
Narrowing the derive lock changes rule project.one-derive-at-a-time; a mistake interleaves two writers in one tree.
A cache restored from an untrusted run is an injection path into a privileged job.

milestones.title: An ordinary derive answers in under a second, runs independent nodes in parallel, and a budget gate holds it
milestones.problem: The 10-13 graph plan makes a derive do less, but it sets no time budget, runs nodes one at a time and publishes file by file. The owner's 10-17 order asks for 'sub second, in parallel' with every algorithm, cache and architectural choice reviewed. ChatGPT's own reply (c292#1) called sub-second without benchmarks 'marketing'. Proposed in ADR 0185 (A derivation is a typed graph of the generators the executable already plans, keyed by the content of what each node reads, and the full derive stays its oracle) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c292#0, chatgpt-majordomus:c292#2.
milestones.outcome: Derive scenarios (no-op, one input, batch, plus the ten of c255#7) are bench targets under the existing benchmark policy. bench --check refuses a regression. milestones.title: A derive does only the work its inputs changed, and can say why
milestones.problem: Every derive regenerates everything. scripts/derive builds the executable, runs majordomus generate over every target, runs scripts/generate-site-data over the whole site (use-case scenarios included), runs majordomus generate over every target a second time and rewrites the merge policy, whatever changed; a one-line edit of a rule costs what a change to the generator costs, and docs/OFFLOAD.md records that cost as about ten minutes on an idle machine and up to an hour on the shared one. The order of the stages is a comment at the top of a shell script, so nothing can be asked which producer owns an output or which inputs it read. The owner's brief of 2026-10-12, campaigns/majordomus-incremental-derive-prompt-pack/README.md, asks for the full regeneration to be replaced by a typed, content-addressed, incremental derivation graph without weakening the full derivation or the freshness checks; its pages 01 to 04, 06, 07, 10 and 11 are what this milestone plans.
milestones.outcome: The derivation is a typed graph the executable owns: every producer is a node with declared inputs and outputs, every node has a key computed from the bytes it reads, a read-only plan says for each node whether it would be reused or regenerated and why, and an incremental run regenerates only the nodes whose keys moved. The full derivation stays as the oracle, and a test holds the incremental result byte-identical to it.
milestones.current_state: Read on 2026-10-13, not re-read when revived on 2026-10-18. scripts/derive runs, under the machine's derive lock (lib/machine_lock.sh), a cargo build unless MAJORDOMUS_BIN is set, then stage A (majordomus generate --strict, all 17 targets of Target::ALL in apps/majordomus-cli/src/generate.rs), stage B (scripts/generate-site-data, 2622 lines of shell, which runs majordomus usecase run for every scenario), stage C (the same generate over all targets again) and stage D (scripts/gitattributes). No stage is skipped when its inputs are unchanged; the only saving is that generate::write leaves a file alone when its bytes already match. scripts/generate-site-data carries one fingerprint over its whole input list (--fingerprint, --inputs), and its --check stages a full generation and diffs it. The executable has no derive command; majordomus offload derive moves the same full derive to another machine. test/cases/400_derivation_is_one_graph.sh proves the stage order with stand-in generators. .github/workflows/validate.yml allows generate-site-data --check 2700 seconds.
milestones.desired_state: One module of the crate declares the derivation graph and answers it as a capability. A derive on a tree whose inputs did not change runs no generator. A changed input regenerates the nodes that read it and the nodes downstream of them, and no others. majordomus derive plan and majordomus derive explain answer what would run and why without writing. scripts/derive --full and scripts/derive-check keep their behaviour and exit codes, and a case compares the two paths byte for byte.
non_scope: A store of outputs shared between worktrees or with CI, and making the incremental path the default: milestone a-derivation-computed-once-is-reused.
Narrowing what a committed fingerprint covers so that an unrelated merge does not invalidate it: milestone derived-data-integrity and I1409.
Rewriting scripts/generate-site-data in Rust. Its sections become nodes of the graph; its migration off shell is the automation inventory's (ADR 0069).
A daemon, a database or a second scheduler outside the crate.
Weakening scripts/derive-check, the derived merge driver or the generation guard that refuses a borrowed executable.
acceptance_criteria: One capability answers the derivation graph, and every path in docs/generated/artifacts.json and every tree scripts/generate-site-data publishes belongs to exactly one node of it
A graph with a cycle, an output claimed by two nodes or a generator no node declares is refused, and the refusal names the node
A node's key changes when a declared input is edited, renamed, deleted or added and when the executable's generation changes, and does not change when an undeclared path changes
A second incremental derive on an unchanged tree runs no generator and writes no file
A missing or altered output is regenerated even when the node's key did not move
For every fixture of the differential case, the tracked files an incremental derive leaves are byte-identical to those of a full derive, deletions included
derive plan and derive explain write nothing, and explain names the input that moved a node's key
scripts/derive-check exits 0, 10 and 15 for the same trees as before
risks: An input a generator reads and the graph does not declare is silent in the dangerous direction: the node is reused and the tree is stale while every check that trusts the key reads green. scripts/derive-check must go on comparing bytes, and the differential case must include a deliberately omitted edge.
ADR 0041 holds that inputs unchanged is not proof. A reused node is a saving in a derive and never a verdict in a gate.
Stage B is shell and runs scenarios with effects in temporary repositories; declaring its reads completely may cost more than the split saves, in which case the node stays coarse.
The subsystem is touched by every branch, so each change lands into contention with whatever else is deriving.

milestones.title: A finish reads what its work serves
milestones.problem: A task now starts bound to the issue and the intent it serves, and the intent engine says which criteria are met and which guards are violated. Finish asks neither. A worker can finish completed while the criterion the work exists for has no evidence.
milestones.outcome: The completion policy asks the intent engine what stands for the work a task named, refuses completed while a served criterion is unmet or a guard is violated where the policy says completed means complete, and decides nothing about any intent.
milestones.current_state: The completion policy and finish semantics are pull request 821; the binding, the opposition, the verdict with guards and evaluations are the intent stack. The two meet in no line of code. Revived on 2026-10-18 from the rescue of 2026-10-09, because the milestone never landed; its dependency on intent-satisfaction was dropped, because no milestone of that id exists on master. Re-read on 2026-10-18 for the IDD plan, against master of 2026-10-17: ADR 0107 and case 895 keep completion and intent satisfaction apart; the #821 completion policy exists only on rescue refs. It revives milestone finish-reads-what-its-work-serves of origin/rescue/d1/feature/a-finish-reads-what-its-work-serves (2026-10-09) under its own id, because that record's order, its dependency on a milestone master does not have, and the ADR number it names do not hold on master.
milestones.desired_state: An ADR records the decision and its measurement, under a number allocated above the high-water mark when it is written (0115 on the unlanded rescue, which master never received); a policy key says whether an owed answer refuses; two questions of the completion policy are answered from intents.binding; the documents and the claim say what finish asks.

acceptance_criteria: Where the policy requires it, finish with the outcome completed is refused while a served required criterion is unmet or a guard is violated

No intent record, stage or verdict is written by any finish

milestones.problem: The owner's report of 2026-10-19 (T1) asks that at least one repository not created or structured around Majordomus be connected. scripts/ci/install-check:17-27 ends when the installed launcher serves a freshly initialised empty repository, and test/cases/1024_an_installed_release_serves_a_foreign_repository.sh:10 uses a local fixture only. I3127 adds the refuse-then-accept stage on a fixture and is BLOCKED, because its milestone a-stranger-adopts-it-unaided depends on a-second-adopter-is-served, which site/data/generated/plan.json derives as ACTIVE. milestones.title: A session leaves what it observed, and the repository routes it
milestones.problem: What a session learns about the tool reaches the repository only when a person writes it up by hand: on 2026-10-08 four sessions produced thirty-six observations of friction (a fast-forward tripping the scope check, a stale rustdoc surface, a gate passing on zero support, a number taken in an uncommitted worktree), and every one lives in an agent's private memory or a chat message. The knowledge pipeline of ADR 0091 already derives candidates at the episode boundary without a model, but from four acts only (a decision, a resolved question, a finished task), keyed by episode, so the same defect seen twice is two files, and with no route to the owner that should act. The friction the ledger records — task.refused, a failing task.gate — is written and never read.
milestones.outcome: Any worker records an observation in one command; the episode boundary derives a candidate that says what it is about and who should look; reading groups recurrence by subject; an episode with nothing to say records that it found nothing.

Upstream transport

milestones.title: A session proceeds through the mesh: it finds the work, claims it once, runs it watched and stops when the intent is met
milestones.problem: Realising an intent is still a sequence a person runs: /proceed names work but nothing claims it, starts it exactly once, fans it out, reports it or schedules the next step; a stuck or dead loop is found by a person; heavy work starves on one lock; idle servers and deleting pushes cost the machine minutes. The pieces exist as unpushed stacks (I2972-I2976, I3040, ADR 0177) and as Mission Control findings B1 to B6, and none of them is one path.
milestones.outcome: A session asks /proceed what to do, receives one idempotent work order derived from intent_realization and the claim-aware plan, takes it under a mesh claim held by the run, starts it once, reports it and schedules its own next step until the intent is met; /watchdog wakes, hands over and reaps a stalled loop from deadlines; heavy work shares the machine through one slot.
milestones.current_state: Planned only. Records I4000 to I4009 and cases 4000 to 4009 exist as plan; no code is written by this milestone's planning pull request.
milestones.desired_state: Every satisfaction criterion of the intent is proved by its case; no new store, scheduler, journal kind or registry exists; every projection is generated.
non_scope: Push assignment of work to peers before I3198
Changing a profile automatically from inferred routing
Editing a person's .claude/settings.json or personal commands
acceptance_criteria: a fresh session in a supervised repository is told by /proceed which admissible work to take, derived from intent_realization and the claim-aware plan.next, with no question asked of a person

two sessions asking for work at once never receive the same item: the item's mesh claim is taken in the handler before any worker starts, an overlap is refused with a reason, and the claim is released when the run ends
a proceeding loop that stopped is detected from deadlines and events, woken, its handover published and resumed by another session, and reaped only by its owner or a seat after assess-before-deleting
a stuck or silent session is signalled by a phase deadline and a liveness event, never by polling, and the signal names the claim, the holder and the overdue phase

heavy work (pre-push, coverage, builds) takes one of N machine-wide slots with the disk floor read from rule data; a full queue answers a bounded wait naming its holders, and an idle serve and a deleting push cost the machine nothing
a /proceed step on an intent whose realisation is met answers that it is done and schedules no next step
an implement request runs once: a repeated executions.start with the same idempotency key answers the same execution id and a double click never starts two executions (Mission Control)
risks: The liveness substrate I3990-I3994 and the fencing epoch I3174 are other sessions' work; I4004 and I4009 name them and write none of them.
The /proceed stack I2972-I2976 and I3040 is unpushed or unmerged; I4005 must build on it, and waits for it to land if it has not.

milestones.title: Landed work is released as a measured version, and how long it has waited is a finding
milestones.problem: The owner's order of 2026-10-19 is a new measured version of majordomus.dev after every session and every milestone, as often as possible, enforced. The cooperation model already says the release seat releases whenever master holds landed work past the last tag (project.the-cooperation-model-is-the-owners-word, rule 4), and the version is measured from the public contract (ADR 0051). Nothing measures that rule, though. Master can hold a day of landed work past the last release while every check, the brief, doctor and the delivery screen stay green. publication-currency asks whether the site serves the trunk, not whether the trunk was released.
milestones.outcome: One capability, release.currency, answers how much landed work the trunk holds past the last release, since when, and which version the contract requires for it. The brief, doctor and /ui/delivery read it. A task holding the release seat cannot finish completed once that work has waited past its threshold. project.land-and-publish names the capability's case as its proof.
non_scope: Cutting releases: that stays the release seat's act, through the pipeline it already runs
Committing the answer into site data: it reads refs, and committed derived data must not
acceptance_criteria: release.currency answers the last release, the landed commits past it with the oldest one's age, and the version the contract requires, on the command line, HTTP and MCP
The brief and doctor warn once landed work is past the last release and warn harder past the threshold; /ui/delivery shows the same answer
finish refuses completed to a task holding the release seat while landed work has waited past the threshold, and counts a pushed tag whose release run is in progress as released

milestones.title: An adopting repository survives a Majordomus upgrade, and what the tool vendors into it is adopter-neutral
milestones.problem: A downstream repository, OSCILLA, audited on 2026-10-04 against v0.13.0 (e08aec8651), shows the tool breaking its adopters in ways no test in this repository sees, because every test here runs this repository's own layout. Installing 0.12.0 machine-wide made doctor report 433 failures in OSCILLA: unsealed plan stamps and use-case steps reclassified as state-mutating. Its pre-commit hook runs doctor, so every commit was refused until the layer was migrated by hand, and the migrated layer is then rejected by 0.10. Nothing records which tool version a layer was written for, and migrate handles only .majordomus to .ai. Live use-case scenarios refuse read-only knowledge subcommands while admitting check --checkpoint, which writes. Upgrading the vendored rules leaves the policy and source keys they depend on behind. The knowledge deriver writes untracked candidates onto a trunk that only pull requests change. The vendored rules and the init skeleton carry this repository's narrative, test paths and stack.
milestones.outcome: An adopter can upgrade the tool, or vendor its rules, and be told exactly what to migrate before anything refuses its commits. The migration is a command, not a hand replay. What the tool writes into an adopter (rules, skeleton, scope, candidates) is neutral to this repository and keeps a PR-only trunk clean.
milestones.current_state: At e08aec8651 the manifest and policy name no tool or layer version. SEALED_FROM is one global constant (lib/project.awk:45, plan.rs:122). share/commands.yaml classes each top-level command once. lib/migrate.sh moves only .majordomus/. docs/INSTALL.md says only to re-run the installer to upgrade. The knowledge deriver writes .ai/repo/knowledge/candidates/ in whichever checkout closes an episode. The rule package manifest says source_revision 0.6.0.
milestones.desired_state: doctor separates version-skew findings from defects and names the migration that clears them. migrate carries a layer from one version to the next, including re-sealing old plan stamps with their original times. The effect class is judged per subcommand and flag. rules vendor update reports or applies the skeleton keys the new rules need. Candidates never dirty a trunk. Vendored rules and the init skeleton say nothing that is only true of this repository.
non_scope: OSCILLA itself: it is the evidence, read only
Fixes already in flight: #780-#784, fix/context-resolves-a-path-not-yet-created, #746 and 9030dc4795
Accepting any ADR these issues propose; acceptance is the owner's act

milestones.title: A desired outcome becomes a draft plan that is checked before a record is written
milestones.problem: Every intent, gap, milestone and issue in .ai/repo/project is written by hand, record by record, and is judged only after it is in the tree: intent validate, intent coverage and plan validate read the committed records. A worker who starts from a desired outcome has no brief of what the repository already holds about it, no way to check a whole draft plan before writing it, and no writer that materialises a checked draft. docs/PLANNING.md:220 says 'Nothing here derives a plan from an intent automatically'; intent-lifecycle and intent-planning put derivation out of scope, and ADR 0112 (branch, :98-101) keeps 'Majordomus still authors no semantic finding and derives no plan'. Both owner packs of 2026-10-07 ask for the layer above the record (closure 70_OUTCOME_TO_PLAN_DERIVATION.md, tight-integration 80_DESIRED_OUTCOME_TO_PLAN.md).
milestones.outcome: A desired outcome enters as a typed draft: one document holding a draft intent, its gap, its milestones and the issues with what each serves and depends on. intent draft brief derives what the repository already holds about the outcome; intent draft check judges a draft with the same derivations that judge the tree, as if it were written, and writes nothing; intent draft apply writes a checked draft as records with identities allocated above the high-water mark, and refuses an unchecked one. An advisor may write the draft from the brief; without one a person or a worker writes it, and the check is the same.
milestones.current_state: No draft kind, no brief and no writer exist. IntentCommand offers list, show, validate, coverage, preflight, binding (apps/majordomus-cli/src/cli.rs:161-198). Intents::derive (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:1323) and the plan loader read records from the index only. Identity allocation above a high-water mark is decided in ADR 0053.
milestones.desired_state: A draft schema in share/schemas/majordomus; three verbs of intent draft backed by capabilities, two read-only and one declared writer; the check reuses Intents::derive, the coverage, plan validation and, once landed, the structural opposition over an overlay of the index; an ADR that supersedes the 'derives no plan' clauses for drafting only.
non_scope: Executing a draft; a written draft is planned work held to the binding and the opposition like any other
A Cockpit wizard; the Cockpit may show a draft check's answer and owns no planning logic
Requiring an advisor; drafting by hand enters the same check
Rewriting records a draft does not name
acceptance_criteria: intent draft check refuses a draft whose criterion no issue serves, whose issue serves nothing, whose dependencies cycle or whose link does not resolve, naming each finding, and writes nothing
intent draft apply writes exactly the records of a checked draft with identities above the high-water mark, and refuses a draft that does not check
intent draft brief lists the intents, milestones, issues, ADRs and rules the outcome touches, each with the source it was read from
An advisor-written draft that does not parse is refused with the reason, and a refused draft's findings are handed back at most the policy's bound of rounds
The command line, HTTP and MCP answer the same check and the same brief
risks: Lane B of the 2026-10-09 audit plans the same outcome from the intent-outcome and IDD-completion packs; one of the two milestones must be dropped before numbering.
A check that re-implements validation for drafts becomes a second validator; the overlay must feed the existing derivations, not copy them (rule project.derived-once).

A new writing capability widens the set pinned by apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mod.rs::the_capabilities_that_write_the_repository_are_these; the widening is deliberate and named in the ADR.

milestones.title: An unmet criterion is drafted into work from the evidence, and the draft is the same on every run
milestones.problem: Majordomus judges the gap and the plan of an intent and writes neither. A worker reads the ledger by hand to say which criterion is satisfied, missing or unknown, copies that into .ai/repo/project/gaps/<intent>.yaml, and then writes one issue per uncovered criterion, also by hand. Every input of that work is already derived: the state of each criterion's evidence (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:1059-1150), the coverage finding criterion_uncovered (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent_plan.rs:522) and the realization finding criterion_closed_unmet (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent_realization.rs:746), the serving scope of a criterion (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:1156-1173) and the gap's own suggested work (share/schemas/majordomus/gap/gap.v1.schema.json, work[].serves and work[].issue). Nothing turns them into a draft, so two workers drafting the same intent produce two different plans, and a rerun cannot be told from new work. The next ready issue is chosen by wave, priority and id alone (apps/majordomus-cli/src/plan.rs:531-543) and never asks whether the issue serves an unmet criterion or would be refused by its binding. An intent that work keeps finishing under while no criterion moves is reported by nothing.
milestones.outcome: `majordomus-cli intent draft gap <intent>` prints a gap record whose conditions are derived from the evidence at the presented commit, with every observation citing the ledger execution or claim it read; `majordomus-cli intent draft plan <intent>` prints one issue draft per criterion no live issue serves, with an identity derived from the intent and the criterion, so a rerun on unchanged inputs prints the same bytes and a criterion already served prints nothing; `majordomus-cli intent next` names the next READY issue that serves an unmet criterion and whose binding would be accepted, with why each issue ranked above it was passed over; and an intent under which tasks keep finishing while no criterion changes state is named stalled. Every draft is a read: nothing is written, and a draft becomes a record only through the worker's own commit.
milestones.current_state: Implemented: per-criterion evidence state (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:143-190), coverage and purpose findings (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/intent_plan.rs::a_criterion_no_work_serves_is_refused_once_the_intent_has_work, ::work_under_an_intent_answers_why_it_exists_or_is_refused), gap and critique validation (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent_review.rs:1-23), the binding's refusal causes (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent_binding.rs:121-140). Absent: any draft of a gap or of work, an intent-aware next, a stall signal. Decided against so far: the intent intent-planning declares the non-goal 'Generating issues or a critique from an intent automatically' (.ai/repo/project/intents/intent-planning.yaml) and the milestones intent-opposition and intent-reassessment declare 'Deriving a plan from an outcome' and 'Drafting work from an outcome' as non-scope (branches feature/opposition-is-executed, origin/rescue/d1/feature/what-remains-of-an-intent-is-derived).
milestones.desired_state: An ADR records that Majordomus drafts the deterministic half of a gap and a plan from derived facts, never writes them, and never drafts a criterion or an intent; the intent intent-planning's non-goal is narrowed to say so. Two read-only capabilities, intents.draft_gap and intents.draft_plan, and one read-only capability, intents.next, are declared once under apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/ and reach the command line, HTTP and MCP by generation. The realization view carries a stalled flag per intent with the tasks that finished since the last change of a criterion's state.
non_scope: Drafting an intent, a criterion or an invariant from an outcome statement; that is the outcome-to-plan pipeline of the intent-tight-integration pack (prompt 80), which lane A audits
Writing a gap, an issue or a critique; every draft is printed and the worker commits it

milestones.title: One capability graph, two projections, and no second inventory of what this repository can do
milestones.problem: The executable already declares a capability once and projects it into MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger, the command line and now the Cockpit (ADR 2, ADR 4, ADR 12). Everything the repository knows that is not a capability is outside that model: the skills, the rules, the decisions, the documents, the use cases, the examples, the benchmarks and the deployment are each authoritative in their own directory and related to the capabilities only in the reader's head. The Cockpit, the landing page, the navigation, the site indexes and the search each therefore assemble their own view of what exists, and every new subsystem costs an edit in each of them. The failure this produces is not visual: a capability with no documentation, no test and no enforcement looks exactly like one that has all three, because nothing resolves the relation.
milestones.outcome: One typed, deterministic capability graph composes the registries that already own their facts — it does not replace them — and adds typed relations between them that are inferred where a stable convention exists and declared where it does not. Both the running server and the published site render from that one graph: the static projection is the snapshot, the runtime projection is the snapshot plus live state. Navigation, overview, detail, search, the relation view and the coverage matrix are all derived, a dangling relation fails generation rather than rendering as a missing section, and a capability that exists with no documentation, no test or no enforcement is visible as such rather than indistinguishable from one that has them.
milestones.current_state: The Cockpit is a projection of the registry and the index with its own graph derivation (ADR 12, feature/ai-artifacts). Web surfaces are being made discoverable from their producers (ADR 13, in flight). Skills, rules, decisions, use cases, documents, benchmarks and — after the deployment milestone — deployments are each indexed as kinds, and none of them is related to a capability by anything a machine reads.
milestones.desired_state: A contributor registers a capability in the subsystem that owns it, runs generation, and the Cockpit, the navigation, the search, the graph, the documentation index, the coverage matrix, the static snapshot and the runtime metadata all change. Nothing else has to be edited, and CI refuses a change that leaves any of them stale.
non_scope: A hand-maintained menu, page list or capability inventory in any format, including a YAML one
Replacing any registry that is already authoritative for what it owns
A client-side application framework; the Cockpit stays server-rendered with progressive enhancement
A layout description language with coordinates, columns or component trees as data
An external search service for a graph this size
Mutating controls in the Cockpit beyond what the existing authorisation architecture already makes safe
acceptance_criteria: The graph composes the existing authoritative registries and introduces no second store of what they own
Every node has a stable identity that survives a title change, identities are unique, and generation is deterministic over identical inputs
Relations are typed, inferred only from stable conventions, and a relation that does not resolve fails generation with a message naming both ends
The static and the runtime projections come from the same graph, and their representations are equal once runtime-only fields are removed
A surface that requires a running backend is not offered as usable in the static projection, and that decision comes from availability metadata rather than from any check on the page's location
Navigation, overview, detail, search and the coverage matrix are all derived, and adding a capability requires no edit to any of them
The coverage matrix reports documentation, tests, enforcement and benchmarks only where an artifact or a resolved relation supports the claim
The Cockpit is usable on a narrow phone viewport and its core information is present before JavaScript runs
Each enforcement rule introduced here has a check that CI executes, proved by a negative test
risks: Composing eight registries into one model invites a ninth store that holds the composition. The aggregate is derived on every build and committed only as a generated artifact; anything hand-edited in it is a defect.
Inference from names is fragile the day two subsystems name something the same way. Inference is allowed only over stable identities, and ambiguity is an explicit declaration rather than a heuristic.
A coverage matrix that reports what metadata claims rather than what exists is worse than no matrix, because it looks like evidence. Every green cell must resolve to an artifact.
The Cockpit and the web surfaces are being built on other branches right now. This milestone extends them and must land after them rather than beside them.
A graph view is the part everyone wants to build first and the part that matters least if the model underneath is wrong. The model comes first, and the visualisation reads it.

milestones.title: The critical path from a change to its verdict, and from a merge to its verified deploy, runs under a minute warm
milestones.problem: A pull request's required verdict takes hours, not seconds: the behavioural suite runs on four shards of 51-86 minutes each, every documentation or layer change runs all four, and one case alone has cost up to 3468 s on a loaded runner. The suite budget has been raised three times in a week to follow runner load, and on 2026-10-09 the slowest case went 18 s over its 3450 s budget and failed the verdict of a pull request it does not touch (#831, run 37926379104). The owner's mission of 2026-10-08 asks for the change-to-verdict and merge-to-verified-deploy paths under 60 s warm, measured on GitHub, with no enforcement weakened.
milestones.outcome: The change-to-verdict path runs p50 under 40 s and p95 under 60 s warm, and merge-to-verified-deploy p50 under 45 s and p95 under 60 s, measured on GitHub with warm, partial and cold reported apart, every skip of a gate explained by the repository's own impact model, and no required test removed, skipped or made advisory to reach the number.
milestones.current_state: Baseline of change-to-verdict measured on GitHub on 2026-10-22, attempt-1 runs, all jobs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest: a full plan is 31 jobs and 740-860 runner-minutes; green runs took 81 min wall alone on the pool (39634495999), 108 min (39762797718) and 122 min (39712017896); master 2034d4a3f0b took 153 min with 774 summed job-minutes of queueing behind overlapping runs (39784979979). The critical path of 39762797718 was plan 0.4 min, suite-shard (1) 98 min (87 of them cases), suite 0.3, evidence 9. Its four shards ran 87, 52, 82 and 43 min because the deal read a record of 410 of 602 cases (2026-10-10) and weighed every unrecorded case 300 s against a median of 9 (I3930). Beside it: ui 94 min, serial (I3931, I3940); rust lane 3 60-84 min, of which plan-record-cases 1602 s and release-record-cases 425 s re-run cases the suite runs (I3937); the executable built about 4.5 min in eight jobs (I3939); case 486_rustdoc_composition 4017 s, the floor of every shard (I3938). Of the last 120 validate runs 23 passed, 43 failed and 49 were cancelled, most by the branch self-cancel on a first red; the pages job failed on 8 master runs from 2026-10-17 to 10-22 because its 1200 s wait expired while pages.yml queued behind validate (I3936). Merge-to-verified-deploy is not yet measured. .ai/repo/ci/suite.yaml budgets the suite at 61700 case-seconds and the slowest case at 5130 s.
milestones.desired_state: A measured baseline of both paths is committed before any redesign; each change that shortens them names the measurement it moves; and the budget of a case is never raised to follow runner load again.
non_scope: Removing, skipping or making advisory any required test to reach the number
Redesigning anything before the baseline of both paths is measured on GitHub and committed
Local timings as the measure; the number is GitHub's
acceptance_criteria: The baseline of change-to-verdict and merge-to-verified-deploy, warm, partial and cold, is committed with the runs it was measured from
Both paths meet the outcome's percentiles over the runs named, and every gate a change skips names the impact rule that skipped it
No required test was removed, skipped or made advisory, shown by the gate model's required set before and after

milestones.title: A command or deployment criterion is met by a recorded run of exactly that command, or an observation of exactly that deployment, current at the presented revision
milestones.problem: An intent criterion may name four kinds of evidence and only two are judged. A deployment criterion reads not_derivable as soon as the deployment object exists (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:1125-1133) and a command criterion reads not_derivable for any reference (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:1135-1139), so neither is ever met and an intent that names one can never reach satisfied. This repository's own intent intent-lifecycle names the command criterion model-is-gated (.ai/repo/project/intents/intent-lifecycle.yaml), so its stage cannot become satisfied whatever happens (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:1424-1433 counts it among all_met). The claim intent-command-deployment-evidence has stood planned with no responsibility (docs/CLAIMS.yaml:961-968), and the intent-satisfaction milestone declares command and deployment evidence non-scope (branch feature/satisfaction-is-explained). The parts exist: `majordomus served observe` fetches a deployment's build identity, judges it against a commit by containment and records the observation (apps/majordomus-cli/src/served.rs:15-35, 646-675, test/cases/384_a_deployment_is_evidence.sh), and every ledger execution already carries the command that produced it (apps/majordomus-cli/src/evidence/mod.rs:612). Nothing joins either to a criterion. And a ledger line is admitted on its shape alone (apps/majordomus-cli/src/evidence/ledger.rs:200-218): nothing says whether a run produced it.
milestones.outcome: A deployment criterion is met when a recorded observation of that deployment served a build containing the newest commit that changed the criterion's serving scope, and reads stale, failing or not_run otherwise, never met on an unreachable, malformed, dirty or undecided answer. A command criterion is met when a recorded execution of exactly the argument vector the criterion names exited 0 at a revision the evidence module's one freshness function judges current, with the scope it serves as its inputs; a different command exiting 0 meets nothing. Both carry the same evaluation a test criterion carries. The negative cases are executable, the claim is guaranteed with its test, and intent-lifecycle can be satisfied.
milestones.current_state: Implemented: deployment observation and containment judgement (apps/majordomus-cli/src/served.rs:367, 646), observation records under .ai/local/state/served/observations.jsonl (apps/majordomus-cli/src/served.rs:52), one freshness function for test and claim evidence (apps/majordomus-cli/src/evidence/freshness.rs:667-700), the verdict word unknown when only underivable criteria are unmet (apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs:327-354). Absent: a judgement of either kind for an intent criterion, a recording path for a declared command, a check that a ledger execution came from a recorded run.
milestones.desired_state: criterion_of judges deployment and command criteria through the evidence module, not beside it; `majordomus evidence record --command '<argv>'` runs one declared command with a fixed argument vector and a bounded time, redacts its output through the one redaction rule set (apps/majordomus-cli/src/redaction.rs), and records an execution whose test identity is derived from the argument vector; the negative matrix is a case; the claim intent-command-deployment-evidence is guaranteed and docs/PLANNING.md says what meets each kind.
non_scope: Deploying anything; a criterion reads what was observed and records nothing on its own
Running a command from an intent read; a read never executes a criterion's command
Probing a deployment from inside intent show; observation stays `majordomus served observe`
Authenticating ledger lines cryptographically; the decision on forged lines is recorded and its limitation stated if not implemented
The finish contract, which is finish-reads-what-its-work-serves
acceptance_criteria: A deployment criterion is current only when a recorded observation of that deployment served a build containing the newest commit of its serving scope, and reads not met for an unreachable, malformed, dirty or undecided observation and for none at all

A command criterion is current only for a recorded passing execution of the identical argument vector at a revision the freshness function judges current; an execution of a different command, a failing one, and one older than a change to its serving scope do not meet it
The verdict of an intent whose only unmet criteria are command or deployment criteria with no observation or run reads unsatisfied, not unknown, once the kind is judged
intent-lifecycle's criterion model-is-gated is met in this repository by a recorded run of `majordomus intent validate`
Command output recorded as evidence passes through the one redaction rule set and the recorded environment carries variable names, never values
The claim intent-command-deployment-evidence is guaranteed and names its test
validation: bash test/run.sh <the negative-matrix case this milestone adds>
risks: Served observations are checkout-local (apps/majordomus-cli/src/served.rs:18-21), so a clone or a CI runner that never observed reads not_run; that is the honest answer and the documents must say so rather than commit observations into the tree they describe.

Moving a verdict from unknown to unsatisfied changes what every consumer of IntentVerdictState sees for intents with command or deployment criteria; the binding, the realization and the Cockpit read it, so the change lands with their tests.
Running a declared command is execution; the argument vector is fixed, no shell is spawned, the time is bounded, and the command is the criterion's own text, never a value from a request.
intent-satisfaction (PR 813) changes IntentCriterion; this milestone adds beside its fields and merges after it.

milestones.title: Cost per accepted outcome, only on measured data
milestones.problem: Cost per token is not a useful unit of work. The unit that matters is what an accepted outcome cost, and that cannot be computed without both telemetry and an acceptance record.
milestones.outcome: The cost of an accepted outcome is computed from measured telemetry and the finish contract that accepted it, and is reported only where both exist.
milestones.current_state: Not started, and not startable: it needs execution telemetry underneath it.
milestones.desired_state: A completed, accepted task can state what it cost, from measurement rather than estimate.
non_scope: Any figure derived from elapsed time or token count as a proxy for progress
acceptance_criteria: Cost is reported only for outcomes that were accepted by the finish contract
An outcome without telemetry reports no cost rather than a modelled one
The denominator is a real acceptance, never a count of sessions
risks: Accepted outcomes are rare enough early on that the number is noisy; it must say so.

milestones.title: The way from a pull request to a verified publication is measured per phase, and its bounds are read where work starts
milestones.problem: Between 2026-09-10 and 2026-10-18 the owner asked more than a dozen times for faster turnaround and an empty backlog, and every audit reconstructed queue waits and lead times by hand from run timestamps. The repository measures CI run durations and merges per day, but not the wait before a run starts, not what happens after a merge, and its backlog bound is an environment default of one script. Proposed in ADR 0196 (Delivery latency targets are budgets of benchmark policy, measured per phase, and never a correctness gate on runners the repository does not own); ADR 0197 (The backlog is bounded by a declared bound that every session reads at start, and the bound reports rather than refuses); ADR 0198 (Delivery is judged by verified outcomes landed per day, with lead time p95 as its control, never by commits, pull requests or sessions) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c199#14, chatgpt-majordomus:c255#7, chatgpt-majordomus:c204#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c216#6, chatgpt-majordomus:c238#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c280#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c287#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c295#7, chatgpt-majordomus:c112#3, chatgpt-majordomus:c207#6, chatgpt-majordomus:c209#3.
milestones.outcome: Queue time, run time and lead time per phase are derived readings; the backlog bound is policy and the brief says when it is passed; finish names the pull request it hands on; budgets exist per phase without turning runner wall time into a correctness gate.
milestones.current_state: Verified on master 707a04c7ce8: integration.timings measures started-to-completed only (timings.rs); I2474 draws merges per day; scripts/ci/backlog-check reads MJ_BACKLOG_MAX (default 10); brief.rs reports prs brief without a bound; lib/finish.sh names no pull request. I2946 (board on 2026-10-18, p7, not on master) measures throughput from prs and ci-timings.
milestones.desired_state: One measured flow from opened to served-verified, read by the drain screen, the brief, CLI, HTTP and MCP from the same capabilities, with unmeasured phases said as unmeasured.

milestones.title: A committed derivation describes something it can be a projection of
milestones.problem: A derived artifact is committed with a fingerprint of what produced it, and the gates compare that fingerprint with the tree. Two things make the recording unable to stay true. It hashes the whole input set, so an unrelated change landing on the trunk invalidates a derivation that is not wrong - the tree simply moved; and where it hashes HEAD, a file inside a commit cannot describe the commit it is in, which apps/majordomus-cli/src/release/changelog.rs:75 states in its own comment while the gate reaches past it. The costs are paid daily and separately: every branch re-derives after every merge, six to thirty-five minutes each time; a fixture without history cannot evaluate the artifact at all; and the refusal that catches a stale recording lives in a pre-commit hook, which cannot run for a merge the server creates. So the first thing in the pipeline that can say no is the publication.
milestones.outcome: A committed derived artifact is a projection of inputs the commit owns. Landing an unrelated change on the trunk does not invalidate it, a fixture whose object database has no history can still evaluate it, and the staleness refusal exists on the path merges actually take - so the first thing that says no is a check rather than the published site.
milestones.current_state: Measured on 2026-09-10. master 3fb515f5c records source_hash e6abaa4665163bcd while its tree hashes to 4fe657a09b10, and three consecutive master Pages runs failed identically at the build step on that refusal; the site last answered from 5e67318db. Two of those three merges were committed by GitHub, where no pre-commit hook exists, and gh api branches/master/protection returns 404 Branch not protected, so the site gate that does check currency is advisory and reports after the merge. c44c2d4c8 and 2ce8d66e5 record the same source_hash as each other - the merge driver resolves derived artifacts to ours, so a stale recording rides through a merge untouched. test/cases/56_derived_current_gate.sh exports git archive HEAD into a fixture with no commits, so the changelog composition reports fatal: Not a valid commit name. One branch paid 185s, 1125s and 2135s of re-derivation in one evening, entirely because the trunk moved underneath it.
milestones.desired_state: The recording covers what the commit owns. The gate that refuses a stale one runs where merges happen. The changelog composes from something a fixture can evaluate. Nobody re-derives to answer a question the derivation was already right about.
non_scope: Making the Pages build re-derive instead of refusing. The input fingerprint is deterministic - three runs on one tree are byte-identical - but the generated content is machine-dependent: %h abbreviates against the local object store, a depth-1 checkout writes a degraded changelog, a concurrent derive can read a sibling worktree root. A build that re-derived could produce a third answer matching neither side. Recorded here because this exit will be proposed again, and because an objection stated as non-determinism of the fingerprint is refutable in one command and would take the correct objection down with it.
Turning on branch protection, or choosing which check is required. A repository setting, and the operator's decision.
Weakening the derived merge driver. Resolving to ours is correct; what is missing is the refusal downstream of it on the server-side path.
acceptance_criteria: A derived artifact committed at one commit is still current at that commit after an unrelated change lands on the trunk
A fixture whose object database does not contain the commit under test can evaluate every derived artifact
The staleness refusal runs on the path a server-side merge takes, or the record names the decision taken instead
No document claims a guard that a merge created by GitHub cannot reach
risks: Narrowing what the recording covers is silent in the dangerous direction: too narrow and staleness stops being detectable, which reads as green rather than as noise. Every change here needs a case that proves the gate still refuses something.
The subsystem is touched by every branch, so a change lands into constant contention with whatever else is deriving.

milestones.title: The runtime has a development surface
milestones.problem: The Cockpit is a faithful projection of a registry that has almost nothing development-shaped in it. Re-measured on today's master, the registry declares exactly three capabilities of kind `command` — executions.start, executions.cancel, peers.announce — and the OpenAPI document the server serves has exactly those three non-GET operations to match. Every command of the development lifecycle lives in a second program, bin/majordomus, and every one of its nodes in the command graph is withheld from every machine surface. So no development surface can be built by adding pages: there is nothing behind the pages to call, and `majordomus_plan_done` answers `unknown tool` because there is no capability for a plan transition. docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md is the evidence; ADR 0040 is the decision it argues for. Until this milestone existed, none of it was in the plan at all: a keyword search of the issues and milestones for palette, diff view, CI status and syntax highlighting returned nothing, so the work could not be scheduled, blocked or reported.
milestones.outcome: A development transition is decided in exactly one place — a `capability!` of kind `command` in the Rust registry — and every surface that offers it is a projection: the CLI, the MCP tool, the HTTP route, the OpenAPI operation and the Cockpit's generated runner form, none of them written by hand. The lifecycle stops being a second program with no surfaces, and the execution history a development surface would show exists somewhere durable.
milestones.current_state: Three command capabilities, all of them about executions or peers. The lifecycle transitions exist only in lib/plan.sh and lib/start.sh. `majordomus run` executes in its own process and never reaches the running server, so the execution plane the Cockpit shows and the one a person uses are disjoint. A server whose executable has been replaced still reports itself `ready`. Two capabilities — devtask.issue and devtask.milestone — landed after the audit's base and give the runtime its first canonical read of an issue and a milestone as work; neither of them writes anything.
milestones.desired_state: Phase A of the audit's plan has landed end to end — one transition, one capability, four surfaces, no hand-written projection — and the phases that depend on it are schedulable against it. The three load-bearing defects named in the audit's F-table are fixed or explicitly deferred with a record, rather than carried silently under every later measurement.
non_scope: A terminal, a PTY or shell execution on any surface. The audit records this as a non-goal and share/cockpit/palette.js already states the boundary in terms.
Editing repository source in the browser. The Cockpit refuses every non-GET route by decision, and this milestone does not reopen that decision.
Retries and a scheduler. apps/majordomus-cli/src/execution/mod.rs states in its own module documentation that it has none, by decision.
A second datastore or a second project model. The records stay canonical and the runtime reads them.
The `/cockpit/worktrees` response time. It is F3 in the audit's table and is being fixed on fix/cockpit-answers-quickly; this milestone references that work rather than duplicating it.
A wholesale port of lib/*.sh. Phase A is one transition; the rest is scheduled behind it or not at all.
acceptance_criteria: The registry declares at least one capability of kind command that changes a development record, and the generated OpenAPI carries its non-GET operation without anyone editing the document
The same transition is reachable from the CLI, from MCP and over HTTP, and the Cockpit's existing generic runner drives it with no Cockpit source edited
An execution a person starts is visible to the server that serves the repository, or the record says which decision was taken instead and why
A surface that reports a runtime as ready cannot be serving an executable that no longer exists on disk
No claim in docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md is left standing that a command in this repository contradicts
risks: Phase A is the whole architecture in miniature. If the pattern does not land cleanly on one transition, no later phase would have worked either, and the correct response is to stop rather than to widen.

A second name for an existing concept can land in parallel. One already has: the devtask module documents itself as a join over plan and trace rather than a second model, and holds an equality assertion against plan.issues. It is additive and should stay, but its readiness vocabulary refines the canonical statuses, and Phase A should converge the naming rather than grow a third.
Master moves during the work. It moved eleven times during the audit that produced this milestone, and again between that audit and this record.
