milestones.title: An episode records the governance and briefing it was handed, and a change is told
milestones.problem: The entry preflight reports governance per claim (ADR 0066, docs/PREFLIGHT.md) but there is no digest of the effective governance, docs/PREFLIGHT.md states 'No compiled context revision exists in a checkout yet, so none is shown', session.started records neither, and a rule edited mid-session is noticed by nobody. intent_binding pins the plan revision of a task's intents (plan_revision) but not governance. Proposed in ADR 0181 (An episode records the governance and the briefing it was handed, each by one digest) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c097#2.
milestones.outcome: One governance digest computed by one function, recorded per episode with the briefing digest, compared at the next interaction, carried by handovers, identical across every entry surface; every route around the preflight is a case or a stated limit; task start states how far its base is behind the remote's master.
milestones.current_state: Verified on master 707a04c: environment/cache.rs fingerprints tiers for caching only; environment/preflight.rs derives the verdicts; cases 118, 190-192 prove entry converges on one server; SECURITY.md lists three bypass limits; lib/start.sh does not report base divergence; environment/vcs.rs reads ahead/behind against the branch's own upstream without fetching; worktree create already starts a new branch from the remote's trunk (case 3131_a_new_worktree_starts_from_the_remote_trunk).
milestones.desired_state: governance digest on the preflight, the brief, session.started and handovers; a parity case across clients; a bypass inventory held to SECURITY.md.
non_scope: Any network call at entry
Filesystem watchers

milestones.title: Everything that happens in the repository is followed in one stream
milestones.problem: A worker that wants to know what is happening around it reads six surfaces with six cursors: the mesh journal (where about 95% of events are identical session re-projections on every heartbeat), the board, the executor trail, the executions, and GitHub's pull requests and checks through gh. Nothing joins them, nothing says which of it is addressed to the reader, and every session that needs it hand-rolls a jq loop over majordomus mesh events and gh pr list. Sessions miss reviews and handovers addressed to them for hours because nothing they read shows them.
milestones.outcome: majordomus monitor is the one stream: a typed, cursor-paged feed of signals from every source, with the heartbeat noise folded away and what is addressed to the reader marked and listed first, served by the running server over HTTP, MCP and the command line (with --follow), shown live in the Cockpit, printed at every session start, named by the provider bootstrap, documented and released.
milestones.current_state: No monitor command, module or capability exists (origin/master 890e112d04, 0.20.0). mesh.events, peers, integration.events and executions.events each answer their own page; the CLI renders mesh events one by one, unfiltered.

non_scope: Writing anything: the monitor reads; acting on a signal stays with the capability that owns the act
A second journal or event store: every signal is derived from a source that already records it
Push notifications to systems outside the repository (Slack, mail); a notifier subscribes to the stream later
acceptance_criteria: One capability answers a page of signals from mesh, board, executor trail and executions after an opaque cursor, and the next page after the answer's cursor repeats nothing

Signals addressed to the reader are marked for_you and listed first in a briefing
majordomus monitor --follow streams new signals and --count/--until let a script wait for one and exit
An unreachable source is reported with its reason, never answered as empty
The Cockpit shows the stream live, and the start briefing and majordomus context print what happened since the last look
The provider bootstrap names the command; docs/MONITOR.md, the README and a blog article describe it; the release carries it

milestones.title: An external workspace is read the way this repository reads anything else, and its content never becomes public by accident
milestones.problem: The operator holds work in vendor-hosted workspaces — a ChatGPT Project first, others after — and has no machine access to it. Whatever is decided there is invisible to every instrument this repository has: it cannot be searched, cited, carried into a handover, or linked to the decision it produced. The obvious repair is the wrong one twice over. Scraping a page produces a corpus with no identity, no provenance and no way to tell a change from a re-render; and building the corpus into the layer the way tracked content is built would publish, on a public website, a body of private conversation the vendor holds under an authenticated session. ADR 0025 settles the shape: the catalogue of workspaces is the repository's own statement and is tracked; the content is this checkout's state and is not.
milestones.outcome: A workspace is a declared object of the layer — vendor, identity, what the operator authorised, which browser profile reaches it, which capabilities it is expected to have — and rides the existing kind pipeline onto every surface with no code that special-cases it. Its content is synced by the Node tooling layer that already drives the system browser, lands under `.ai/local/workspaces/`, carries provenance and a support level on every record, and is read back through exactly one capability shaped like `continuity`: served, never published. A sync is incremental from a durable checkpoint, idempotent on replay, fails closed when an observed contract breaks, and never writes a credential anywhere.
milestones.current_state: Nothing exists. There is no workspace kind, no adapter, no store, no capability and no gate. The repository does drive a browser — Playwright over the system Chrome, in `scripts/lib/ui-audit.mjs` and `scripts/lib/cockpit-probe.mjs`, wired into CI and skipping cleanly where Chrome is absent — and it has no convention at all for holding a credential, only a negative one that fails the site build when a secret-shaped string reaches rendered output.
milestones.desired_state: `majordomus workspaces` lists what is declared and what is synced, with the age and the support level of each. A sync is one command in the tooling layer, resumable, bounded, and provable from sanitised fixtures in CI without touching a live account. Adding a second vendor means writing an adapter and a declaration, not editing every consumer. Nothing under `.ai/local/workspaces/` reaches the website, the generated documentation, or any published projection, and a gate proves it rather than a sentence promising it.
non_scope: Any write to the vendor — no message is sent, no file is uploaded, no conversation is renamed
Any dependency added to majordomus-cli; the boundary of ADR 0025 is the point
Any credential, cookie, token or authorisation header stored anywhere in the tree or the state directory
Any bypass of authentication, multi-factor prompts, rate limits or anti-abuse controls
Publishing synced content to the website or any public projection
A second vendor adapter before the first one is proven
acceptance_criteria: A workspace declaration is a tracked object of a declared kind, closed by an allow file, described by a schema, and reaches the object surface with no code that special-cases it

Every synced record carries its upstream identity, a local identity that does not depend on a title, a content hash, the transport that produced it and a support level, all as typed fields rather than prose
The store under .ai/local/workspaces/ has a declared layout, a checkpoint, a retention cap in policy and a doctor stanza that measures it
A sync resumes from its checkpoint, produces the same store when replayed, and marks a record removed upstream rather than deleting it silently
An observed contract that breaks fails closed and falls back to the browser transport; no partial parse is ever persisted
CI proves the mapper and the sync from sanitised fixtures, with no live account and no network
No credential reaches the repository, the state directory, a fixture, a log or a snapshot, and a gate greps for it
A gate fails if majordomus-cli gains a dependency, and a gate fails if any published projection reaches .ai/local/workspaces/
The subsystem is documented in docs/ and every rule it states is enforced by a check CI executes
risks: The vendor's private surface is not a contract and will change without notice. Anything that treats an observed shape as canonical will break loudly and, worse, silently. The observed shape is a transport detail with a fingerprint and a compatibility state; the canonical model is this repository's.

A synced corpus is the largest body of text this repository has ever held and the only one it did not write. Every mechanism that walks files must be told about it explicitly, because none of them will notice it on their own.
The distance between reading one's own authorised workspace and automating a vendor's site is a policy, not a technicality. The declaration names what was authorised; the adapter never exceeds it.
The tooling layer is a devDependency of this checkout, not part of the released tool. A feature that only works where node_modules is installed must say so rather than appear broken.

milestones.title: Every failure the runtime can suffer is bounded, tested or stated, and changes the health it reports
milestones.problem: Readiness stays true for a degraded index and knows nothing of a lost lease or the mesh (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/health.rs:214; was_lost reaches only GET / at apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/router.rs:710); health.report has no mesh dimension (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/health.rs:299); 'degraded' has three unrelated meanings. The HTTP server reads request bodies with no deadline on four workers (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/server.rs:23,208-222), so four slow clients hold the server. Of the failure classes the pack names, the audit found tests for SIGKILL, port collision, an unwritable lease directory and a frozen owner, and none for disk full, a read-only journal directory, a slow client, a frozen worker or a kill between lease creation and its first write; lease keep-alive write errors are swallowed (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:1058-1060). The pack's premise of structured logging is refuted: logging is human tracing fmt on stderr with no JSON, correlation id or redaction (apps/majordomus-cli/src/logging.rs:29-37). The top-level doctor is a governance doctor (lib/doctor.sh:53-77). Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: A client can tell running from ready from mesh-healthy from degraded on one endpoint; no client can hold a worker past a declared deadline; each failure class in a published table names its test or its stated limitation.
milestones.current_state: Implemented: /api/v1/live, the lease's client-side bounded waits, link timeouts, clock-skew bounds, the mesh doctor's typed checks (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/doctor.rs:93-372). Partial: readiness, health, failure-class coverage. Absent: server-side request deadlines.
milestones.desired_state: The failure table in docs/DEVELOPMENT_RUNTIME.md has no row without a test or a limitation, a case refuses a row with neither, and readiness and health reflect every state the runtime already knows about itself.
non_scope: Circuit breakers; the audit found no evidence one is justified.
A metrics stack or log shipping; the runtime reports through its own capabilities.
Journal durability, which is I2137 (mesh-journal-converges).
acceptance_criteria: /api/v1/ready reports false with a named reason after a lease loss
health.report carries a mesh check when the mesh is enabled
Slow clients hold no worker past the declared deadline
Every failure class in the published table names a CI test or a stated limitation
validation: cargo test --test health_server --test http_serve --test mcp_shared --test lease_busy
MJ_TEST_JOBS=4 bash test/run.sh <the cases these issues add>
risks: Making readiness stricter can make deploy health checks fail where they passed; the fly-deployment health block reads /api/v1/live and must keep doing so.
A deadline on request reads that is too short breaks slow links; it must be declared and measured.

milestones.title: The container image is a projection of the repository model, and its smoke is its evidence
milestones.problem: Majordomus has no deployment at all: no container, no hosting provider, no way for anyone who is not standing in front of this checkout to see the layer it serves. The obvious repair is the wrong one. A Dockerfile and a fly.toml written by hand would be a second description of facts the repository already holds — the port the server binds, the routes it registers, the assets the site build produces, the binary the workspace names — and every one of those pairs would drift the first time one half changed. The repository already refuses that shape everywhere else: capabilities are declared once and projected into CLI, HTTP, MCP, OpenAPI, docs and the site, and generate --check fails when a projection is stale. A deployment must arrive the same way or not at all.
milestones.outcome: One canonical deployment object under .ai/repo/deployments/ describes the image; a typed Rust model parses and validates it; the Dockerfile, its ignore file, the GHCR image that docker-image.yml and release.yml build, its smoke derived from the route registry, the doctor checks, the documentation and the cockpit view are projections of that object and of the capability registry, each checked for drift. The published image runs as a non-root user, carries no secret and no developer path, answers live and ready in its smoke, and has measured size, cold-start and memory baselines. Re-scoped 2026-10-14 from a Fly.io deployment, which the owner disconnected on 2026-10-12.
milestones.current_state: Measured 2026-10-14 on master e28daccd9b: .ai/repo/deployments/majordomus.yaml is the canonical object; deploy/Dockerfile and its ignore file are generated from it (Alpine, uid 10001, exec-form entrypoint); docker-image.yml builds and smoke-tests the image on pull requests and on master, and release.yml publishes it to GHCR; .github/actions/image-smoke checks the image runs as non-root and answers /api/v1/live and /api/v1/ready; deploy.list, deploy.get, deploy.check and deploy.observed are capabilities. Missing: a smoke derived from the route registry, a secret and developer-path scan of the image, an SBOM, size, cold-start and memory baselines, a documentation page. The object still carries region, machines and resources, which nothing reads since Fly.io was disconnected on 2026-10-12.
milestones.desired_state: The GHCR image is a projection of the canonical object like every other artifact: generated, checked for drift, smoke-tested from the route registry, scanned for secrets and developer paths, measured against recorded budgets, documented and shown in the cockpit. Whether region, machines and resources leave the deployment/v1 schema is decided and recorded.
non_scope: Any dependency, in code, script, documentation, CI or default, on ~/dev/prismatic-platform
A provider abstraction covering hosts other than the one this repository deploys to
Kubernetes, Nomad, buildpacks, Nixpacks or a second container implementation
A persistent volume, a database or any stateful service, unless a measured requirement forces one
Mutating deployment operations exposed to unauthenticated HTTP or to the browser
Profile-guided optimisation
acceptance_criteria: One canonical deployment object is the only place the port, the region, the resources, the Machine count, the health routes, the build inputs and the budgets are stated
Every image artifact — the Dockerfile and its ignore file — is generated, marked as generated with its source and its regeneration command, and fails generate --check when edited by hand
The deployment reads are declared once in the capability registry and appear in the CLI, the HTTP API, MCP, OpenAPI and the generated documentation without a second registration
The smoke suite is derived from the route registry; no second list of endpoints exists anywhere
The production image runs as a non-root user, contains no build toolchain, no repository history, no secret and no absolute developer path
The published image answers live and ready in its smoke, run from outside the container on a free host port
Image size, binary size, build context size, cold start, resident memory and endpoint latency are measured, recorded as baselines and gated against unexplained regression
No credential is written to the repository, to a Docker layer, to a generated file, to the site or to a log, and the image is published with the workflow's own token
Every rule this milestone states is enforced by a check that CI executes
risks: Generation can hide the Dockerfile from the people who must read it. The generated file has to stay idiomatic and reviewable; the source describes intent, the output describes mechanics, and a contributor who edits the output is told which file to change instead.

The route topology and the served surfaces are being rewritten on other branches under ADR 0013. A smoke suite pinned to today's paths would be stale on arrival, so it must read the route registry rather than a path list.
256 MB is a hypothesis. It is held only as long as a measured run under that limit passes; the evidence, not the preference, decides the final number.
A deployment touches money. The first deploy must not leave two Machines running, and the Machine inventory is asserted rather than assumed.

The bootstrap credential comes from outside this repository. It may be used to obtain an authenticated session and nowhere else; anything else would make Majordomus depend on Prismatic Platform, which is forbidden.

milestones.title: A supervisory control layer that is real rather than described
milestones.problem: An AI worker in a repository has no durable memory, no declared scope, and no contract that says when its work is finished. Every session starts from nothing and ends by asserting success. The evidence that a rule is enforced is usually a sentence claiming it is.
milestones.outcome: A repository carries one policy, a small set of profiles, durable task state, and a set of commands that refuse work which does not meet a declared contract — with every rule dispatched from a registry that proves it reaches the command claiming to run it.
milestones.current_state: Delivered. The policy, the profiles, the durable records, the command surface, the doctrine registry with wiring reconciliation and the provider projections all exist and are covered by the behavioural suite.
milestones.desired_state: Unchanged: this milestone is the base every later one is measured against.
non_scope: Measuring tokens or cost
Constraining a provider's runtime
acceptance_criteria: One canonical policy projects to every provider and drift is detectable in one command
A task declares scope, and work outside it is reported
A finish contract is evaluated rather than asserted
Every enforced rule is declared in a registry, dispatched from it, and proven to reach its command
Every behaviour has a case in the suite and CI runs it
risks: The floor is bash 3.2 and BSD userland, which bounds what the engine can be asked to do.

milestones.title: A task is bound to the intent it serves
milestones.problem: The intent engine can say which intent an issue or a set of paths serves (intent preflight), and nothing asks it. `start` takes a description and a scope; the task record names no issue and no intent; the context a worker is handed says nothing of the criteria the work is for; a handover carries a commit and no trace of the intent it was written under. Work under an intent whose plan was never critiqued is found by `intent validate` after it began, not refused before.
milestones.outcome: `start` names an issue, an intent or a declared exemption, asks the binding capability what the task serves, and refuses a refused binding where the policy requires binding. The task record carries what was named and the revision it resolved at. `context` briefs the worker from the binding, `handover` pins the revision, and `handover --resolve` reports drift.
milestones.current_state: intents.preflight exists with no caller. The task record has no issue, intent or exemption field. No exemption class exists anywhere. Nothing computes a revision of an intent, its plan or its critique.
milestones.desired_state: One derivation, `Intents::binding`, answered by `intents.binding` on every surface and asked by start, context and handover.
non_scope: Refusing a finish on unmet criteria
Producing or executing a critique
Moving the task lifecycle from shell to Rust (ADR 0047)
acceptance_criteria: A task started with --issue, --intent or by scope resolves through intents.binding, and an ambiguous or refused binding does not start where the policy requires binding
An exemption is a policy-declared class with a reason, recorded in the task record and the ledger
The context of a bound task carries the intent section, from the binding
A handover carries the binding revision and --resolve reports drift
The command line, HTTP and MCP answer the same binding
risks: The records, the ADR and the tests they name land in one change: a criterion whose evidence reference does not resolve fails intent validate, so no part of this milestone reaches the trunk without the rest.

Requiring binding in this repository refuses the scope-only `start` every session uses today; the refusal must name the three ways through (an issue, an intent, an exemption) or it reads as the tool being broken.
A pin stored in a task is one step from stored intent state; it must stay a hash compared on read and never a stage or a verdict (rule project.an-intent-outlives-its-sessions).

milestones.title: Work is traceable to the intent it serves, and an intent is satisfied only by evidence
milestones.problem: This repository models the work: milestones are outcomes, issues are execution contracts, commits trace to issues and claims trace to recorded runs. Nothing above the milestone records what must become true for a person, so no command can say which outcome a change serves, whether a set of finished milestones achieved what they were for, or which intents have no work and which work has no intent. The public site stated as much: 'There is no intent object, no intent registry and no intent id.' An intent lived only in a prompt, and a prompt is unversioned, unenforced and gone when the session ends.
milestones.outcome: An intent is a typed record above the milestones that realise it: a statement, its invariants, and satisfaction criteria each naming the evidence that settles it. Its stage is derived from the plan's milestone status and its satisfaction from the evidence ledger, never stored. A gate refuses an intent that names no milestone or evidence that resolves to nothing, a session's preflight names the intent its work serves or refuses, the Cockpit shows intents with measured and enforced coverage of its scripts, and a milestone closes on GitHub only when the intents it serves are satisfied.
milestones.current_state: Milestones and issues are validated by `majordomus plan validate`; claims are joined to recorded runs by `majordomus evidence`. There is no intent kind, no intent capability and no gate that relates work to an intent.
milestones.desired_state: A worker asks which intent a change serves and one capability answers from the plan, or refuses naming the missing link. A reader asks whether an intent is satisfied and the answer is derived from recorded evidence, not from a merged pull request.
non_scope: A second task lifecycle beside the plan; the stage is derived and nothing transitions
Storing an intent status, or stamping an intent from a merge
Deriving a plan from an intent automatically
acceptance_criteria: Slice 1 — typed record and gate: the intent kind, its schema in the distribution and the skeleton, the read-only capabilities intents.list, intents.record, intents.validate and intents.preflight on every surface, and the intent-check gate refusing an invalid intent model

Slice 2 — satisfaction is decided by evidence alone (ADR 0107): completion discharges obligations and never decides whether an intent is satisfied; the intent engine is the one authority for a criterion's verdict, and a derived `verdict` answers satisfaction separately from the plan-derived stage
Slice 3 — preflight join: devcontext and the session start name the intent the task serves, from intents.preflight, and load its governance
Slice 4 — Cockpit Intent view, with the Cockpit's JavaScript coverage measured and enforced by a gate
Slice 5 — GitHub reconciliation: milestones projected with the intent they serve, and a closure gate that refuses to close a milestone whose intents are unsatisfied
risks: An intent model that grows a status or a transition becomes a second lifecycle beside the plan, and the two would disagree the first time an issue is re-planned.

Satisfaction criteria backed by commands or deployments are not derivable from the ledger yet, so an intent resting only on them can never read satisfied; its verdict reads unknown until those kinds become derivable.

milestones.title: The plan of an intent is held to it before execution
milestones.problem: An intent (ADR 0070) names its milestones and the evidence that settles each criterion, but nothing relates a criterion to the work meant to make it true. An intent can name a milestone whose issues address two of its four criteria and nothing says the other two have no work until verification finds them unmet. Planning starts from a prompt: what a worker observed was missing, and what a review of the plan overlooked, live in a terminal scroll and are gone when the session ends.

milestones.title: Landing green work survives any session, any restart and any machine
milestones.problem: On 2026-10-22 a machine restart ended the landing seat, the release seat and the loop that landed green trains; the executor that exists, majordomus prs drain, had merged nothing since 2026-10-11, its trail and lease were one clone's, and the auto-mode classifier refused every landing a session tried. Green work waited for hours until the owner fast-forwarded master by hand.
milestones.outcome: Landing green work on master never waits on a person or on one session staying alive.
milestones.current_state: Landing is a loop inside one session reading a queue file in one home directory; prs drain lands one pull request at a time with a merge commit and keeps its audit trail in .git/majordomus/integration/events.jsonl of one clone; a seat whose holder died stays vacant; standing approvals live in one machine's ~/.claude/settings.json; train order lives in ~/.cache/mj-a3.
milestones.desired_state: Every criterion of the intent is carried by an issue here and proven by its test.
acceptance_criteria: Every landing on master, a combined top included, is a fast-forward made by majordomus prs drain; none is made by hand, by --admin or by a loop that lives in one session

The executor reads its audit trail, its halt and its lease from origin, so a clone that takes over starts with the same verified count and the same halt, and a holder whose lease expired is refused before it lands
A seat whose holder stopped beating is reported vacant within one expiry and offered to live sessions by capability, and the session that accepts it resumes from the newest handover for that seat
The executor runs as a user service outside every agent session; an exit that is not a halt or a refusal is restarted, and a halt or refusal is not
A standing approval of the owner is one dated, owner-attributed record in the repository, every machine says whether its settings carry it, and only the owner, interactively, writes it
A combined top is composed by a typed command from members declared in a tracked train manifest, and two machines compose the same pre-derive tree from it

milestones.title: Every MCP transport delivers each request at most once, bounds what it carries, and honours cancellation
milestones.problem: The MCP projection is already one registry walk: tools and resources come from apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/surface.rs:367-394, annotations from the declared effect (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/protocol.rs:446-456), held by apps/majordomus-cli/tests/projections.rs:26, apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_conformance.rs and case 940. The pack's premise that MCP keeps independent lists is refuted. The transport is the defect. The stdio bridge resends the same tools/call after a 60 s timeout or any 4xx other than 404 (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:25,352; apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:283,301), so a slow writer can run twice. notifications/cancelled is dropped (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/protocol.rs:234-238) and could not be forwarded anyway because the bridge is sequential under a mutex (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:218). stdin lines and bridge responses are unbounded (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/stdio.rs:40, apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:85); the Streamable HTTP endpoint ignores MCP-Protocol-Version, issues predictable session ids (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:159) and can reap a session whose request is still running (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:138). The provider launch configurations are hand-written and diagnosed by substring (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mcp.rs:394-399). Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: A client gets each answer once or is told the outcome is unknown, can cancel what it started, cannot exhaust the server with one message, and finds its launch configuration generated from the provider declaration and diagnosed by parsing it.
milestones.current_state: Implemented and tested: stdout hygiene (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_stdio.rs), malformed traffic (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_conformance.rs::malformed_traffic_is_answered_and_the_session_survives), session isolation over HTTP (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_conformance_http.rs), protocol negotiation (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/protocol.rs:71). Absent: idempotency on resend, cancellation, symmetric bounds, the version header, generated client configs. Authorization of writers and the effect laundering through executions.start for remote callers are I2123 (runtime-trust).
milestones.desired_state: The audit's MCP rows are all I in plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md, each with a real-process test: a timed-out writer runs once, a cancelled call stops, an oversized message is refused with its real cause, a long request is not reaped, a Codex config without its table is reported unwired.
non_scope: A GET/SSE stream on the Streamable HTTP endpoint; docs/MCP.md documents its absence and no client here needs it.
Authorization and remote callers, which are I2123.
A second tool list or MCP-specific capability metadata; the registry stays the one source.
acceptance_criteria: A mutating tool call that outlasts the bridge timeout is executed exactly once
notifications/cancelled stops a running call within a bound
One declared message bound applies to stdin, request bodies and bridge responses, each with a test one byte over it
The three client launch configurations are generated and their diagnosis parses them
validation: cargo test --test mcp_shared --test mcp_conformance --test mcp_conformance_http --test shared_units --test providers_projection
risks: Claude Code once dropped every tool of this server for a month because of one schema detail; any change to the initialize answer or tool listing needs the client-acceptance test (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_conformance.rs::every_listed_tool_is_one_a_client_accepts) green.
Answering 'outcome unknown' instead of resending moves a decision to the client; the error text must say what to check.

milestones.title: Coverage and CI cost are kept, exported and drawn over time, from the one measurement each has
milestones.problem: Coverage is measured on every run and kept nowhere: scripts/rust-coverage's export is a 14-day artifact, no format another tool reads is written, nothing is uploaded, and no history or graph exists. CI cost is the same: ci-timings reads only the open pull requests' latest observation, so a regression of a job's minutes or a gate's pass rate is seen by a person reading runs, not by the repository. The owner's order of 2026-10-22 asks for coverage and pipeline telemetry that can be analysed, improved and connected to Coveralls, Codecov and OpenTelemetry.
milestones.outcome: Every master run's coverage and CI cost is kept as a derived series, exported in LCOV and Cobertura from the one measurement docs/COVERAGE.md requires, uploaded to Coveralls and Codecov when their secrets exist, drawn on the site and in the Cockpit, and emitted as OpenTelemetry when an endpoint is configured; no number differs between the gate, the export and the graph.
milestones.current_state: rust-coverage writes one JSON export per run; validate.yml uploads it for 14 days; .ai/repo/ci/suite-durations.tsv is the only kept CI cost, refreshed by hand.
milestones.desired_state: LCOV and Cobertura exports of the one measurement (I3932); a coverage and CI-cost series per master run with graphs (I3933); OpenTelemetry traces of CI runs (I3934) and of agent sessions (I3935) when an endpoint is configured; every external upload skipped, never failed, without its secret.
non_scope: A second coverage counter, threshold or parser anywhere
Sending anything outside the repository without the owner's secret configured for it
Changing any gate's verdict
acceptance_criteria: The export, the gate and the graph give the same line totals for the same run, shown by a case
A master run's coverage and CI cost are in the series without anyone running a command
With no secret or endpoint configured, every upload and export step is skipped and the run's verdict is unchanged

A GitHub issue created by hand with a record title is adopted by github-sync. A commit need not name its issue. The landing duties of a train member are a table in docs/INTEGRATION.md.

milestones.title: Trusted nodes connect across NAT through proven transports, and every surface says which path
milestones.problem: Master links nodes over multicast on one segment and through rendezvous hubs that must be directly reachable; docs/MESH.md states 'no NAT traversal'. The owner asked four times (10-12, 10-16 twice, 10-18) for NAT traversal, relays, WebRTC and a serverless bootstrap; Operation Convergence defers it past v1.0.0-alpha.1. Proposed in ADR 0202 (The mesh routes work to an identity, never an address, and selects among proven transports instead of implementing NAT traversal); ADR 0203 (GitHub Pages is a signed bootstrap anchor for the mesh, never its signalling channel) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c237#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c237#4, chatgpt-majordomus:c275#19, chatgpt-majordomus:c279#5.
milestones.outcome: A connectivity decision record, a relayed path through a trusted hub, a signed bootstrap manifest on Pages, and a NAT matrix in the mesh lab.
milestones.current_state: Verified: apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/{multicast,broadcast,rendezvous}.rs; rendezvous hubs register but do not relay; seeds: none; no WebRTC/STUN/TURN anywhere in apps/; test/mesh-lab/run has ten scenarios, none behind NAT. Tailscale and Bonjour providers are on branches (I2410).
milestones.desired_state: Endpoint candidates are expiring observations; a link names its path; a node behind NAT cooperates through a relay; a cold node bootstraps from Pages.
non_scope: WebRTC data channels for browsers: after the browser-authentication question (proposed on an unlanded branch, no ADR on master) is decided
Route learning from telemetry: only after the relay is measured
DHT, coordinator election, multi-region gossip
acceptance_criteria: A relayed link and a direct link are both proved in the lab
Pages unavailable leaves every existing link up
risks: A relay is a hub that carries traffic: bandwidth and trust both grow; relayed frames stay authenticated by the existing link signatures but are not encrypted, so a relay hub is private, overlay or behind an encrypted ingress (case 491)
Tailnet users may never need it (open question)
It follows the-mesh-works-out-of-the-box in practice; the edge is kept off the milestone so two milestones of one order are not reordered.

milestones.problem: The signed journal's grammar and fold are sound where tested: events are signed over canonical JSON (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:934-948), the fold orders by (lamport, stream, seq) (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/state.rs:508-513), and proptests permute deliveries. Its durability and its claims are not. Journal::persist ignores write errors (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1984), never fsyncs, and reload drops unparsable lines silently (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1407-1413); an append after a torn tail fuses the next event into the corrupt line. Claims have no fencing: expiry is a fold-time verdict that reverses when the same stream beats again after a sleep or partition (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1681-1697, apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/state.rs:656-661), and the revived claim then beats a claim admitted legitimately in its absence. Release is checked per run, not per session (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:3373-3390). The sync budget ignores the size of the marks (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1734-1766), so a busy journal can exceed MAX_LINK_MESSAGE (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/link.rs:67,70). mesh.events paging returns the journal's maximum lamport as the cursor and skips events (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mesh.rs:594-596, apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:2124-2133). docs/MESH.md:189-190 claims permutation testing that covers one stream of six events. Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: An event the runtime accepted survives a crash or is reported lost; replicas with the same authenticated event set produce the same digest after any delivery order; a claim that expired never returns to beat a claim admitted while it was gone, and every claim conflict is announced; every page of the journal returns every event once.
milestones.current_state: Durable: the node key and every accepted event, with no fsync and ignored write errors. Memory only: registry, links, nonces, tombstones, beats. Exclusivity is local admission plus deterministic post-hoc naming of the winner, with no fencing token and no notification on Held to Conflicted. The journal reload trust check and the Lamport forward bound are I2124 (milestone runtime-trust, in progress on fix/a-remote-caller-cannot-write) and are not repeated here; runtime-trust's criterion that 'an expired claim does not return as live' is met by I2138 in this milestone.
milestones.desired_state: Every row of the audit's consistency contract (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md) names a test: torn tail, failed write, crash during compaction, revived claim, release by another session, sync at the mark bound, paging across shared lamports, and a randomized multi-stream property test with permutation and duplication. docs/MESH.md states exclusivity as local admission with announced conflicts, not as a lock.
non_scope: A global lock, quorum or coordinator. Pack invariant 5 allows refusing strong guarantees instead; the docs already disclaim linearizability (docs/MESH.md:26-27,612-613) and this milestone keeps that position unless an ADR decides otherwise.
The journal reload trust check and the Lamport bound, which are I2124.
Persisting tombstones, which the docs record as a deliberate limit.
acceptance_criteria: A torn or unreadable journal line is counted and reported by mesh doctor, and no complete event before or after it is lost
A write failure is reported and the event is not acknowledged as stored
A claim that expired and revived after a partition is Conflicted, not Held, against a claim admitted during its absence, on every runtime
Two replicas fed the same authenticated events in any order and with duplicates report equal digests, by a multi-stream property test
No sync message exceeds MAX_LINK_MESSAGE, and mesh.events pages return every event once
risks: Adding an epoch to ClaimAcquired is a wire change; it needs the link or event schema version handled as I2164 prices it, or old runtimes will refuse or misread the new field.
fsync on every append costs latency on the heartbeat path; the bound chosen must be measured, not assumed.
I2124 edits the same reload path in apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs; I2137 should land after it.

milestones.title: Work is offered to a peer by capability under a fenced lease, and runs there as an execution
milestones.problem: Since 2026-09-11 the owner asked for work to be placed on peers by capability, health and history. Proposed in ADR 0205 (What a runtime can do is a set of separately evidenced facts, and detection never authorises) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c113#6, chatgpt-majordomus:c154#5, chatgpt-majordomus:c226#2.
milestones.outcome: An assignment is offered, accepted or refused by a peer whose declared capabilities and execution profile satisfy it, and an accepted one runs through the execution plane under the same authorisation as a local call.

risks: Remote execution is the largest trust widening the mesh can make: it waits for ADR 0126's authenticated caller and a decision record of its own

milestones.title: The peer blackboard is one projection, pushed live to every surface
milestones.problem: Who is working on what is already recorded — the board of every checkout (peers.list, gathered per ADR 0044), the mesh journal (sessions, claims, reviews, handovers per ADR 0067) and the monitor's folded signals (ADR 0133) — but no surface shows it as one picture and none shows it live. /cockpit/peers renders peers.list once and never changes; /ui has no peers screen; /cockpit/monitor polls the whole monitor every five seconds; the only WebSocket, /events, carries executions and nothing else; and nothing between the board, the journal and the socket says that anything changed. The unmerged ADR 0162 draft proposed a board channel for the kiosk alone and was never implemented.
milestones.outcome: One capability computes the blackboard from the records that exist; a change of the board or the journal is pushed over one WebSocket to every page that follows it, with the monitor's cursor for resume; /ui, /cockpit and the home page read the same frames; the published site carries a public-safe snapshot labelled as one.
milestones.current_state: peers.list, mesh.state and monitor.stream answer separately; /cockpit/peers is static; /cockpit/monitor polls; socket.js follows executions only.
milestones.desired_state: blackboard.snapshot answers on every interface; a board or journal change reaches a connected page in under a second on this machine; every surface that shows peers reads that one projection.
non_scope: A second peer registry, a message store or a broker; a peer message kind is added to the journal only when reviews and handovers are shown not to carry what peers send each other
A public WebSocket into a private mesh, or credentials in a published bundle
Presence for a provider (OpenAI Dots included) that exposes no supported, authenticated event source
acceptance_criteria: blackboard.snapshot answers the same projection over the command line, HTTP and MCP, with completeness, sources, workers, conflicts, reviews, handovers, typed relations and signals
A board or journal change is pushed to a connected page over one WebSocket that resumes from the monitor's cursor and resynchronises when the cursor cannot be served
/ui/peers, the /ui home panel, /cockpit/peers and the home page read the same frames, and say live, reconnecting, offline or snapshot truthfully
The published site shows a public-safe snapshot of the blackboard with its revision, and no private path, message body or scope
risks: The monitor rereads the whole journal on every page; pushing it on every change multiplies that cost by the subscribers unless one computation is shared by all of them.
A worker's board session and its own mesh session are two records; joining them by anything weaker than an identifier invents a person.

milestones.title: A visitor sees the product prove itself, and can check every claim it makes
milestones.problem: A developer who has never seen Majordomus meets a homepage whose first viewport describes a supervisory control layer in its own vocabulary, beside a console that illustrates each lifecycle command separately. Nothing on it shows the tool doing the one thing that sets it apart — refusing work a worker calls finished — as one story a newcomer can follow, and no page exists that a link from outside could send somebody to. The README's first transcript is hand-written. milestones.title: One usable server per checkout starts, attaches, stops and reports its state without races or hidden kills
milestones.problem: The shared server's election is sound at the create step (O_CREAT|O_EXCL at apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:516-520, proved by apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_shared.rs::a_storm_of_clients_converges_on_one_server_and_one_board and case 191), but what follows it is not. The lease probe is GET / on the same four workers that run tool calls (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:896-925, apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/server.rs:23), so four long calls make a healthy server look dead and a new client takes it over. A server that lost its lease keeps its bridged sessions forever, because bridges ping every 20 s (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:19) and the serve loop counts them as attached (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:136-146). `serve stop` is a SIGTERM whose handler unlinks the lease unconditionally and re-raises (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:1164-1212), so it can delete a successor's lease and never runs the ordered stop (apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:282-289). The lease timings the policy declares never reach the mcp and serve elections (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:89-191 OnceLock filled before apps/majordomus-cli/src/policy.rs:364 runs). Lifecycle state is an observer's reading of a file (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/server.rs:163-177) with no degraded, stopping or failed, and the live server of 2026-10-09 had logged nothing for eight hours because it inherited MAJORDOMUS_LOG=error (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:727-729). A UI-first server stops after 900 s while being viewed, because only MCP sessions count as use (apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:250-253). Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: Entering a checkout, opening the Cockpit, or starting any number of MCP clients converges on one server for that checkout, which is taken over only when it is dead, stops in order when asked, removes only its own lease, reports a typed state every surface reads, and stays up while any surface uses it.
milestones.current_state: Implemented and tested: atomic create, a published URL only after the socket serves (apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:294-305), stale, corrupt, abandoned, busy and superseded leases, port fallback, stdio hygiene. Partial: the probe, takeover and publish are compare-then-act (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:778-798, 1082-1107); a lost server's existing sessions are served indefinitely (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:113-118); SIGTERM is not graceful (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_shared.rs::sigterm_removes_the_lease_before_the_process_dies asserts signal 15); declared timings are dead in mcp and serve. Absent: degraded, stopping and failed states, and liveness from non-MCP use. Refuted premises of the pack: there is no `majordomus ui` command, `serve ensure` and `env enter` are the UI-first entries (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:481-576, apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/env.rs:701-760); `serve ensure` and `serve stop` are CLI-only by stated design and not capabilities; apps/majordomus-cli/src/served.rs is deployment observation, not server lifecycle; the top-level `majordomus doctor` is a governance doctor (lib/doctor.sh:53-77) and checks nothing about the server. The launcher rebuilding the executable in the primary checkout is I2059.
milestones.desired_state: Every lifecycle fault in the audit's matrix has a test: N concurrent first clients, a busy owner, a killed owner, a lost lease with live bridges, a SIGTERM racing a takeover, a declared timing, a UI-only user. server.status answers one of absent, starting, ready, degraded, outdated, stale, stopping or failed, decided in one function. docs/MCP.md and README.md describe the server that ships: one per checkout, what it writes, when it ends.
non_scope: A `majordomus ui` command, unless I2131's record decides one is needed beyond `serve ensure`.
One server for all repositories. ADR 0044 decided one per checkout and the board is gathered across them.

milestones.problem: The runtime pack's baseline audit (2026-10-09, M01) read the server and the mesh against their documents and found the security model held only on the network hop. A server bound beyond loopback accepted every state-changing request from any host that sent no Origin header: plan transitions, continuity writes, any capability through executions.start, and mesh sessions, claims, handovers and reviews that the node then signed with its own trusted key. Three servers on the owner's machine were bound that way at the time. Beside it: reloading the journal skips the trust check, so a revoked key's events return on restart; Lamport stamps are not bounded, so a trusted key can backdate a claim to win every conflict; an expired claim revives and wins after a partition; hello messages name no recipient; trust is read from the branch's working tree; discovery inputs have unbounded channels and reply reads.
milestones.outcome: Discovery is not trust, trust is not authorization, and a caller is admitted to change anything only by a key the trust policy names. A host that can reach a runtime reads it and changes nothing it cannot authenticate; every event in the journal was checked against the trust policy that holds now, whether it arrived over a link or from disk; and the limits the documents state are the limits the code enforces.
milestones.current_state: Remote state-changing requests were admitted by address alone (fixed by I2123). The journal reload, Lamport bounds, claim revival, hello recipient, trust-root and unbounded-input findings stand as recorded in the audit.
milestones.desired_state: Every threat in docs/MESH.md's security model names the test that defends it, and every finding of the baseline audit's threat list is either defended with a test or recorded as a limitation the documents state.
non_scope: Encrypting the transport. ADR 0032 decided no TLS dependency; confidentiality stays the network's.
Accounts or a login. A remote writer, when one is needed, is admitted by a key the trust policy names.
acceptance_criteria: A request from an address that is not loopback runs only a capability that reads or whose input is a signed message, on every transport that knows the caller's address
Every event the journal holds passed the trust policy in force, whether it arrived over a link or was reloaded from disk
A trusted key cannot order its claim before claims already admitted, and an expired claim does not return as live
Every bound the security model names is enforced on the input it names, with a test that sends one more
risks: A remote MCP client loses writes it used to have (announce, mesh sessions). The route that remains is a tunnel that ends on loopback.

milestones.title: Every mesh node follows the published release by itself, versions meet safely, and a release's provenance can be checked
milestones.problem: The pack assumes a self-updater and signed releases. Both premises are refuted. `majordomus update` regenerates provider projections from policy (lib/update.sh:4); there is no self-update command, and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:416-439 says so; to upgrade, a person reruns install.sh with --version. Artifacts are checksummed, not signed: sha256 and size in releases/<tag>.json are checked by site/static/install.sh:478 (called at :706), and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:151-153 defers signing on purpose. What exists is compatibility risk: the superseded check covers only a binary replaced at the same path (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:695-709), while the installer uses one directory per version, so a new client attaches to an older server and only an Outdated warning records it (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/server.rs:410-424). version-surface prices the public surface only; mesh discovery and link versions (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/protocol.rs:36-40, apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/link.rs:50-53), the lease schema and journal events are outside it. Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: An enrolled mesh node follows the stable release by itself through the one installer, forward only, activating in order and rolling back a failed activation (ADR 0161); a newer client replaces an older server in an ordered hand-off and an older client is told it is older; a change to any wire or on-disk schema needs a version bump; a released archive carries a provenance attestation the installer checks.
milestones.current_state: Implemented: install.sh verifies checksum and size, refuses traversal and non-HTTPS; release-verdict gates the release on CI; version-surface covers capabilities, routes, tools, commands and schemas; MCP protocol negotiation. Absent: a reader of the stable pointer on any node (every node is upgraded by hand), cross-path version hand-off, wire-schema pricing, a v1 advertisement fixture, provenance.
milestones.desired_state: The compatibility matrix in plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md lists adjacent client/server and mesh versions with a test for each pair, and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md states what each install path verifies. The owner decided on 2026-10-14 that a background update check is wanted (ADR 0161): every enrolled node follows releases/latest.json through self update, which re-runs install.sh, and the mesh shows each node's version (I2720-I2724).
non_scope: A second installer or updater; install.sh stays the one path (pack M11), and self update re-runs it (ADR 0161).
A network fetch on entering a repository.
Restarting a client's server while it has work in flight; hand-off goes through I2127's session move.
acceptance_criteria: An enrolled, following node is on the version releases/latest.json names within one check interval of a release, with no person on it
A failed activation rolls back to the previous version by itself and the board names node, version and failed check
A client of version N+1 beside a server of version N at another path ends with one server of N+1 and no lost session
A wire or lease or journal schema change without a version bump fails version-surface
Each release archive carries an attestation that verifies for this repository
risks: A hand-off between versions depends on the old server ending its sessions (I2127); landing I2163 first would strand clients on the old server.
Following automatically raises the cost of a bad archive; I2165 (attestation) is raised to p1 with ADR 0161.
Attestation needs repository permissions in the publish job; the release workflow's permissions block changes with it.

milestones.title: Shared policy across repositories and workers
milestones.problem: Policy is per repository. An organisation running many repositories has no way to state a rule once, and no way to see where it is not being followed.
milestones.outcome: A policy can be shared across repositories and workers, with local override remaining explicit and drift from the shared source detectable in one command.
milestones.current_state: Not started. Everything the tool does today is scoped to a single checkout.
milestones.desired_state: One policy statement governs many repositories, and every deviation from it is visible rather than assumed.
non_scope: A hosted service, a registry, or any component that must be running for the tool to work
acceptance_criteria: A shared policy can be consumed by more than one repository without copying it
A local override is explicit and survives an update of the shared source
Drift between the shared policy and a repository's effective policy is reported by one command
risks: Shared policy is where a local tool becomes a distributed one; the offline guarantee has to survive it.

milestones.title: Every surface projects the same state, says when it was observed, and keeps no list of its own
milestones.problem: The core projection holds: the live server's 181 /api/v1 routes equal the 181 OpenAPI operations, which equal the committed docs/generated/openapi.json, and the executor is the only dispatch path (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/executor.rs:156). Around it: freshness is not uniform, since dashboard/overview, episodes, lifecycle/runtime, plan/status, served and mesh carry no observed_at, the overview badge is permanently stale on an idle repository (apps/majordomus-cli/src/index.rs:44, apps/majordomus-cli/src/live.rs:250-252) and GET / said stale: null while serving a build 12 commits behind HEAD. The parity property compares HTTP only for GET routes and excludes the coordination read models (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/properties.rs:166-168,300), and nothing compares CLI JSON with HTTP. /swagger has no CSP and no SRI on the same origin as the write routes (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/swagger.rs:52,79). The Cockpit and the site keep at least nine consumer-side catalogues of what the registry declares, and ADR 0004 says nothing has a second registry. Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: A reader on any surface sees the same value, the time it was observed and whether it is stale; a capability added to or removed from the registry appears or disappears everywhere with no consumer edit; a page served beside the write routes runs only script it shipped.
milestones.current_state: Implemented: routes, OpenAPI, MCP and the generated registry dataset are registry-derived and drift-checked. Partial: freshness, parity, Cockpit data access (five pages read ctx.registry directly, .ai/repo/ui-integrity-baseline.txt:9-13). Second registries: the clap tree (checked both ways by apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/closure.rs), cli/local.rs LOCAL (89 commands), native web surfaces (apps/majordomus-cli/src/web/discover.rs:150), Cockpit routes (three lists, cross-checked), and the consumer copies listed in plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md.
milestones.desired_state: Every state-reporting answer carries observed_at and source, enforced over the registry; the parity property covers writers and the CLI; no Cockpit or site file names a value an enum, a capability or HttpExposure already declares; /swagger and every GET refuse what a hostile page or rebinding host could do.
non_scope: Removing the clap tree or cli/local.rs LOCAL; both are measured second declarations (SURFACES F-1, F-4) and this milestone records them rather than rewriting the CLI.
Writing a static site that claims live state; the site stays a picture labelled as one.
Reporting a replaced executable, which is I1502.
acceptance_criteria: A test over the registry fails when a state-reporting capability answers without observed_at
The parity test covers every capability with an HTTP route and every capability with a CLI path
GET /swagger answers with a CSP and integrity hashes, and a foreign Host is refused on GET
A gate fails on a literal /api/v1/ path or a copied enum value in Cockpit or site code
validation: cargo test --test properties --test projections --test dashboard --test http_serve --test http_host
risks: Adding observed_at to capability outputs changes their schemas and so the public surface; version-surface will price it as a change, which is correct.
Extending parity to POST routes runs writers in tests; each must run against a synthetic repository, never the checkout.

milestones.title: Every verifiable claim and widget resolves to revision-bound test evidence, on every surface
milestones.problem: Claims bind to tests by path, and only `majordomus evidence show` asks whether a claim is proven, always at the working tree of whoever runs it. The site cannot ask that question about the commit it was built from, and no widget on it names the subject that would prove what it shows: where a page says verified, the word was placed by hand. CI runs the suite and the crate tests on every merge and keeps none of it in the ledger. A test that declined to run reads `failing`, while a case that declines by exiting zero is recorded as a pass. The rules module holds a second copy of the freshness derivation, the entry preflight proposed in PR #578 counts a run as current by a filter of its own with no containment test, and ADR 0068 and ADR 0080 disagree about where CI evidence goes. Each surface that wants to say verified derives it differently or not at all.
milestones.outcome: Evidence is indexed by subject and judged at the presented revision, as ADR 0087 records. Every claim, rule, feature, command, capability, MCP tool and use case is a subject of one derived index, and every widget that states behaviour names one. Every surface reads its verdict from the tracked ledger alone, through one freshness function and one aggregation, at the revision it presents: the CLI and HTTP and MCP at the working tree or the checked-out commit, the site at the commit it was built from. A trunk run reaches the ledger through a reviewed recording pull request, and a supplementary record (a run record, coverage, a local row) can only weaken a verdict, naming itself when it does. Verified is rendered only for the one proven row of the freshness table, on every surface.
milestones.current_state: On master at 5a0770c437 the tracked ledger holds local recordings only, and how many claims reach each state is what `majordomus evidence show --format json | jq .totals` prints. There is no subject index; the command-to-test join is derived in shell more than once (`scripts/generate-site-data`, `lib/commands.sh`, `scripts/ci/command-furnished`). `rules/mod.rs` carries its own `changed_since` and its own state mapping beside `evidence/mod.rs`. The decisions this milestone builds on are proposed and unlanded: ADR 0068 on PR #577 (CI evidence as an artifact and a published dataset), ADR 0080 on PR #629 (the recording branch, and the skip word), ADR 0071 on PR #600 (delivery dimensions, with a private containment implementation); PR #597 adds the rules corpus verdict and PR #578 the entry preflight.
milestones.desired_state: A reader of any page of the site follows a widget's badge to the evidence of its subject and sees the verdict at the commit the page was built from, with the run that produced it and every record that weakened it. `majordomus evidence subject <key>` answers the same question from a terminal, over HTTP and over MCP, and the Cockpit shows the same verdict. A merge to master is followed by a recording pull request that lands its run's executions in the ledger. A claim then reads `proven` at a trunk commit that nothing but ledger-only commits separates from the recorded one, and `inputs_unchanged` or `stale`, naming what changed, where other merges landed in between; whether the process makes the first the rule is the owner's decision (ADR 0087, Consequences). A skipped test reads `not_run` with its reason, and no surface anywhere reads greener than the ledger for the revision it presents.
non_scope: Accepting ADR 0041, 0068, 0080 or 0087; acceptance is the owner's act
Bumping the version; a pull request that moves the public surface inherits the version already on master by merging it
Judging a commit other than the checked-out one or the site's build commit
MCP resource templates per subject; evidence is reached through tool calls
Making the required `ci` check depend on the evidence job
New shell automation (ADR 0069)
A regex crate or any other new dependency for the redactor
Stamping use-case evidence with a commit in the committed catalogue
acceptance_criteria: Model: one freshness function, one presented revision, one containment and one aggregation judge every verdict, a skip reads `not_run`, and one derived index names every subject; proven by test/cases/502_evidence_is_judged_at_the_presented_revision.sh, test/cases/507_evidence_subjects_are_derived.sh and test/cases/501_verdict_words_are_status_words.sh

Producer: every recorded run carries the commit and tree it measured, a crate binary that ran nothing is a skip, CI's report is the tracked ledger's verdict derived before the run records, and a trunk run reaches the ledger through one recording pull request, stopping at a commit the ledger covers and recording a ledger-only commit over an unrecorded merge; proven by test/cases/505_a_recording_carries_what_its_run_measured.sh, test/cases/506_a_crate_binary_that_ran_nothing_is_not_a_pass.sh, test/cases/357_ci_records_evidence.sh, test/cases/510_ci_evidence_reaches_the_ledger_through_a_recording_branch.sh and test/cases/511_every_runner_report_carries_its_revision_and_reason.sh

Surfaces: the CLI, HTTP, MCP, the Cockpit and the entry preflight answer by subject from the one authority, and a supplementary record only weakens; proven by test/cases/508_evidence_answers_by_subject.sh, test/cases/509_supplementary_records_only_weaken.sh, test/cases/513_cockpit_shows_evidence.sh, test/cases/514_every_test_line_is_read.sh, test/cases/515_a_local_run_stays_local.sh and test/cases/529_the_preflight_reads_the_one_verdict.sh

Site: every widget names its subject, every subject has an evidence route, the publication is bound to its build and allow-listed, and published text is redacted once; proven by test/cases/504_public_text_is_redacted_once.sh, test/cases/512_evidence_publication_is_a_projection.sh, test/cases/516_evidence_routes_render_from_the_subject_index.sh, test/cases/517_a_panel_subject_is_joined_from_its_route.sh, test/cases/518_evidence_publication_is_bound_to_its_build.sh and test/cases/520_every_widget_names_its_proof.sh

Policy: subject findings refuse, the evidence baseline is rewritten in the same change, and the validator reads every widget; proven by test/cases/522_evidence_check_reads_widgets.sh and test/cases/523_evidence_rules_are_gated.sh

Tests: no surface is greener than the ledger, the badge works in a browser at phone width, tampered evidence is refused, and coverage is shown with its commit; proven by test/cases/524_no_surface_is_greener_than_the_ledger.sh, test/cases/525_an_evidence_badge_works_in_a_browser.sh, test/cases/526_tampered_evidence_is_refused.sh and test/cases/527_coverage_is_shown_with_its_commit.sh
Docs: the evidence reference names what the code declares and is held to the tree; proven by test/cases/528_the_evidence_reference_is_held_to_the_tree.sh

Deploy: a deploy verifies the evidence routes it publishes, and the evidence survives artifact expiry on gh-pages; proven by test/cases/521_deploy_verifies_evidence_routes.sh, test/cases/519_evidence_survives_artifact_expiry.sh and the live page https://majordomus.dev/evidence/
risks: Until the recording branch runs, the tracked ledger holds only local rows and the site renders mostly `not_run`. That is the true state; the badges follow the CI wiring for that reason.
The decisions this milestone builds on are proposed on open pull requests (#577, #578, #597, #600, #629). A slice stacked on one of them waits for it, and the landing order is the owner's.

`proven` at a trunk revision needs a quiet trunk: a recording costs a full suite run and then the required checks, and a code merge landing in that window leaves claims `inputs_unchanged` or `stale` at the landing commit. Until the owner decides whether the process makes `proven` reachable or `required_tests_current` binds to a reachable state, on a busy trunk the delivery dimension rarely passes and the site rarely renders verified (ADR 0087, Consequences).
The recording pull request needs a token whose events start the required workflow. Until the owner chooses between dispatching validate.yml and an App token, the CI wiring slice cannot land.
Every landing makes the open slices' pull requests conflict on derived files; each is refreshed by merging master with the derived merge driver, never by a rebase.

milestones.title: The mesh works out of the box: trusted machines find each other by every means and their sessions cooperate from the first turn
milestones.problem: On 2026-10-10 the owner called mesh cooperation tragic and ordered it to work out of the box, by every discovery means, from the moment an LLM client, the MCP server or `majordomus serve` starts. A read of the code found six gaps that no existing milestone covers: no Tailscale discovery (the tailnet is reached only through 100.x addresses hand-written in .ai/repo/mesh/majordomus.yaml); a server binds and advertises 127.0.0.1 unless told otherwise, so two machines on default settings never dial each other (apps/majordomus-cli/src/cli.rs:3355-3362, mesh/address.rs:39-45); `majordomus init` ships no mesh declaration, so a fresh repository has no mesh at all; a linked worktree with no server of its own has no cooperation (`mesh handover publish` answered 'cooperation inactive'); mesh.state and mesh.peers return 56-134 kB with no filter; and a review request has no body, cannot be closed and never expires.
milestones.outcome: A trusted machine that starts any Majordomus surface in a repository with the mesh declared is linked to every other trusted machine on the LAN or tailnet without a hand-written address, every worktree takes part, and what the mesh holds can be read in one tool answer.

milestones.title: A repository that adopts Majordomus gains two directories and two lines, and can give them back
milestones.problem: What Majordomus leaves in a repository it adopts is not decided anywhere; it is the sum of what each subsystem happened to write. Provider files at the root, scripts, configuration beside configuration, generated registries that became inputs, and no record of which of them Majordomus put there. The costs compound in three directions at once. A person cannot tell what is theirs and what is the tool's, so nothing can be safely removed. A second provider means a second copy of the same instructions rather than a second adapter. And every subsystem rediscovers the repository for itself — the CLI, the environment entry, the documentation, the server — so the same facts are read four ways and disagree on the fourth.
milestones.outcome: Adoption is a reconciliation, not a template copy. One typed repository model is discovered once and every consumer reads it. A desired integration is computed from that model, diffed against what the repository actually holds, and applied as the smallest mutation that closes the gap — with everything Majordomus owns living under `.ai/` and `.majordomus/`, and anything outside those two namespaces reduced to a small managed bridge whose ownership is recorded. Running the reconciliation twice changes nothing the second time, and uninstalling gives back exactly what was taken and nothing a person authored.
milestones.current_state: `.ai/` and `.majordomus/` both exist and carry real material, and directory contracts are already enforced under `.ai/` (ADR 0011). Against that: provider bootstraps are generated to the root, the environment entry and the CLI each discover the repository their own way, `init` writes what it was written to write rather than what the repository lacks, no ledger records what was placed outside the two namespaces, and nothing can undo an adoption.
milestones.desired_state: `majordomus init` on a foreign repository adds `.ai/`, `.majordomus/`, a managed block in `AGENTS.md` and — when direnv is wanted — one stable line in `.envrc`. A second run reports no change. `majordomus uninstall` removes what the ledger records and leaves authored knowledge alone. Adding a valid artifact under a discoverable namespace registers it everywhere, and no list anywhere enumerates what discovery already finds.
non_scope: A configuration format that restates what the repository can be inspected for
Rewriting a working subsystem for symmetry rather than for a defect
Deleting user-authored content on any path, under any flag, without an explicit and separate instruction
A second worktree convention, a second handover format or a second doctor
Provider-specific semantics anywhere but an adapter
acceptance_criteria: Everything Majordomus persists in an adopted repository lives under `.ai/` or `.majordomus/`, and every exception outside them is a bridge recorded in the ownership ledger
One typed repository model is discovered once per process and every consumer — CLI, environment, API, MCP, Cockpit, documentation, providers, completion — reads that model rather than the filesystem
The desired integration is a value, the plan is a diff against what is there, and the apply is the smallest mutation that closes it
A second `init` on a conforming repository produces no change, proved by a test rather than by observation
`uninstall` reverses every recorded mutation, refuses to touch a bridge a person has edited, and leaves `.ai/` authored content in place by default
Every generated artifact declares its provenance, its generator and the inputs it derives from, and no generated artifact is read back as canonical input
No hand-maintained list enumerates artifacts that discovery finds, and adding a valid artifact registers it in every consumer with no second edit
Environment entry stays local and bounded, with no network and no build, and its cost is measured against a declared budget
Every invariant above is a project rule with a check that CI executes, each proved by a negative test
risks: A reconciler that computes a desired state can also impose one. Everything it would change outside the two namespaces has to be visible in a dry run before it is applied, and a bridge a person edited is a conflict rather than an overwrite.

One repository model is a bottleneck as well as a spine: every consumer that reads it pays its discovery cost. The cost has to be measured against the environment-entry budget before the model becomes mandatory, not after.

Migrating this repository's own footprint is the most dangerous phase, because the tool is being changed by the thing it is changing. The migration runs through the reconciler with a dry run first, never through a move script.

An ownership ledger that drifts from the filesystem is worse than none: it authorises deletions it cannot justify. Every recorded mutation carries the hash it was written with, and a mismatch stops the removal.
Provider adapters invite provider semantics to leak into the model. The test is whether a new provider is an implementation of one trait, or an edit in six places.
