The consequence is exact — /cockpit/executions can only ever show work started through that server by executions.start, everything a developer actually runs is invisible to it, and docs/EXECUTIONS.md's live channel, which genuinely works and streams frames, is a window onto a plane almost nothing writes to. Combined with non-durability, which the execution module already states as its own decision, the execution history a development surface needs does not exist anywhere today.

issues.title: A rebuild that fails consumes no change: the next request retries it
non_scope: The stamp's watched files (WORKTREE_FILES, COMMON_FILES)
The mid-rebuild rule: a request arriving during a rebuild is still served the existing generation
issues.objective: When a long-lived server's rebuild of its repository picture fails, keep the change it noticed unconsumed, so that a later request retries the load (bounded, not on every request) instead of serving the previous generation until git happens to move again.
issues.why: Found while closing the case 545 flake (fix/ci-flakes-545-and-multicast 79ecdbb944, batch B3 #788): Live::reload (apps/majordomus-cli/src/live.rs, the Err arm of `match built`) records `state.stamp = taken` when App::load fails, so the stamp the failed load was taken under now reads as current. A transient failure — a git process caught mid-write, an index.lock, a manifest saved half-way — therefore makes the server miss the commit that triggered it, and every answer (HTTP, MCP, Cockpit) keeps the old head with a fresh-looking observed_at until some unrelated move. The comment there gives the reason (not to retry a failing load on every request); the cost of that choice is a commit silently not seen. Case 545 now polls for the new head and prints the server's 'would not load' line when it fails, so an occurrence names this path.
issues.current_state: A failed App::load sets the generation's stamp to the stamp it was taken under: the change is consumed, and no request retries the load until the git control files move again.
issues.desired_state: A failed load leaves the generation's stamp as it was and records the failure (stamp and moment) beside it; a request whose stamp equals the failed one retries the load once a bounded interval has passed since that failure, and is served the previous generation (with the failure said) inside it. A stamp that moves again retries at once. The warning names the retry.
acceptance_criteria: A load that fails and then would succeed, with no further repository move, is retried after the interval and the next answer carries the new head
A load that keeps failing is attempted at most once per interval, not once per request
Case 545 still passes; with the retry removed, the new test fails

The signal handler unlinks the lease whenever HELD is set and re-raises with SIG_DFL (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:1164-1212, the unlink at 1197-1211), so between a takeover and the old owner's next 500 ms tick a SIGTERM to the old owner unlinks the new owner's lease. take_over reads, compares and then calls remove_file (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:778-798) in three steps, so two electors that both judged one lease stale can interleave and the second unlinks the first's fresh lease; publish checks is_mine and then renames the fixed tmp name server.json.tmp (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:1082-1107) with no fsync, so a takeover between the check and the rename is overwritten. serve stop sends SIGTERM (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:814,890-903) and SharedServer::stop (apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:282-289, closing episodes and draining the mesh) never runs; apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_shared.rs::sigterm_removes_the_lease_before_the_process_dies asserts the process dies of signal 15, while the comment at apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:274-281 implies serve stop runs the ordered stop. Every serve stop leaves open episodes for recover_orphans and cuts in-flight answers. LeaseView.pid is documented as informational (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/server.rs:236) although liveness (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:742), the spawn claim (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:354-356) and serve stop (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:814) decide from it. Baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44, lifecycle gaps 5 and 11, drift 5 and 6. Graceful termination of in-flight responses in the production container is I0906 (fly-deployment); this issue covers the lease and the episodes locally.
issues.current_state: Lease removal by the signal handler and by take_over does not re-check the token. serve stop is a hard kill that removes the lease first.
issues.desired_state: The serve loop turns SIGTERM into a flag it polls, waits a bounded time for peers to leave and runs SharedServer::stop; only then is the lease released through the path that checks is_mine. take_over renames the stale file aside under its own token and confirms what it moved before claiming. publish writes a tmp file named for its token and syncs it before the rename. A second SIGTERM, or the bound passing, still ends the process.
acceptance_criteria: A SIGTERM to a server whose lease was taken over within the same tick leaves the new owner's lease file in place
After serve stop, the stopped server's episodes are closed and recover_orphans finds none of them
Two electors that both judged one lease stale end with exactly one lease, held by the process the file names
The stopped process exits by its own return, not by signal 15, within serve stop's documented bound
The comment at apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:274-281 and the LeaseView.pid doc describe what the code does

issues.title: A hello names the runtime it is meant for, and no other runtime accepts it
issues.objective: Bind each link hello to its intended recipient inside the signed bytes, refuse a hello addressed elsewhere, and make the documented check order the one the code runs.
issues.why: Hello (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/link.rs:444-456) names no audience. The nonce cache that refuses a replay is per answerer, held in memory and checked after trust (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:1847-1875), so a captured hello replays to another runtime of the same repository, or to the same runtime after a restart, within the 300 s skew window (threat T6). The effect is a displaced inbound link and a false 'connected' for the real peer (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:1918-1934); the replayer cannot sync. docs/MESH.md:128-136 and item 1 of rule project.mesh-cooperation-is-authenticated put the nonce check before protocol, self, repository and trust; the code checks it last on purpose, so strangers cannot fill the cache, while the blocking rule says 'verify, in order'. Baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44, mesh gap 9 and drift 1.
issues.current_state: A valid hello is accepted by any runtime of the repository that trusts its key and has not seen its nonce.
issues.desired_state: Hello carries an optional to (the runtime key it means to reach) inside its signed bytes; the dialer fills it whenever it knows the key (a registry target, or a runtime it linked before); accept_hello refuses a hello addressed elsewhere as misaddressed, before the replay cache sees its nonce; a hello without to is still admitted (seeds, first contacts, releases before this one), so the link protocol version is unchanged and a mixed fleet keeps linking. docs/MESH.md states the order the code checks in and why the nonce cache is last. The deferred part, bringing rule project.mesh-cooperation-is-authenticated to the code's check order, is I2703.
acceptance_criteria: A hello captured from a link to runtime A and replayed to runtime B within the skew window is refused with a typed refusal and changes no link of B
A hello replayed to A after A restarts cannot displace an established link

issues.title: Every mesh input and answer has a bound, and a refused registration learns nothing
issues.objective: Bound the discovery channel, every reply a runtime reads and the candidates it accepts; answer a refused registration with its refusal alone; and give every link retry a floor and jitter.
issues.why: The provider channel is unbounded (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/manager.rs:425 channel()) and feeds one thread that runs an Ed25519 verify per datagram, with no per-source rate and no drop counter (threat T3). Rendezvous and link replies to the dialer are read with an unbounded read_to_end (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:84-85) under a per-read timeout only, so a slow trickle holds the worker and the per-runtime round lock (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:2383-2387) (T4), and the candidate count received is unbounded. docs/MESH.md:341 lists 'messages (900 KiB)' as a flood bound, which holds only for what the answerer receives (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:1769-1779, 2010-2020) and the dialer sends (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/link.rs:883-888). mesh.register answers its own envelope and up to 32 candidates even when the caller's envelope is refused (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/manager.rs:623-636), and the candidates include untrusted nodes of any repository (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/registry.rs:342-357) (T2, T13). An UnknownLink answer is retried with zero delay (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:2592-2595), so a peer that welcomes and then refuses sync drives a busy loop, and the link backoff has no jitter (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:2611-2614). Baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44, mesh gaps 5 and 11, threats T2, T3, T4 and T13, drift 5.
issues.current_state: Inputs the answerer receives are bounded; the discovery channel, replies the dialer reads, received candidates and registration answers are not.
issues.desired_state: Providers send through a bounded queue (OBSERVATION_QUEUE, 1024) whose drops are counted as overflow in mesh.status refusals; a refused registration is answered with the refusal alone, and an admitted one with this node and the trusted nodes of the caller's own repositories (MeshRegistry::candidates_for; the unfiltered candidates is gone); an answerer that keeps answering unknown_link is retried no faster than a heartbeat after the first immediate retry. The deferred part, the dialer's reply and candidate bounds, jitter on the link backoff and a test of the unknown_link retry rate, is I2704.
acceptance_criteria: Datagrams beyond the channel bound are dropped and counted in mesh status, and the process's memory stays bounded under a flood test
A registration whose envelope is refused receives no candidate, and no answer carries a candidate of another repository

issues.title: A key removed from the trust list loses its links without a restart, and a node key can be rotated
issues.objective: Re-read the trust declaration while the runtime runs, drop the links and admission of a de-listed key, offer a key rotation that peers can follow, and create the node key file private from its first byte.
issues.why: Trust is frozen at activation (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/manager.rs:466,486, apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:1150): a key removed from trust.allow keeps its links until every peer restarts, and there is no rotate or revoke flow (threat T11). A compromised key therefore cannot be cut off without restarting every runtime. The node key file is written and then chmodded to 0600 (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/identity.rs:338-347), so it exists for a moment at umask permissions. Reloaded events of a revoked key are I2124's (the journal reload applies the trust policy, milestone runtime-trust); this issue is the live half. Baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44, mesh gap 6 and the identity row.
issues.current_state: Revocation takes effect only on each peer's restart. Rotation does not exist. The key file is briefly readable at umask permissions.
issues.desired_state: Cooperation holds its trust as a replaceable value; Cooperation::retrust puts a new one in force and ends the link of every peer it no longer trusts, and the server calls it with each new generation of the repository it reads, so a key withdrawn from trust.allow and committed loses its links without a restart: its next sync meets unknown_link and its hello is refused untrusted. The deferred part, rotating a node key and purging a withdrawn key's events from the running journal, is I2705.
acceptance_criteria: Removing a key from trust.allow on a running runtime closes that key's links within one heartbeat and refuses its next hello, with no restart
Under a permissive umask the node key file is never readable by group or others

issues.title: An accepted mesh event is on disk before it counts, and a damaged journal line is reported, never fused or dropped silently
issues.objective: Make journal appends and compaction rewrites durable and failure-reporting, and make reload survive a torn tail without losing or fusing a complete event.
issues.why: Journal::persist ignores write errors (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1984, let _ = file.write_all) and never fsyncs; reload reads the whole file with read_to_string and drops every unparsable line silently (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1407-1413); an append after a torn tail with no trailing newline fuses the next event into the corrupt line (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1969-1984), so one crash also loses the event after it. The compaction rewrite (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:2250-2264) has the same properties, and the file is created at the default umask. The only reload test uses a clean file (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:2655, a_reloaded_journal_keeps_events_and_resurrects_no_liveness). Disk full is handled nowhere on this path; the only sync_all in the crate is apps/majordomus-cli/src/economics/runner.rs:1035. The journal holds other runtimes' events and handover bodies (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1961-1985), so a lost line is lost cooperation. Baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44, failure gap 4 and the failure-class rows disk full, truncated journal and partial write.
issues.current_state: Writes are best effort and unreported; a torn tail corrupts the next event; unreadable lines vanish on reload.
issues.desired_state: An append writes a missing trailing newline first (a torn tail stays one unreadable line), syncs, and counts a failure in JournalTallies.write_failures instead of discarding it; reload counts unreadable lines (JournalTallies.unreadable); compaction writes a synced file and renames it over the old one, then syncs the directory; the file is created owner-only (0600); mesh doctor fails its journal check while either count is nonzero. The deferred part, a reload size bound and refusing to acknowledge an own event whose append failed, is I2706.

A failed write on a read-only or full file system in a test is counted and reported by mesh doctor

issues.title: A sync message stays under the link bound whatever the marks weigh

issues.title: A tool call that may have run is never sent a second time
issues.objective: Make the stdio bridge resend a message only when the server provably did not receive or run it, and report every other failure as the error it is, so no tool call executes twice.
issues.why: The bridge waits REQUEST_TIMEOUT, 60 s, for an answer (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:25). A timeout is Unreachable, which makes Session::failover re-elect (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:229-311); when the election finds the same server as Peer, the bridge reinitializes and calls b.handle(&message) again (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:301, and :283 after a takeover), so the same tools/call is sent twice. A slow repository_mutation tool (there are six, plus executions.start, which runs any capability) can therefore run twice. Any 4xx other than 404, such as 413, 403 or 400, also triggers a re-election (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:352): a message over the 1 MiB body limit (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/server.rs:20, the 413 at :227-232) becomes 413, then a resend, then -32603 'shared server unavailable', which names the wrong cause. issues.title: The MCP transports bound what they read and follow the Streamable HTTP rules they claim
issues.objective: Apply one declared message bound to stdin lines, request bodies and every response the bridge reads, validate MCP-Protocol-Version, issue unpredictable session ids, and never reap a session whose request is still running.
issues.why: Bounds are asymmetric. stdin lines have no length bound (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/stdio.rs:40); request bodies are capped at 1 MiB (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/server.rs:20,207-214) but the owner's in-process stdio session is not; responses the bridge reads have no cap (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:85, read_to_end), and the mesh's rendezvous and link replies go through the same function (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:84-85). On the Streamable HTTP endpoint the MCP-Protocol-Version and Accept headers are ignored, session ids are pid-seq-subsecnanos and predictable (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:159), and the 90 s idle reaper can expire a session whose single request is still running, because last_seen is stamped only when a request starts (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:138). Baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44, lifecycle gap 14, the payload-limit row and the Streamable HTTP row.

issues.desired_state: stdio lines are bounded at MAX_LINE_BYTES (the HTTP body bound, 1 MiB) and an over-long one is answered with a parse error while the session goes on; every reply bridge::request reads is bounded at MAX_REPLY_BYTES (32 MiB) — the stdio bridge, rendezvous and mesh links alike; MCP-Protocol-Version is validated against PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (400 otherwise); session ids are 128 bits from the OS random source; last_seen is stamped again when the answer is written. Not done here: the Accept header and the GET/SSE half of Streamable HTTP.

Session ids are drawn from the operating system's random source

issues.title: The record pull request's dispatched verdict does not satisfy branch protection
issues.objective: Make the record pull request a release proposes mergeable without a person closing and reopening it, or stop docs/DISTRIBUTION.md and case 996 from saying that it is.
issues.why: docs/DISTRIBUTION.md ('Why the release asks for the verdict of its record') says the publish job dispatches validate on release/record-<tag>, that the check-runs attach to the head commit the pull request reads, and so the record no longer sits with an empty rollup until somebody closes and reopens it. On 2026-10-10 the v0.19.1 record, #866 at head 03e1d8a597, had exactly that dispatched run (38015081212) conclude success with a `ci` check-run from app 15368, the app and context master's branch protection requires (strict false, no rulesets). The merge was refused with 'base branch policy prohibits'. The pull_request run the record's opening caused (38015082449, actor github-actions[bot]) concluded failure with zero jobs; both check suites are associated with pull request 866, and its statusCheckRollup stayed empty until a close and reopen at 05:22Z started pull_request run 38027303212. The dispatch has not yet made a record mergeable on its own: v0.18.0's (#832) dispatch failed and it merged after a close/reopen run, v0.19.0's (#861) was admin-merged. Case 996 holds that the two workflows are wired to each other; it never observes a record pull request become mergeable. Each release since has lost one CI cycle, about 90 minutes, between publication and the record reaching the site.
issues.current_state: The publish job opens the record pull request with GITHUB_TOKEN and dispatches validate on its branch. The dispatched run's `ci` does not count: the rollups of #1142 and #1147 list no check although their dispatched `ci` passed, and on 2026-10-16 v0.27.0's record (#1273, head a2aa25f) was refused with its dispatched `ci` green (run 38865302829). Its pull_request run (38865305333) was created action_required, not failed with zero jobs as through v0.26.0, and the record merged on that run once a person approved it. Since fix/the-record-dispatch-is-not-the-records-verdict, release.yml, the record pull request's body, docs/DISTRIBUTION.md ('Who starts the record's verdict', the runbook and the failure table) and case 996 call the dispatch an early reading and name the person's step: approve the waiting run, or close and reopen (majordomus prs drain). What remains is the owner's decision on a GitHub App or fine-grained token that would make the record's own run start without a person; until then record_pull_request_mergeable_without_reopen cannot be shown.

When the lower one lands, the upper head does not contain master's merge commit, so the queue calls it `behind` and wants a refresh: a merge of master that changes no file, a new head, and a second 398 job-minute run for a tree the first run already judged. issues.title: No screen waits for a source: a page shows the latest reading with its age, read again behind the reader
issues.objective: Take every handler, git call and file read off the path of a UI request: the executor keeps the latest reading of each source a page asked for, a screen is rendered from those readings at once, and a worker reads a source again behind the reader whenever the reading is not of the repository as it is now.
issues.why: The owner said on 2026-10-12 that the UI 'is tragically slow' and is to be solved 'architecturally'. Measured on the UI-performance batch's build (c66f49e406, debug, load 20): /ui 2.2-2.5 s on every request, because health.report (2.4 s, probes, not cacheable) is in its first paint; the first request after a start or a change 5.6-8.1 s for roadmap, evidence and governance, because a cache keyed by the repository's state is empty exactly then; /ui/panels/delivery 75.7 s. A page costs its slowest source and no cache changes that. ADR 0142 records the decision.
issues.current_state: A screen asks its sources through ctx.execute and waits for all of them (ui/source.rs ask_all). A cached source answers at once while the repository stands still; an uncached one and the first read after any change run the handler on the request.
issues.desired_state: capability::readings keeps, per source and input, what it last answered, when, how long it took and in which state of the repository. Context::read hands that over: at once when it is of the repository as it is now, with a worker reading it again behind the caller once it is older than a second; after at most 50 ms, marked stale and refreshing, when the repository has moved, and then every other source read lately is read again too; after waiting for the first reading when there is none, said as pending past a minute. One worker per source, four at once in all, above the executor's own cache and single flight. execute is unchanged and exact. ui::source asks for readings; an answer carries its standing (age, current/stale/pending, refreshing); a source line says a reading's age once it is older than five seconds and says when it predates the last change; a line whose reading is catching up carries data-catching-up and the page's script reads the screen again after 0.4 s, doubling to 6.4 s, until none is left. The first reader of the UI starts one background pass over SCREENS and PANELS. MAJORDOMUS_CAPABILITY_CACHE=off makes a reading run its handler; MAJORDOMUS_READING_PATIENCE_MS sets the patience, and wait makes every read exact.

issues.objective: Decide which HTTP stack the shared server keeps, from a measurement of the two candidates on the same routes, a streamed route and long-lived subscribers, and record the decision so that the repository has one stack and knows why.
issues.why: ADR 0142, part 3, and step U6 of the owner's UI-performance pack, which the caching work deferred because a cached capability already answers in under 6 ms at p95. That measurement did not include what a streamed UI adds: a connection held open per page. The server runs each request on a thread of its own, at most 64 at once (http/server.rs MAX_HANDLERS), writes a response whole, and has no compression. The owner asked on 2026-10-12 for a top-notch architecture; the pack says the choice is made on same-route benchmarks and that two stacks are not kept.

issues.title: A screen over its budget fails the build: the UI's latency budgets are benchmark policy, and bench --check holds them
issues.objective: Make the owner's UI latency budget something CI enforces: the benchmark policy declares absolute bounds, bench --check holds them with or without a baseline and on every host, and the ui job runs that check on every change that can slow a screen.
issues.why: ADR 0142, part 4. The owner's pack set the budgets (a cached capability under 50 ms at p95, a warm server-rendered page under 100 ms, a live update under 250 ms) and said they are 'measured, never invented'. Today nothing holds them: the bench times the UI's screens since the UI-performance batch, and reports; it refuses nothing. The UI was eight seconds slow on master for a day before a person said so.
issues.current_state: majordomus bench times every screen of the UI (system.http.ui.* over a pinned context, system.http.live.ui.* over the live view) and bench --check compares a run with a baseline of the same host. A target that was always too slow never regresses, and a platform with no baseline compares nothing, so nothing held a screen to a bound. Measured before this change, debug build at load 57: every warm screen at 1-21 ms p95 except /ui/command at 400-660 ms.
issues.desired_state: .ai/repo/benchmarks/rust/policy.yaml gains budgets: each a prefix of target keys, a cache mode, a metric, a bound in milliseconds and a minimum number of samples, every key but the last required and a malformed one a policy error that names it. Check::compare judges every measurement a budget bounds, whether or not a baseline exists and whatever host recorded it, as PASS, OVER or SHORT; bench --check prints the budget lines with the target, its value and its bound, says within or over budget, and exits 10 when anything is over. The policy declares a warm screen of the UI within 100 ms at p95 for both views. The ui job of validate runs bench system.http. --check before the browser audit, as a step of the ui-audit gate. /ui/command no longer walks the registry once per command: it indexes command lines once per screen. Not done here: measuring the first request after the repository moved, which is I2485.
acceptance_criteria: A warm screen measured over its budget fails bench --check with exit 10 and no baseline to compare, and the report names the screen, its value and its bound
A budget bounds only the prefix and the cache mode it names, and a measurement of fewer samples than its minimum is SHORT and does not fail
A budget with a required key missing, or a cache mode that is not one, is a policy error that names the key
The repository's policy declares the UI's budget for the pinned and the live view, and every screen is within it
The ui job runs the check before the browser audit, under a bound smaller than the job's

issues.title: A personal layer changes nothing shared: init --personal and install.sh --personal keep the layer one person's own, verify it, and --shared hands it to the team
non_scope: Access control, or any way around an organisation's rules about tools: the layer is on the disk in plain sight
Installing the commit and push hooks: init installs none in either mode
Carrying a personal layer to another machine: it is one checkout's, and the mesh is the way across
issues.objective: Let one person use the tool on real work in a repository other people share without changing anything shared: one flag on init and on the installer, every later writer covered by the same mechanism, the result verified at install and on every doctor, the executable reading an untracked layer without being told to, and one command that hands the layer to the team.
issues.why: ADR 0145. A plain init writes the tracked .gitignore (lib/init.sh, mj_init_gitignore), update writes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md at the root (lib/update.sh), capture install writes .claude/ (lib/capture.sh), and doctor fails until README.md names AGENTS.md (lib/doctor.sh, mj_validate_bootstrap). No product code wrote .git/info/exclude. The Rust executable enumerates tracked files only (apps/majordomus-cli/src/discovery/mod.rs), so an untracked layer was an empty one unless --discovery filesystem was passed, and no launcher, hook or client configuration passes it. Case 86 held a hand-written list of the installer's flags, so a new flag could go undocumented and pass.
issues.current_state: A person who wants a layer of their own writes an exclude file by hand; update and capture install write past it; nothing verifies it; the executable sees no rule, prompt or record in such a layer; there is no step from a personal layer to a shared one.
issues.desired_state: majordomus init --personal and install.sh --personal create the plain layer, cover it in the common git directory's info/exclude, and fail unless git status reads the same after as before. update and capture install cover each path before writing it and refuse a tracked one whole. doctor verifies the cover on every run. Discovery walks the work tree when the manifest is tracked nowhere. init --extend --shared removes the cover and commits nothing. Case 86 reads the installer's flags from its parser.
acceptance_criteria: In a repository with uncommitted work, init --personal leaves git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all byte-identical, writes no tracked file, and exits 10 if it could not
update and capture install under a personal layer leave git status identical, and update refuses (15) a projection target git tracks before writing any target
doctor reports the personal layer verified, names a file of it that is tracked, and does not fail the tracked README for not naming AGENTS.md
The executable lists the rules of an untracked layer with no --discovery option
install.sh --personal verifies the result itself and says so; outside a repository it keeps the installed tool and says which half failed
init --extend --shared removes the block, writes the two .gitignore lines, prints the paths to commit, commits nothing, and refuses (15) a layer that is not personal
A flag accepted by the installer's parser and absent from its --help fails case 86

One node per generated file; a node is a producer whose run is the unit of cost

issues.title: A node's key is computed from the bytes its producer reads, the index membership it enumerates and the generation of the executable
non_scope: Changing the fingerprint committed in site/data/generated/source.json or any stamp a generated file carries; those are I1409's
A new hash algorithm or a new cryptographic dependency; the crate already uses sha2
Remembering keys by modification time or size
issues.objective: Give every node of the derivation graph a deterministic SHA-256 key over its identity, its operation version, its declared inputs as the producer actually reads them, the keys of the nodes it depends on and the generation of the executable, with a schema version of its own.
issues.why: campaigns/majordomus-incremental-derive-prompt-pack/03_03_HASHES_FINGERPRINT.md asks for length-framed content keys that honour both git index membership and working-tree bytes and never rely on modification time or on the HEAD tree alone. The repository already has both halves in separate places and neither per producer: apps/majordomus-cli/src/generation.rs frames path and content lengths into a SHA-256 over the crate's sources, and scripts/generate-site-data hashes one list of every input of the whole site. majordomus generate enumerates through the index (--discovery vcs) and reads working-tree bytes, which scripts/derive states as the reason it refuses untracked files, so a key over either alone would be wrong.
issues.current_state: One fingerprint covers all of stage B and none covers a target of majordomus generate. A change to any input of the site moves the one hash; a change to an input of a single target moves nothing that can be read.
issues.desired_state: derivation::key computes, for a node, a digest over a domain separator, the key schema version, the node id, the operation version, each input in canonical order as kind, path, presence and length-framed bytes, the dependency keys, and crate_generation of the tree. A missing file differs from an empty one, a rename moves the key, a path entering or leaving the index moves the key of a node that enumerates it, a symbolic link is hashed as a link and never followed outside the root, and an input kind the function cannot read makes the node always regenerate. Amended on 2026-10-18 by the derive-performance plan: the key covers negative lookups (a path that would be enumerated if it were created), creation and deletion; derive explain reports the exact invalidation frontier of a change; and a detected fact never authorises a materialisation, so facts, inference, policy and permission stay separate.

A missing declared file and an empty one give different keys
A different crate generation or operation version changes every key that depends on it
A symbolic link pointing outside the repository root is not read, and its node is reported as always regenerating
For each node, the declared inputs contain every path the producer was observed to read in I2521

issues.title: A resumed mesh.events walk returns every event exactly once, across partitions
non_scope: mesh state's fold and digest, which already converge on any delivery order
The sync protocol and its marks budget, which the milestone's other issues own
A global order of events across runtimes; the walk is complete and duplicate-free, not linearizable
issues.objective: A reader that walks mesh.events page by page and resumes from the cursor each page answers receives every event the runtime accepts, exactly once, including an event from a writer that was partitioned from the mesh and stamped it at or below a position the walk already passed.
issues.why: Leaf M02.5.1 (PR #1207, I2140) proved that a walk resumed from each page's lamport returns every event once while the reader's own events, and peers' events stamped above the walk's position, keep arriving (unit tests paging_by_stamp_returns_every_event_exactly_once and paging_while_events_arrive_returns_every_event_exactly_once), and documented in docs/MESH.md, under 'Paging the raw journal', the one arrival outside that walk: a runtime partitioned away keeps writing with its own Lamport clock, and when the link returns its events arrive stamped at or below the reader's cursor. events_after filters lamport > after (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:2367-2385), so those events are never returned to the resumed walk; they reach only mesh state's fold or a walk restarted from an earlier after. A Lamport stamp is its writer's, not the reader's arrival order, so no single-stamp cursor can fix this; the cursor itself has to change.
issues.current_state: mesh.events answers lamport, the stamp of the last event on the page, as the next after (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mesh.rs:754-786), and a page never ends inside a run of equal stamps. An event that arrives after the walk passed its stamp is silently missing from the walk, with no signal to the reader. Sync between runtimes already exchanges per-stream high-water marks (Journal::marks, marks_for, missing_for in apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1765-1974); paging does not use them.
issues.desired_state: The cursor mesh.events answers, and mesh events --after and /events?after= accept, names every event already returned, so a resumed walk returns a late event below the reader's position once and never repeats one; docs/MESH.md states the guarantee and drops the stated gap. The design is chosen when this issue is taken, recorded with its evidence, and not here. Candidates: (a) a per-writer cursor, the last (stream, seq) returned per stream, so a page returns each stream's events above its own seq; (b) a version vector over streams, the same marks sync already exchanges, carried as an opaque token; (c) per-runtime high-water marks of arrival, a local arrival sequence the reader resumes from, which keeps the token small but is valid only against the runtime that issued it. Each must state its token size bound, how it behaves after compaction drops events below a mark, and whether the scalar lamport after stays accepted for existing readers.
acceptance_criteria: A test reproduces the gap before the fix: two runtimes, A and B, linked; a reader walks A's mesh.events with a small limit past B's stamp; the link is cut, B appends an event whose lamport is at or below the reader's cursor, the link is restored and A accepts it; resuming the walk from the last answered cursor returns that event
The same test, with the walk resumed repeatedly and with the late event also delivered twice, returns every event of the journal exactly once over the whole walk
The cursor the schema documents is the cursor the next page accepts on the command line, over HTTP and over MCP
docs/MESH.md 'Paging the raw journal' states the guarantee across partitions and names the test

issues.title: A provider hook declares its timeout, and the session end closes its episode inside the budget
issues.objective: `capture install` writes a per-hook `timeout` for every hook it generates. The values come from one declared table per provider and event, read by both the configuration writer and the end handler. The SessionEnd handler keeps the episode close inside that budget: it skips the optional closing checkpoint and continuation, as typed failures, when running them would leave the close too little of the budget. A configuration that byte-for-byte matches the shape this tool wrote before timeouts existed is rewritten to the new shape. Any other configuration is left as it is, and install names the timeouts it lacks.
issues.why: Claude Code gives SessionEnd hooks a shared 1.5-second budget unless a per-hook timeout is set, and then at most 60 seconds (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, Hook timeouts). It cancels a command hook that reaches its timeout and discards its output. The generated configurations set no timeout. Measured on 2026-10-19 on a scratch adopter (OSCILLA) under 0.30.0, the SessionEnd capture took 2.9 to 4.0 s at load 28-56 and 8.5 s at load 66: the closing checkpoint about 2 s, the continuation about 2.5 s, then the close. The end event was therefore cut short before the episode closed, which matches the adopter's doctor findings 'the writer has stopped' and 'open episodes nothing closed'. The same configurations leave SessionStart and PreCompact on the 600-second default, so a hung start can stall a fresh client for ten minutes.
issues.current_state: mj_capture_config writes type and command only. mj_capture_session_end runs checkpoint, continuation, mesh leave and close in order, with no deadline. An installed configuration that names the hooks is left without timeouts.
issues.desired_state: Every generated hook carries the declared timeout. The end handler measures its own elapsed time against the declared budget and always reaches the close. Upgrading an untouched generated configuration adds the timeouts; a hand-edited one is reported, not rewritten. Case 3460 proves all three.
acceptance_criteria: After `capture install`, each of UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, SessionEnd and PreCompact in .claude/settings.json carries the timeout the provider table declares, and SessionEnd's is at most 60
A configuration identical to the pre-timeout generated shape is rewritten with the timeouts; a configuration with any other content is left byte-identical and install names the missing timeouts
The SessionEnd shim, given a provider session that was started, closes the episode in less than its declared timeout
With the end budget forced below the optional steps' cost, the episode still closes, and the skipped checkpoint and continuation are recorded as typed failures

issues.title: A headless or nested provider session is not the worker: its end never hands over the task or writes a tracked record
issues.objective: The lifecycle tells a provider session that is the worker apart from one the worker spawned, for example a headless `claude -p` run by an adopter's review script inside a supervised worktree, or a session started under another live session of the same checkout. A start event from such a session opens at most a local episode bound to nothing; it never adopts the checkout's active task. Its end event, interrupted or not, never marks the active task handed_over and never writes a tracked record under .ai/repo/sessions/; anything it keeps stays under .ai/local. The distinction is read from what the provider's payload and environment actually say (the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID column of MJ_CAPTURE_LIFECYCLE, the start source, whether a live episode of another provider session already holds the task), and the rule is stated where the lifecycle is declared.
issues.why: Reported by the prismatic-platform adopter session on 0.30.0, 2026-10-19. A headless `claude -p` subprocess launched by a review script inside a supervised worktree bound to that worktree's active task (session s-20261019062312-c137, task t-20261018225527-077f). When it was killed mid-run, its SessionEnd hook did two things. (1) It wrote a TRACKED record .ai/repo/sessions/20261019T062345Z--s-20261019062312-c137--...--3bb1e48--867c75fadb2a05ec.md with outcome: interrupted, which dirtied the tree and blocked the adopter's push gate. (2) It marked the active task outcome: handed_over, so the real worker's next `finish --check` answered 'already handed_over' and the worker had to start again. Normal completions wrote nothing; the trigger is the interrupted end. The stray record is kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-korczis-dev-prismatic-platform/031be0ea-45bf-41ce-84e5-d7b951d35331/scratchpad/stray-session-records/.
issues.current_state: mj_capture_session_start opens an episode for any provider session that fires SessionStart in the checkout. mj_capture_session_end runs `handover --derive --close` against the checkout's current task and closes the episode into a tracked record, whoever the session was.
issues.desired_state: A session that is not the worker leaves the worker's task and the tracked tree exactly as they were, and says so in its local log. The worker's own interrupted end keeps today's behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: With a worker episode open on an active task, a second provider session's start then interrupted end leaves the task's outcome unchanged (not handed_over) and git status clean under .ai/repo/sessions/
The same second session's end writes its record, if any, under .ai/local only, and the worker's own end afterwards closes the worker's episode as before
A worker's own interrupted end (no other live session) still hands the task over and writes its tracked record, as case 54 holds today
Case 3461 drives all three through the shims the provider runs

issues.title: release.currency measures the landed work past the last release, and the brief and doctor say when it waits
issues.objective: Declare release.currency with capability! in the release module. It answers the last release (the release record the layer holds, or the newest v* tag the trunk contains when that tag is newer), the landed commits on the trunk past it (release commits and merges left out), when the oldest of them landed, and the version the public contract requires for them (release::version::select), decided only from a recorded release in a checkout at the trunk. The stance is current when nothing has landed past the release, owed when work has, and overdue once the oldest of it has waited longer than six hours, the threshold stated beside its declaration. The brief shows a release line and section, doctor warns on owed and on overdue, and project.land-and-publish names case 3470 as its proof. It is a runtime read only and never enters committed site data.
issues.why: The owner wants a new measured version after every session and milestone, enforced. The cooperation model's rule that the release seat releases whenever master holds landed work past the last tag is measured nowhere. Master held landed work past v0.30.0 for hours while every surface stayed green.
issues.current_state: release.version reports the last release and the commits since it as evidence, and says nothing about how long they have waited. Nothing in the brief, doctor or finish asks.
issues.desired_state: A session's brief and doctor say how much landed work waits for a release, since when and at which version. The release seat can see the debt without reading git.
acceptance_criteria: In a repository with a release record and commits landed after it, release.currency names the release, the landed commits past it without the bump and record commits, the oldest one's landing time and the required version; with nothing landed past it, it says current
The brief has a release line saying owed or overdue with the count and the age, and doctor warns accordingly
A pushed v* tag newer than the last record counts as the last release

The oldest landing is dated by when this clone's remote-tracking trunk first held it, from that ref's reflog, so a top composed hours before it landed waits from its landing; where the reflog does not show it arrive, its commit time bounds the wait from above, the answer says so, and that bound alone never makes the stance overdue (the plan critique of 2026-10-19)

issues.title: A task holding the release seat does not finish completed while landed work has waited past the threshold
issues.objective: Add a doctrine of its own, enforced by finish with its own validator, policy key and wording, that reads release.currency. It refuses the outcome completed only to the release seat's task. A task is the seat's when a live exclusive claim matching release/seat is held by a mesh session whose provider session is the task's own. The join is derived, never declared. The MCP bridge reads the provider session from the variables the lifecycle adapters declare and hands it to the server at initialize. The board projection carries a digest of it into the mesh session record as provider_session, and start records the same digest in the task record, so no raw session id leaves the machine. Before the field ships, a test shows that an event's signature covers the bytes received, so that a runtime that does not know the field still verifies the event. The seat's task is refused completed when release.currency says overdue, and when the measurement is unknown, naming the count, the wait and the version or why none was decided. A pushed v* tag counts as released only while scripts/ci/release-check reads its run as queued or running, or once that run has succeeded. A failed run, or none past release-check's grace, refuses the seat, and a forge that cannot be read is reported, never counted. Every other finish is told the stance and who holds release/seat, its session and machine, or that the seat is vacant, and is never refused by it. A measurement or seat that cannot be read refuses no other task. A task whose provider session differs from the seat holder's, such as a new session that resumed the seat's handover, is told that release/seat is held by another provider session, so the seat sees why its work was not gated. A task started with no observable provider session is never the seat's. Case 3472 proves each of these, and the intent's criterion the-seat-releases names it instead of case 3470.
issues.why: Rule 4 of the cooperation model binds the release seat. A seat that ends its session with overdue landed work leaves the owner's order unmet, with every check green. The plan critique of 2026-10-19 found that nothing joins a finishing task to the seat (a task's own claim is advisory and holds no seat), and that a gate copied into publication-currency's shape would refuse every task on an unknown measurement and name the published site as the cause. The join was agreed with the release seat on 2026-10-21. A seat held by each release task would show the seat vacant between tasks and invite a second session to take it, and a seat claim that carried a task id would go silent whenever its holder forgot to claim it again. Claude Code exports its session id to the Bash tool and to every MCP process it starts, so the session that holds the seat and the task that finishes can be told apart, or matched, without anyone declaring it.
issues.current_state: finish asks publication-currency about the site and nothing about the release. No task record names its provider session, and no mesh session record carries one.
issues.desired_state: The release seat's finish says completed only when the trunk's landed work is released, still inside the threshold, or being released by a run the release check reads as alive. The seat's task is found by its provider session, and every other finish names the stance and the seat's holder.
acceptance_criteria: A task is the seat's exactly when a live exclusive claim matching release/seat is held by a mesh session whose provider_session digest equals the one start recorded for the task, and nobody declares it
The seat's task is refused completed when release.currency says overdue, naming the count, the wait and the version or the reason none was decided, and when the measurement is unknown

The same task finishes when its tag's run is queued or running by release-check's reading, or has succeeded, and when nothing has landed past the release; a failed run, or none past the grace, refuses it

A task that is not the seat's is told the stance and who holds release/seat, and is never refused by this gate, including when release.currency or the mesh cannot be read; one whose provider session differs from the holder's is told the seat is held by another provider session, and one started with none is never the seat's
The provider_session field replicates to a runtime that does not know it, and that runtime still verifies the event

On 2026-10-18 f6 settled the overlap on the mesh: I2965, which qualifies the site's proof words by their verdict, lands first, and the count qualification f6 had staged as I2970 is carried here instead. issues.title: check and finish count the refusals later overridden and the completions later reverted, per rule and per release
non_scope: Deciding which refusals were wrong (reported as candidates)
issues.objective: From the ledger, derive two rates per rule and per release. Candidate false refusals: a refusal followed by an override, or a later finish of the same task with no relevant change. Candidate false acceptances: a completed finish whose commits are reverted, or whose issue reopens, within a window. Publish both with denominator, window and provenance.
issues.why: The owner's audits of 2026-10-13 (c256#2) and 2026-10-14 (c262#10) named false refusal as a critical class of bug, because a tool that refuses correct work gets bypassed. The second adopter met a personal-mode bootstrap that update later refused. Neither rate is measured. It extends milestone cost-per-accepted-outcome. Proposed in ADR 0208 (The product's value is stated as the false dones its finish caught, beside the friction it cost) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c256#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c256#5, chatgpt-majordomus:c262#10.
issues.current_state: The ledger records finish outcomes and refusals. Nothing joins them over time.
issues.desired_state: Two derived measures, never typed, on the economics or evidence view.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture ledger with an overridden refusal and a reverted completion yields one of each
Each rate carries its denominator and window

issues.title: A refusal answered by no change to the tree is not counted as a caught false done
non_scope: Deciding why a refusal was wrong
issues.objective: Record on task.refused and task.finished an answer digest over every input a refusing doctrine reads (the tree id from mj_worktree_tree_id, already written as verify.tree, the completion note's content, the verify command and the obligation evidence), and have the aggregate classify a refusal as unanswered only when none of the inputs its own doctrine reads changed before acceptance, and as downgraded when the accepted outcome is lower than the refused one.
issues.why: The 2026-10-14 assessment named false refusal a critical bug class, because a governance tool that refuses correct work gets bypassed; counting such refusals as value would inflate the very metric meant to be honest. On 2026-10-18 the ledgers of every checkout `git worktree list` reported held 129 task.refused lines, 95 of them refused by majordomus.note-integrity alone (recount: `git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2}' | while read w; do cat \"$w/.ai/local/state/ledger.jsonl\" 2>/dev/null; done | grep -c '\"event\":\"task.refused\"'`); a note-integrity refusal is answered in the gitignored completion note, which a tree-only digest never sees. The tree id is reused at the cost of one temporary-index `git add -A` per refusal. Proposed in ADR 0208 (The product's value is stated as the false dones its finish caught, beside the friction it cost) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c262#10.

issues.desired_state: Both events carry the answer digest; the aggregate separates caught, unanswered, downgraded and digest unknown by the doctrine-to-input map derived from the doctrine declarations; a case holds it.
acceptance_criteria: A task refused and then accepted with no input its refusing doctrine reads changed is reported unanswered, not caught
A task refused, edited and accepted is reported caught
Ledgers written before the digest existed read 'digest unknown', never caught

Relaying for an untrusted node

Confidentiality is the network's (docs/MESH.md:189), so the relay inherits case 491's private-hub rule. This issue waits for it, and the next planner adds depends_on I2825 once its record exists. Proposed in ADR 0202 (The mesh routes work to an identity, never an address, and selects among proven transports instead of implementing NAT traversal) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). issues.title: An operation started from /ui/mesh is authorised, executed, audited and its result streamed back
non_scope: Natural-language operations
Self-update from the UI before I2722
The action button, its journal-rendered result and the disabled snapshot rendering already delivered by I3139
An audit kept only in the in-memory ExecutionStore
issues.objective: First propose the ADR amending ADR 0126 that decides which credential admits a remote write and how a mesh event names its human author; then take the one mesh action I3139 offers on /ui/mesh through executions.start, authorise it by the caller's identity and the capability's declared effect, record its audit as the signed mesh journal event the write produces (author, operation, policy, result, evidence), stream the result to the page, and refuse it from an unauthenticated remote caller.
issues.why: The 10-18 Lumen critique: do not defer identity, authorisation, typed commands, freshness and reconnect; one authorised action end to end is v0.1. The 10-08 pack asked for a self-update with rollback from the UI; that is the same path with a riskier effect. Critique 10-18: ExecutionStore is in-memory and bounded, and the shared server stops when idle, so an execution cannot be the audit. ADR 0126 leaves open who may write remotely and how a mesh event names its human author, and this issue's first step is the ADR that decides both. I3139 (prismatic-lumen) is the same action, so this issue builds on it rather than beside it. Proposed in ADR 0201 (The persistent runtime is the authority; every operator surface, Lumen included, is a client of it) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c296#12, chatgpt-majordomus:c200#5.

acceptance_criteria: The action is refused without authentication from beyond loopback

issues.title: The lundra hub is a declared deployment target served over its tailnet name, and a second device reaches it
non_scope: Tailscale Funnel (public)
Any write through the ingress before web-sign-in
Widening deploy.check to reach the network; it stays a read over the local index
A host-level resident or a mesh presence beside the repository's server
A public ingress (a tunnel hostname): a later phase, outside this intent
issues.objective: Declare the hub as a deployment target whose listeners are declared separately (the mesh rendezvous port answering only the signed link and register routes; the UI/API/MCP origin on loopback behind a tailnet HTTPS ingress set up through the installed Tailscale CLI), run it as the user-scoped unit I2722 writes, prove reachability from a second authorised device with served observe extended to a named deployment target plus an off-tailnet negative probe, and commit each run as the target's evidence.
issues.why: Owner 2026-09-11: Tailscale domain now, majordomus.dev later, fully functional; 09-15: the default backend is lundra over Tailscale. Public CI must not join the tailnet, so the acceptance is a canonical command whose evidence is recorded. Critique 10-18: lundra is the mesh rendezvous hub on 0.0.0.0:8791 (docs/MESH.md). Moving the origin to loopback without splitting listeners would cut every peer off, and leaving it on 0.0.0.0 means the UI/API/MCP are already served in plain HTTP beyond the tailnet. deploy.check takes no input and contacts nothing (deploy.rs), so the network-reaching proof is served.observe, which is already CLI-only and records what it saw. It absorbs I3186, which once narrowed to ADR 0199 was this target's service; The tunnel hostname target is dropped from this plan as a later public phase. Proposed in ADR 0204 (The hub is reached privately over the tailnet first; a public ingress is a deployment target, never an application change) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c118#9, chatgpt-majordomus:c240#2.
issues.current_state: Verified: the hub runs `serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8791 --idle 0` under a hand-made systemd user unit (docs/MESH.md), so its UI, API and MCP answer in plain HTTP on every interface; no deployment object describes it; deploy.check takes no input and contacts nothing (capability/builtin/deploy.rs), and served observe is the CLI-only probe that reaches the network.
issues.desired_state: A deployment object for the hub with its listeners; served observe probes the named target positively from a tailnet device and negatively from outside it; deploy.check stays a read.
acceptance_criteria: A second device reaches /ui and MCP over the tailnet name
A second deploy of the same configuration changes nothing

The hub target declares its listeners separately: the mesh rendezvous port, which answers only the signed link hello/sync and register routes, and the UI/API/MCP origin on loopback behind the tailnet ingress

issues.title: The trunk's protection is compared with the CI model, and a drift is a finding that names the change
non_scope: Changing the protection from the tool
Reading the forge from doctor
issues.objective: Declare the aggregate verdict check once in .ai/repo/ci/gates.yaml, then compare the required checks the last forge observation read for master with it, and report a missing, extra or unread requirement as a finding with the idempotent gh command that would fix it, from the recorded observation and without reaching the network; scripts/ci/release-verdict reads the same declaration.

Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c112#3, chatgpt-majordomus:c113#10, chatgpt-majordomus:c130#10, chatgpt-majordomus:c295#3, chatgpt-majordomus:c112#2.

issues.title: A publication never replaces the site with a build of an older commit than the one gh-pages serves
non_scope: Changing pages.yml concurrency
A second deploy path
Applying the commit guard to the --release-metadata path
issues.objective: Make scripts/site-deploy refuse to push a build whose source commit is a strict ancestor of the commit gh-pages:build.json records (the served build, the source pages.yml already reads), the way it already refuses an older release, so a delayed run or a manual deploy from a stale checkout cannot overwrite a newer site; --release-metadata stays exempt because it leaves build.json unchanged.
issues.why: The 2026-10-17 release pack asked that a stale Pages build never overwrite a newer snapshot (c291#2). The site-deploy guard compares releases and that HEAD is on origin/master, but two masters can both be on origin/master and the older one can publish last. Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c291#2.
issues.current_state: scripts/site-deploy refuses a HEAD not on origin/master and a build whose release is older than the served one (ADR 0131). A build commit's message records 'source: <sha>', but --release-metadata commits 'source: <release job's HEAD> with the record of <tag>' onto gh-pages without rebuilding, so the head commit's source line can name an older commit than the build it serves. pages.yml reads the served commit from origin/gh-pages:build.json and serialises runs per ref with cancel-in-progress: false. No check compares the served build's commit with HEAD.
issues.desired_state: site-deploy reads the served commit from gh-pages:build.json and refuses a build when HEAD is its strict ancestor, with --any-ref the only override; --release-metadata keeps only its release-version guard; scripts/pages reports the publication's freshness with the same predicate.
acceptance_criteria: Deploying commit A after gh-pages already records its descendant B is refused with both commits named
Deploying B over A, and redeploying the commit gh-pages already records, both proceed
A gh-pages head that records no source commit is unknown and is reported, not treated as older
The served source commit is read from gh-pages:build.json's commit, the source pages.yml already reads, never from the gh-pages head commit's 'source:' line
--release-metadata is exempt from the commit guard and says so: it leaves build.json unchanged (I2303, ADR 0131), and only its release-version guard applies

A case publishes build A, then a metadata commit naming an older HEAD, then attempts an older build: the older build is refused against A, a descendant build proceeds, and the metadata publication itself is never refused by the commit guard
After a deploy lands, scripts/pages reports the served build.json commit with the same predicate, so the publication is observed rather than assumed

issues.title: CI timings measure the wait before a run starts beside the run, and count what cancelled runs spent
non_scope: Changing what CI runs
Publishing a target before it is measured
A persisted history of runs beyond the window one refresh reads
issues.objective: Read the Actions workflow-runs and jobs API over a declared window in prs refresh, so integration.timings gives each run its queue time (created to started) beside its execution time (started to completed) and tallies the runner minutes of cancelled and superseded runs, and the one-at-a-time pool's wait is measured instead of inferred.
issues.why: Audits read validate wall times of 59-98 minutes on 2026-10-10 and 90-115 minutes on 2026-10-15..17, and 41 of 67 validate runs on 2026-10-11 cancelled (c199#14); a 2026-10-13 proposal asked that queue time, execution time and wasted minutes be told apart (c255#7). Those were timestamp readings by a reviewer, not repository measurements. Proposed in ADR 0196 (Delivery latency targets are budgets of benchmark policy, measured per phase, and never a correctness gate on runners the repository does not own) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c199#14, chatgpt-majordomus:c255#7.
issues.current_state: apps/majordomus-cli/src/integration/timings.rs measures completed_at - started_at of an open pull request's head checks and counts queued runs without measuring them (I2472 DONE). The forge observation (forge.rs) reads statusCheckRollup CheckRun{name status conclusion startedAt completedAt} for the current heads of open pull requests only: it holds no created or queued time, no run of a superseded head and no run of a merged pull request. The /ui CI/CD & Releases screen (ui/timings.rs, ui/delivery.rs) draws integration.timings.
issues.desired_state: integration.timings reports per run: queued, started, completed, queue seconds, run seconds, conclusion; per window: p50/p95 of each, cancelled and superseded run minutes, sample size and observation time. A run still queued is pending, never zero.
acceptance_criteria: A three-run fixture yields the stated queue and run seconds for each run
A cancelled run's minutes are counted as spent and its conclusion stays cancelled
Re-reading the same observation creates no duplicate rows

Queue and run times come from the Actions workflow-runs and jobs API (created_at, run_started_at, updated_at, status, conclusion, run_attempt, head_sha), read by prs refresh with pagination over a declared window, never from statusCheckRollup
The window is written into the existing forge observation, which each refresh replaces; no other file or store holds runs
A run is identified by run id and attempt: reading the same window twice counts each run once
A run is superseded when its head_sha is no longer its branch's head; its minutes are counted as spent
The /ui CI/CD & Releases screen renders the new reading's shape, and a case or test holds the screen to it

issues.title: Delivery lead time is measured per phase, from a pull request's opening to its verified publication
non_scope: A second metrics store
Forecasts or scores
A delivery or throughput figure as ADR 0198 (proposed, not on master) defines it; this issue measures lead time only
Publishing lead-time readings to majordomus.dev before a measured window exists
Depending on I2946 (board, not on master); it remains an overlap only
issues.objective: Time the phases of the delivery stages plan.delivery derives per issue (I2740: pr_open, merged, released, deployed, each with the object that proved it) and report p50/p95, sample size and observation time per phase, taking a merged pull request's opened and merged times from the forge's pull request record so merges made outside the drain are counted, and writing no join of its own.
issues.why: The owner asked for minutes, not hours or days, between a change and its deploy (c204#0) and later for releases as fast as possible (c291#0); every audit since 2026-10-09 reconstructed lead time by hand from run timestamps (c204#2, c238#2, c295#7). No single figure for green pull request to verified deploy exists. Proposed in ADR 0196 (Delivery latency targets are budgets of benchmark policy, measured per phase, and never a correctness gate on runners the repository does not own); ADR 0198 (Delivery is judged by verified outcomes landed per day, with lead time p95 as its control, never by commits, pull requests or sessions) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c204#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c216#6, chatgpt-majordomus:c238#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c280#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c287#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c295#7.
issues.current_state: integration.events holds the drain's own trail only: no opened time, and no merge made by a person or an expedited landing. I2474 (DONE) draws merges per day; served.observe records what each deployment served; release records under .ai/repo/releases carry their commits. I2740 (master, READY, p0) plans plan.delivery's stages none, branch, pr_open, merged, released and deployed with their proving objects (ADR 0166). I2946 (on the board on 2026-10-18, not on master) measures throughput from prs and ci-timings. Nothing times the phases.
issues.desired_state: A delivery lead-time reading, computed only from recorded sources, with unmeasured phases shown as unmeasured; drawn on the drain screen and served by CLI, HTTP and MCP from the same capability.
acceptance_criteria: Each phase's p50 and p95 come with their sample size and the moment they were observed
A change whose publication was never observed is counted as unmeasured, never as zero
CLI JSON, HTTP and MCP return the same reading for the same inputs
The stages (pr_open, merged, released, deployed) and the objects that prove them are read from plan.delivery (I2740); this issue adds only per-phase timing over them and writes no join of its own

The opened and merged times of a merged pull request come from the forge's pull request record (createdAt, mergedAt) and its merge commit, including merges made outside the drain; a merge whose opening cannot be read is counted as unmeasured with its count reported, never dropped silently

issues.title: The backlog's bound is declared once in policy, and every session brief says when the landable backlog is past it
non_scope: Refusing new work (an open question to the owner)
Querying the forge at session start
issues.objective: Move the landable-backlog threshold from the MJ_BACKLOG_MAX default in scripts/ci/backlog-check into .ai/repo/policy.yaml, read it in both backlog-check and the session brief, and have the brief's integration section say 'past the bound' from the last recorded observation, without a network call and without refusing anything.
issues.why: The owner's repeated demand was that pull requests be processed, not accumulate (c209#0, c220#0); on 2026-09-11 the review asked for one typed policy source for staleness and age thresholds and a cached entry warning (c112#3). Rule project.accumulation-is-measured asks for a threshold that makes growth loud; today the threshold is an environment default of one script. Proposed in ADR 0197 (The backlog is bounded by a declared bound that every session reads at start, and the bound reports rather than refuses) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c112#3.
issues.current_state: scripts/ci/backlog-check --remote measures the landable backlog against MJ_BACKLOG_MAX (default 10); the brief (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/brief.rs) reports prs brief without any bound; .ai/repo/policy.yaml declares release.floor but no integration bound. The session-start context does not pass through brief.rs: lib/context.sh mj_context_integration calls prs brief and writes no section for a checkout that never observed the forge.
issues.desired_state: policy.yaml declares integration.backlog_max (and the age after which a ready pull request is starving); backlog-check and the brief read it; the brief line reads 'N landable, bound M: past the bound' when exceeded. Rule project.blocking-checks-cheap holds: it is reported, never a refusal.
acceptance_criteria: The bound appears in exactly one canonical file and both readers name it
A recorded observation over the bound makes the brief say so; under it the brief says nothing extra
A checkout that never observed the forge says the backlog is unobserved, not zero

The session-start context (lib/context.sh mj_context_integration) writes 'backlog unobserved' for a checkout that never observed the forge when policy declares integration.backlog_max, and writes nothing when no bound is declared, keeping its rule that a repository which does not integrate pull requests grows no section
The context line and the brief line are the same text, produced by prs brief

issues.title: A pull request's change is split into canonical, derived and incidental paths, and the drain shows each
non_scope: Changing what is derived
Ranking by the counts (a later decision)
issues.objective: Classify every path a pull request changes as a canonical input, a derived projection (what .gitattributes merge=derived and the generators declare) or incidental, carry the counts on the queue's assessment, and report change amplification: how many derived files one canonical change rewrote.
issues.why: On 2026-10-10 large pull requests (#807 with 706 files, #292 with 499) were unreviewable and mergeable=false dominated (c207#6); the same day another review asked how many files of a pull request are canonical versus generated, and how many open pull requests rewrite the same outputs (c216#6). It supports delivery-is-measured-per-phase and serves no criterion of the intent. Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c207#6, chatgpt-majordomus:c216#6.
issues.current_state: The integration model knows a pull request's changed paths and the derived merge driver knows derived files (.gitattributes, test/cases/57_derived_merge_driver.sh); nothing classifies a pull request's paths or measures amplification.
issues.desired_state: integration.queue and integration.explain carry canonical, derived and incidental counts per pull request, derived from the declarations already in the tree; the drain screen shows them; a pull request whose only canonical change is a record is told apart from a code change.
acceptance_criteria: The derived set is read from the tree's own declarations; no path list is written in the code
A fixture pull request that changes one canonical file and its projections reports 1 canonical and N derived
The counts are the same on CLI JSON, HTTP and MCP

issues.title: The delivery phases have budgets in benchmark policy, and a phase over its budget is a finding with its trend
non_scope: Weakening any gate to meet a budget
Choosing the numbers (ADR proposed: delivery latency targets are budgets)
issues.objective: Once I3202 and I3203 measure the phases, declare each phase's budget beside the UI budgets bench --check already holds, report a phase over budget as a finding with its last window's trend, and keep wall time a report rather than a correctness gate where the runner is not ours.

A goal with no budget in policy is not enforced; a budget on a shared runner pool cannot be a red gate without becoming flaky. Proposed in ADR 0196 (Delivery latency targets are budgets of benchmark policy, measured per phase, and never a correctness gate on runners the repository does not own) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c204#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c287#2.
issues.current_state: I2489 (DONE) made the UI's latency budgets benchmark policy held by bench --check; .ai/repo/ci/suite.yaml and structure-durations.tsv bound the suite; no delivery phase has a declared budget.
issues.desired_state: Benchmark policy carries a budget per delivery phase with its source (owner goal or measured baseline); the reading marks each phase within or over; over-budget phases surface on the drain screen and in the brief; nothing turns the ci verdict red on GitHub wall time.
acceptance_criteria: Each phase budget names where its number came from
A phase over budget is a finding with the window and sample it was read from
No required check depends on runner wall time

issues.title: A finished task names the pull request that carries its branch and that pull request's disposition
non_scope: Opening or pushing from finish
Refusing finish on a disposition
issues.objective: Make majordomus finish report, from the last recorded queue observation, the pull request whose head is the task's branch, its disposition and next action, or that no pull request carries the branch yet, so the work a worker hands to the landing seat is named at the moment it is handed.

issues.current_state: lib/finish.sh judges the task's own scope, obligations and verification and says nothing of pull requests; integration.queue knows each open pull request's head branch and disposition.
issues.desired_state: finish prints one line 'pull request #N: <disposition>, next: <action>' or 'no pull request carries <branch>; push it and open one', read from the recorded observation with its age, never from the network; the handover body carries the same line.
acceptance_criteria: A task whose branch heads an observed pull request names it with its disposition and the observation's age
A task whose branch no pull request carries says so
A checkout with no observation says the queue is unobserved

issues.title: Whether a commit may be released is one read that names each condition and the evidence that settles it
non_scope: Tagging or publishing
A second release engine; the read composes what exists
Starting before the alpha top (0.30.0) and I2829 land on release.yml and scripts/site-deploy
issues.objective: Add release.readiness to the release capability: for a commit and a candidate version, decide what release.yml's plan and verdict phases, the version gate and the base branch's ci verdict decide, and answer ready, not ready with the failing condition, or unknown with what could not be read, including the surface fingerprint the record will publish; release.yml's plan and verdict phases then call it, so one implementation decides both. The install job is the after-tag half and is named as not readable before a tag.
issues.why: The owner set the alpha for 2026-10-19 with GO only on current master, green CI and real install tests, not an automatic GO (c281#2). Audits asked for a single derived readiness authority shown on CLI, UI and Pages (c283#2) and a machine-evaluated definition of done for a stage (c258#2). Today each condition lives in a different script and is first combined when a tag is pushed. Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c111#6, chatgpt-majordomus:c238#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c258#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c283#2, chatgpt-majordomus:c089#1.

issues.desired_state: majordomus release readiness <sha> (and its HTTP and MCP projections) returns each condition with its evidence and age, read from the same functions the release path runs, so the workflow and the read cannot disagree; a condition that cannot be read is unknown and the answer is not ready.

A candidate version below what the contract requires is not ready and both versions are named
The read and the release workflow's plan and verdict phases share their implementation

release.yml's plan and verdict phases call majordomus release readiness, and scripts/release-version --check and scripts/ci/release-verdict become thin callers of it; no condition is implemented twice
The install job is the after-tag half of the proof: readiness names it as not readable before a tag and never reports it as passed
The trunk's red state is the ci verdict of the base branch's head, read by the same function as the candidate commit's verdict; I2709's carrier is not a readiness condition
The release screen under /ui shows the readiness read from the same capability

issues.title: An intent proposed or an issue moved by any client reaches an open intent workspace without a reload

issues.title: A vendor workspace reads the plan through the authenticated remote MCP surface, and a tunnel never makes it look local

The Claude in Chrome side panel is the same case: it is an agent on claude.ai and reaches only a connector Anthropic's cloud can call over the public internet (support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166), so it cannot reach the loopback server either (docs/MCP.md#claude-in-the-browser, 2026-10-21).
