A protocol has version, registered_at, changes and a decision of one of three kinds: paired (names an economics suite and the digest of that suite's registration block), trials (record fields with their classes, min_trials, min_successes, all_must_pass) or window (period, admitted work, a bound per field on its not-observed share). Each protocol carries registered_digest over its own canonical form, computed by one public digest function the suite registration also uses. The validator refuses a digest mismatch, an unknown dimension or decision kind, a duplicate id, a claim CLAIMS.yaml lacks, a paired protocol whose suite or registration digest does not resolve, and a version without a changes entry. Expose counts_toward(record, test): a record counts only when it carries its test's protocol digest and postdates registered_at. The plan file is a freshness input of no suite.
issues.why: The owner's report of 2026-10-19 asks that T1 to T6 be decided by measurement, and T2 that the split be fixed in advance. The critique of this plan showed that putting one shared plan file into every suite's freshness inputs would stale the T2 corpus whenever T4 or T5 registered later, so each protocol is frozen by its own digest and records carry it. A paired protocol references the suite's own registration block, so pre-registration exists once.

issues.title: Where the work is is cached by what it reads, and a warm roadmap does not walk the trunk
non_scope: Making delivery::infer itself faster (an incremental history read); this record removes repeated work, not the first.
Caching the mesh claims, which stay live.

issues.objective: plan.flight keeps its delivery inference under a key made of what it reads (the trunk's commit, the refs, the plan's records, the release records and the forge and deployment observations) and recomputes it only when that key changes, with the live mesh claims laid over the cached part on every call; a warm /ui/roadmap then answers without walking the trunk's history.
issues.why: On 2026-10-19 the owner asked that /roadmap be correct and connected. Review finding U4: plan.flight is declared CachePolicy::Disabled, the readings layer revalidates a source after one second, and delivery::infer runs over the whole trunk history behind every warm view (the review measured 4.5 to 14 s). The work starts only after the exclusive mesh claim another session holds on apps/majordomus-cli/src/plan/flight.rs, apps/majordomus-cli/src/ui/roadmap.rs and apps/majordomus-cli/tests/ui_roadmap.rs is released or handed over.
issues.current_state: plan.flight is declared with cache: CachePolicy::Disabled (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/plan.rs:712-727), as plan.delivery is (plan.rs:696-711). Its handler (plan.rs:861-896) calls flight::observe, which runs delivery::infer over the trunk on every call (apps/majordomus-cli/src/plan/flight.rs:518-525); infer reads the whole history with one git log of the trunk (apps/majordomus-cli/src/plan/delivery.rs:860-895, history_of at delivery.rs:610-622), then the branches, the forge observation, the release records and the deployment observation (published_live, delivery.rs:676-699). On 2026-10-19 one plan delivery at origin/master 9904000d2df took 7.3 s wall clock at a load average of 45, reading 1723 merge commits and 2841 other commits. The Overview does not read plan.flight at all because it is too slow for a first paint (apps/majordomus-cli/src/ui/dashboard.rs:137-139). CachePolicy::Checkout (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/model.rs:350-359) fingerprints HEAD, the index, the refs and the work tree but no other process and no ignored file, so it cannot hold the mesh claims or the observations under .ai/local.

The capability's declaration states the policy, the executor's counters show a warm call that ran no git log, and a test proves an answer equal to an uncached one after each input moves.
acceptance_criteria: A second plan.flight call with no input changed runs no git log of the trunk (the executor's counters or a git-invocation counter in the test say so) and returns an answer equal to the first

issues.title: A claim released on a runtime that is not replicating reaches every linked runtime, or the release is refused
non_scope: Releasing another runtime's claim, which stays refused as not_own

issues.objective: Make a claim release either reach every linked runtime or be refused: (a) mesh.release (MCP majordomus_mesh_release, POST /api/v1/mesh/claims/release) refuses with not_active, naming the reason, when the runtime that holds the claim's stream is not replicating, instead of answering with a written event that no linked runtime will ever see; and (b) a journal written while the runtime was not replicating is caught up by every linked runtime once replication resumes, so a release already written is folded everywhere.
issues.why: Found on 2026-10-19 while the owner's /ui/roadmap fixes were being claimed. The session that holds the release seat (9c) released claims c-4976f99ae66b, c-5dd3dfe0fda9, c-effc074ec6f2 and c-76d4d93c073e through its server on 127.0.0.1:8741, and the releases were written there (events 551 and 552 on stream 8241af227eccef89). That server answers GET /api/v1/mesh/state with active: null. The live primary server on 127.0.0.1:51311 (mesh active) still folds the claims as exclusive and held, and does not list stream 8241af227eccef89 among its streams, so an exclusive claim on the same paths stays refused with claim_conflict. The acquisitions had replicated while that mesh was active; the releases never did. The milestone promises that a stale claim never wins, and today it wins indefinitely. 9c and 2b confirmed the defect on the mesh.
issues.current_state: apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mesh.rs:998-1000 mesh_release calls cooperation(ctx)?.release(...); cooperation() at :246-256 refuses only when no Cooperation is running in the process. apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:3596-3612 release checks ownership and existence, then writes ClaimReleased to this runtime's journal. Nothing in either path asks whether the journal is being replicated to linked runtimes, and nothing replays to a linked runtime the events written while replication was off: a release written then stays local to the holder's journal.
issues.desired_state: A release on a runtime that is not replicating is refused as not_active with its reason, or is accepted and provably delivered: when replication resumes, each linked runtime folds every event the holder wrote in between, in order, and a claim released on the holder reads released on every linked runtime. mesh doctor names a runtime that holds live claims while not replicating.
acceptance_criteria: Two linked fixture runtimes: a release written while the holder is replicating reads released on both

issues.title: Two live instances of one runtime slot keep their links, and the mesh names them instead of flapping
non_scope: Stopping either process: which server survives is the lifecycle's and the owner's decision

Two server processes of the primary checkout carry that runtime slot (instances 7eab159b6b89c7c5 and 8241af227eccef89, serving on 55765 and 8741; a dial of 127.0.0.1:8741 is refused self_link: that is this runtime). Every round re-signs a hello and a welcome per link, the reconnect counter no longer tells a dropping link from this, and each peer's view of the runtime alternates between two instances.

On a hello, a different card.instance counts a restart and clears the outbound link, and the old inbound link is dropped. On a welcome after the first, the dialer counts a reconnect. A sync on a dropped link is refused unknown_link and the dialer says hello at once (after_round). I3175 detects one node key on two hosts, not two processes of one runtime on one host.
issues.desired_state: A peer keeps one inbound link per (runtime, instance) while both instances beat within the expiry. Neither instance re-handshakes on a steady link. mesh peers lists the runtime once, with its instances and their endpoints, and mesh doctor fails a check that names both, because one checkout should run one server (runtime-lifecycle). The reconnect counter counts only links that dropped.
acceptance_criteria: Two instances of one runtime that both dial one peer each keep their link for ten heartbeats: zero unknown_link refusals, zero reconnects and zero restarts on either side

issues.title: An open review says how old it is, and lapses when nobody can answer it any more
non_scope: Answering or withdrawing a review on someone's behalf
issues.objective: Give every mesh review its age on every surface that lists it, and lapse an open review whose requesting session has closed or expired, or that has stood unanswered past a declared bound, with the reason recorded, so the open list holds only questions someone can still act on.
issues.why: On 2026-10-20, majordomus_mesh_state kind=reviews open=true listed 20 open reviews, the oldest from 2026-10-17 (r-182b4e75e8df, r-19732de5ba2e, about v0.29.0), none answered. They name releases that have shipped and sessions that are gone, next to one live question (r-2780b7196cce, PR #1748). A reader cannot tell the live one from the dead ones without opening each, which is the stale claim winning, in the review queue.
issues.current_state: A review is open until it is answered or withdrawn. The listing carries no request time, nothing lapses it, and a requester whose session closed leaves its reviews open forever.
issues.desired_state: Each review carries requested_at and its age on mesh state, the brief and /ui/mesh. An open review lapses, recorded as lapsed with its reason, when its requesting session has closed or expired, or when it stands unanswered past the bound declared in the mesh configuration. A lapsed review is still readable and is not counted as open.
acceptance_criteria: Every listed review carries requested_at, and the open list is ordered by it
An open review whose requesting session closed lapses with reason session_closed, on every runtime that holds it

A lapsed review is readable by its key and is not counted as open

issues.title: A claim replayed after a re-attach keeps the time it was made, and an announce answers with the claim it made
non_scope: The mesh journal's own claim times, which are lamport-ordered events
issues.objective: When the MCP bridge replays a client's claims onto the board after a re-attach, carry each claim's original time rather than stamping it now, and make an announce answer with the announcement it just made, not with whichever claim of the peer sorts last.
issues.why: On 2026-10-20 at 20:35Z the board connection of session d3 re-attached, and the bridge replayed its ten claims. Every one came back stamped 20:35:43Z: 'site-probe-split', written at 09:37Z and long superseded, read as the newest work on the board. The same call's announce answer named 'ui-trains' as its announcement although the claim announced was 'mesh-session-findings', because Peer::announcement is the claim with the latest time, every time was equal, and the tie went to the last name. A board that re-dates stale work says nothing true about when anything happened.
issues.current_state: mcp/bridge.rs replays each remembered claim through announce after Bridge::reinitialize. PeerBoard::announce_claim stamps `at` with SystemTime::now(). PeerBoard::latest takes max_by `at`, and among equal times it returns the last in key order.
issues.desired_state: The bridge stamps a claim with made_at when the server first accepts it, a replay or a takeover carries it, and the board keeps a made_at in the past as the claim's `at` (a newer or unparsable one is replaced by now), so a replayed claim is as old as it was. A server older than made_at, which refuses the unknown field, gets the claim again without it rather than not at all. announce answers with the announcement it made, and Peer::announcement breaks ties by the most recent announce call, never by name.
acceptance_criteria: A claim replayed after a re-attach keeps the `at` it was announced with
announce answers with the announcement it made, whatever the peer's other claims are called
Among claims with equal times, Peer::announcement is the one announced last
A made_at in the future or one that does not parse is replaced by now, and a replay that a server refuses for made_at is sent again without it

issues.title: plan.next never names an issue whose delivery is merged or released, and plan.roadmap names that issue with its drift
non_scope: Writing any stamp from inference: a merge is not acceptance (ADR 0166)
Recording I0702 or any other unrecorded issue; that is the record sweep
Changing the readiness derivation in plan.rs or lib/project.awk; statuses stay a function of the records
Live sources (branches, the forge observation, the published site) in the next answer
Which commits count as delivery; I2749 owns that rule
Which milestones are now and next; I3439 derives them once, and the delivered-issue list this issue adds to plan.roadmap names no now or next of its own
issues.objective: Every answer that names the next issue (plan.next, plan.status's next_ready, plan.transition's next_ready and the shell's plan next) comes from one function: the plan.rs ranking of READY issues, each candidate then set against plan.delivery read from the trunk's history and release records only, and a candidate at stage merged, released or deployed passed over and listed with its stage, its proving commit and the remedy (record it with plan start, verify and done). plan.roadmap lists, under each open milestone, the issues of that milestone the history shows delivered while their status is not DONE, so the milestone named as now is read together with its drift.
issues.why: On origin/master 9a5a9b77520 (2026-10-20) plan next answered I0702, whose ADR merged in e59b86b66c9 and was released in v0.28.0; its record was never stamped, so plan roadmap named M002 as now and /plan/ showed I0702 as the next ready issue. The one answer a worker asks for before starting was false, and nothing in the derivation reads delivery. Recording I0702 settles this instance only; the next merge left unrecorded repeats it.
issues.current_state: Verified on origin/master 91c0b5d5658. apps/majordomus-cli/src/plan.rs:562-574 (next_ready, ready_ranked) ranks READY issues by wave, priority and id from the stamps alone. apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/plan.rs:422-445 (plan_next) returns that pick unchanged, :358 (plan_status) and :1241 (plan_transition) repeat it, and the plan.next declaration at :602-617 has no command-line exposure (:612) and caches by index generation (:615). The shell is a second copy: lib/plan.sh:336-350 (mj_plan_next) and lib/project.sh:259-274 (mj_pj_next_ready, mj_pj_ready_ranked) read model.tsv only, and lib/plan.sh:230 and :262 print the same pick in plan status, while lib/plan.sh:66-71 already hands delivery and drift to the executable. Delivery is inferred by apps/majordomus-cli/src/plan/delivery.rs:860 (infer), which already reads the history alone when given a commit. test/cases/99_plan_capabilities.sh:83-86 compares the shell's and the executable's next issue.
issues.desired_state: One function in the capability module picks the next issue: the plan.rs ranking first, then delivery at the trunk head from its history and release records only (no branch, forge or deployment source, so the answer is a function of that commit), skipping every candidate at stage merged, released or deployed. plan.next's output gains passed_over (issue, stage, commit, remedy) and the trunk commit it read; plan.status and plan.transition take next_ready from the same function; plan.next gains the command-line path plan next, and lib/plan.sh hands next to the executable the way it hands delivery and drift, its plan status lines printing the delegated answer. plan.roadmap gains, per open milestone, the delivered issues whose status is open. The cache key includes the trunk commit, so a merge changes the answer without a restart. When the history cannot be read, the answer says delivery was unread and returns the stamp ranking, never silently. plan.rs next_ready and lib/project.awk stay pure, so statuses and waves still agree field for field in case 99.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture whose highest-ranked READY issue is named by a merge on the trunk gets the next-ranked READY issue from plan.next, and passed_over names the first with stage merged and its merge commit
Negative: a READY issue named only by a branch or an open pull request is still handed out; only merged, released or deployed passes an issue over
Negative: a fixture with no delivered issue gets exactly the pick plan.rs ranks, and case 99's next comparison still agrees on its fixture

With a history that cannot be read, the answer names delivery as unread and returns the stamp ranking

issues.objective: When a screen is read as a published snapshot, the plan.flight sources that are unread because of the snapshot itself (the mesh, which no process on a Pages runner activates, and the publication pointer of a deployed commit the CI clone did not fetch) are not drawn as unread notices on /ui/roadmap/ and on every milestone inspector; the screen states once, in plain words, that a snapshot does not observe them and that the live UI does. issues.objective: scripts/lib/site-i18n.mjs cuts every run of digits in a segment's text into a numbered value placeholder that is never translated, so the memory key of a sentence does not change when the count inside it does; scripts/site-translate re-keys the existing memory to that form without losing an admitted translation; the build publishes each copy's untranslated share per route in /<lang>/i18n.json; and scripts/site-check prints that share for every language and refuses a homepage copy with any untranslated segment.

issues.title: The Pages run of a release head publishes with fresh evidence, or publishes the site with the evidence lag stated, and never fails on a missing snapshot artifact
non_scope: The baseline of published-evidence, which may only fall
Keeping pre-release metadata across deploys, which I3448 owns
Moving publication to the Pages artifact model, which I2660 owns
Making validate faster
issues.objective: Make the Pages run of a master head whose own validation has not recorded its evidence end in one of two stated outcomes: it publishes with that head's evidence once validate's evidence job has recorded it, or it publishes the site now with the UI snapshot's evidence lag stated (the commit the evidence was recorded at, how many commits and changed files behind, and that a later run replaces it). A refused UI snapshot never leaves the deploy job failing on a missing artifact and the whole site unpublished.
issues.why: Found on 2026-10-20 at the v1.0.0-alpha.1 head 9a5a9b77520 (roadmap audit finding F10): Pages run 39438897759 failed in ui-snapshot, 'pages evidence: stale: recorded against 82ac259d0ae7, 3 commit(s) and 18 changed file(s) behind', and the deploy job then failed with 'Artifact not found for name: ui-snapshot'. The earlier push run 39392245576 failed as well. The live site stayed at the previous hand deploy, so /roadmap/ and the homepage lagged master while every check of the head was still running. A release head is the commit whose validation is always in flight when Pages first runs, so this happens on every release unless the run waits or states its lag.
issues.current_state: Verified on origin/master 91c0b5d5658. .github/workflows/pages.yml:277-279 runs the ui-snapshot job on every push; its step at :336-341 runs scripts/pages evidence --ledger-out and then scripts/pages published-evidence, and the comment at :329-335 says that while the head's validation is still going the nearest validated ancestor's ledger is used and validate's evidence job dispatches Pages again when it finishes. scripts/pages:781 cmd_evidence labels an ancestor's run stale (:906-907) and, per its comment at :773, is never a gate; but cmd_published_evidence (scripts/pages:1578) exits 10 at :1619 when more claims would read not run than .ai/repo/evidence/published-not-run.txt allows (0), which a stale ledger readily exceeds, so the job fails. The deploy job (.github/workflows/pages.yml:399-401) needs ui-snapshot but runs when only rustdoc succeeded, and its download of the ui-snapshot artifact at :495-498 then fails, so nothing is published. I2853 (test-evidence, merged) excuses only claims whose test is newer than the ledger; it does not address an old ledger on a fresh head.
issues.desired_state: When published-evidence refuses because the ledger is an ancestor's, the ui-snapshot job ends with a declared outcome (deferred, with the commit, distance and reason) instead of a failure; the deploy job reads that outcome and either publishes the site with the last published /ui and /cockpit kept as they are, or with the new snapshot carrying a visible lag line, and in both cases writes the lag into the run summary and the publication state. The dispatch from validate's evidence job then republishes with current evidence. The deploy job never downloads an artifact the ui-snapshot job did not upload. Which of the two snapshot behaviours holds is declared once in .ai/repo/ci/pages.yaml and stated in docs/GITHUB_PAGES_ARCHITECTURE.md.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture run whose ledger was recorded at an ancestor three commits back: the ui-snapshot step ends deferred naming that commit and the distance, the deploy publishes the rest of the site, and the summary states the lag
Negative: a fixture whose ledger is the head's own and within the baseline is published as current, with no lag line
Negative: a ledger of the head itself that is over the baseline still refuses the UI, so the change hides no real not-run claim
The deploy job never reaches a download of an artifact that was not uploaded: a workflow structure check over pages.yml refuses that wiring
The next release head after this lands is published within one Pages run of its push, and the run after validate's evidence dispatch reads current

issues.title: A server that lost its checkout lease answers every mesh read by naming the server that holds it, never with an empty mesh
non_scope: Moving the attached client to the holder automatically
Stopping either server, or deciding which of two servers of one checkout should hold the lease
The health report's own wording beyond adding the holder
issues.objective: Make a shared server that has retired from the mesh because another process took its checkout lease answer mesh.status, mesh.state, mesh.cooperation and mesh.peers, and every refusal of a cooperation write, with the lease holder it can read: that holder's pid and URL, the time this server lost the lease, and the remedy (reconnect the client, or read the mesh through the holder). A client attached to such a server can then tell 'this server is retired' from 'nobody is working'.
issues.why: Found on 2026-10-20 by the mesh audit while the campaign's coordinator read the mesh: the coordinator's own MCP tools majordomus_mesh_state and majordomus_mesh_cooperation answered active false with 'not active: the server no longer holds its checkout lease', while the live mesh held 38 sessions and 166 claims served by the lease holder. A worker attached to an orphaned server sees an empty mesh and can conclude that nobody holds a scope it is about to build. The milestone promises that sessions cooperate from the first turn; an attached session that cannot see its peers does not.
issues.current_state: Verified on origin/master 91c0b5d5658. apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:261-273 notices the lease file no longer carries this server's token, records crate::lease::lost(), stops the mesh and calls mesh.decline with the fixed text 'the server no longer holds its checkout lease'; the LeaseDocument it has just read (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:315-332, with pid and url) is not kept. apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/manager.rs:344-350 decline stores only that reason, and status at :562-590 answers active false with it, so every mesh read projects the same sentence. apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mesh.rs:246-256 cooperation refuses writes as not_active with that reason alone. The health report already says a lost lease outranks the standing (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/health.rs:647-655) but names no holder either. apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mesh_lease_retirement.rs:94 proves the retired server keeps its attached client and leaves the mesh; nothing asserts what that client is told. docs/MESH.md has no paragraph on a retired server.
issues.desired_state: When a server retires on a lost lease, the mesh status carries a holder object (pid, url, started_at, read from the lease at answer time so a later takeover is followed) and lost_at; the reason names the holder's URL and says to reconnect or read the mesh there. mesh.peers, mesh.state and mesh.cooperation answer through the same status, and the not_active refusal of a claim or release names the holder too. When the lease file is unreadable the answer says so instead of naming nobody. docs/MESH.md states what a retired server answers.
acceptance_criteria: Two fixture servers of one checkout, the second taking the lease: the first answers mesh.state and mesh.cooperation with active false, a holder whose url is the second server's, and lost_at
A claim through the retired server is refused as not_active and the refusal names the holder's url
Negative: a server that never had the mesh (declaration disabled, or a command-line process) answers without any holder field, so a holder is never invented
Negative: with the lease file removed after the takeover, the retired server says the holder cannot be read, and does not report an empty mesh as active

issues.title: A claim scope that is not a repository path is refused, or mapped to the record file it names, so a milestone claim excludes what it says
non_scope: Advisory board announcements of peers.rs, which refuse nothing by design
A milestone claim that also excludes every issue file of the milestone, which needs the plan inside the fold
Releasing the milestone: claims already held
issues.objective: Give the mesh one rule for a claim scope written as a namespace and a name (milestone:<id>, issue:<id>, or any other word followed by a colon): milestone:<id> and issue:<id> are mapped to .ai/repo/project/milestones/<id>.yaml and .ai/repo/project/issues/<id>.yaml before admission and in the fold, so they meet the record and anything claimed under it; any other namespaced scope is refused at admission as scope_not_a_path, naming the entry and the accepted forms. The seat scopes the cooperation rule declares (campaign/*/landing, release/seat, refs/heads/*) keep their meaning unchanged.
issues.why: Found on 2026-10-20 by the mesh audit: that day's dispatch gave four milestone owners exclusive claims with the scope milestone:<id>. Claims meet by a path test, so milestone:idd-workspace meets neither the milestone's record nor any issue file or source path: four exclusive claims that the board shows as held refuse nothing, and every owner believed the milestone was protected. The milestone promises that a stale or wrong claim never wins; a claim that silently excludes nothing loses the race it was taken to win, unseen.
issues.current_state: Verified on origin/master 91c0b5d5658. apps/majordomus-cli/src/peers.rs:314-337 claims_meet is equality or a prefix ending at a slash, after trimming slashes, so milestone:x meets only the identical string. apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/state.rs:849-852 scopes_meet and :900 admission_conflicts use it unchanged for exclusion, and the module comment at :18-19 says both machines share that one predicate. apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mesh.rs:918-927 ClaimInput documents scope as repository-relative paths, and mesh_claim at :958-978 passes input.scope to apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:3523 Cooperation::claim, which checks only conflicts (:3535) and writes ClaimAcquired with any strings at all. docs/MESH.md:291-293 says a claim is a scope of repository-relative paths, and nothing enforces it. The seat names are declared in .ai/repo/rules/project/the-cooperation-model-is-the-owners-word.v2.md:61-63 and matched in apps/majordomus-cli/src/ui/mesh.rs:49-65.
issues.desired_state: One pure function in mesh/state.rs normalises a scope entry: milestone:<id> and issue:<id> become their record paths, path-shaped entries pass as they are, and any other namespace is an error. Admission (Cooperation::claim) refuses an entry the function rejects as scope_not_a_path before anything is written, and the answer of an accepted claim lists the mapped scope it holds. The fold applies the same mapping to replicated ClaimAcquired events, so a milestone:<id> claim written by an older runtime also excludes its record. docs/MESH.md names the accepted forms and the refusal.
acceptance_criteria: An exclusive claim on milestone:idd-workspace holds the scope .ai/repo/project/milestones/idd-workspace.yaml, and a second session's exclusive claim on that file is refused as claim_conflict
An exclusive claim on issue:I2781 meets a claim on .ai/repo/project/issues/I2781.yaml
Negative: an exclusive claim on intent:anything, or on a scope with an unknown namespace, is refused as scope_not_a_path and writes no event

issues.title: Every mesh link counts its failed sync rounds, and a link whose rounds fail does not read plainly connected
non_scope: Finding and fixing why rounds fail, which is a follow-up once the counters have run
Changing the link state machine or the backoff
The /ui mesh screen, which reads the same status and follows in a later issue
issues.objective: Count sync failures per link and say them where a link is read: each PeerView carries cumulative rounds attempted and failed as the dialer, with the last error, beside the consecutive count it has today; the runtime-wide line states attempted and failed rounds so neither reads as a subset of the other; mesh doctor names a link whose recent outbound rounds mostly fail while it reads connected. This records the churn so it can be diagnosed; it does not diagnose or fix its cause.
issues.why: Found on 2026-10-20 by the mesh audit: over 27 hours the primary checkout's lease-holding server reported 153,632 completed outbound sync rounds and 153,372 failed ones, the older server 179,202 and 101,869, while every link read connected and the digests agreed. Half the rounds failing is either harmless retry noise or a link losing events and recovering through relays; today nothing lets a reader tell which link fails, how often, or since when. The milestone promises a journal that converges under any delivery order, and convergence cannot be judged on links whose failures are invisible.
issues.current_state: Verified on origin/master 91c0b5d5658. apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:320-336 keeps runtime-wide counters only; syncs_out is incremented at :2686 only after a successful round, and syncs_failed at :2621 inside the failure path, so the two are disjoint (documented at :542-545). Per peer, :2620-2627 increments failures and stores last_error, and a single successful round at :2679-2683 resets both to zero, so PeerView.failures (:416-417, 'Consecutive failed rounds') never shows an alternating link. state_of at :2866-2880 derives connected from the age of last_exchange alone, which inbound exchanges also refresh (:2053, :2195), so a link whose every outbound round fails can still read connected. apps/majordomus-cli/src/cockpit/pages.rs:3514-3519 prints '<out> out (<failed> failed)', which reads failed as part of out, and the link row at :3589-3598 shows handshakes, reconnects and the last error but no failure count. apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/doctor.rs:223 doctor_at has no check over link failures.
issues.desired_state: PeerLink and PeerView gain rounds_out and rounds_failed (cumulative for the link's life, kept across a reset of the consecutive count) and the time of the last failure; CooperationCounters says attempted as syncs_out plus syncs_failed, and the Cockpit line reads '<attempted> attempted, <failed> failed, <answered> answered'. A connected link whose failed share of outbound rounds over the last window exceeds a bound declared once in the cooperation config is reported by mesh doctor as a warning naming the peer, the share and the last error; the link state itself keeps its meaning. docs/MESH.md states the counters and the bound.
acceptance_criteria: Two fixture runtimes with a transport that fails every second outbound round: the dialer's PeerView shows rounds_out and rounds_failed in that ratio after ten rounds, while failures (consecutive) is at most one
mesh doctor over that fixture warns, naming the peer, the failed share and the last error
Negative: a fixture link with no failed round shows rounds_failed 0 and mesh doctor raises no link warning
Negative: a link that failed once and then succeeded for the whole window raises no warning, so one blip is not churn
The Cockpit line states attempted, failed and answered rounds, and its test fails on the old wording

Any percentage in the landing page's marketing copy, which homepage-check keeps refusing

issues.title: Every completed step of a session is announced on the mesh by the step itself, and the board, the monitor and the UI show it
non_scope: Announcing work in progress, which stays the session's own announcement
Replacing the board's claims, which stay what a session expects to touch
issues.objective: Make a session's completed steps reach its peers without the session remembering to say so: a commit, a push, an opened pull request, a landing, a task finished and a release tagged each publish one event to the cooperation journal under the session that made it, the board shows the session's latest step beside its claims, majordomus monitor and /cockpit/monitor stream it, and /ui/mesh shows each seat's last step and its age.
issues.why: Asked by the owner on 2026-10-20/21, repeatedly: after every completed step, consult and coordinate with the peers on the mesh, always and automatically, enforced, documented and visible in the UI and the dashboard. During that night the landing seat could not see that a records head was refused by a gate, a peer could not see that a follower had already landed a head, and steps were relayed by hand in messages that arrived minutes late. The peer board only carries what a session announces, and announcing is a step a busy session skips.
issues.current_state: The board (peers.announce, majordomus_announce, POST /api/v1/peers/announce) holds what a session chose to announce, and an announcement needs an MCP session, so a hook or a script cannot post one. majordomus monitor streams sessions, claims, handovers, reviews, the executor's merges and GitHub's runs, but not a session's own commit, push, pull request or finish. The commit and pre-push hooks (.githooks) and majordomus finish write no cooperation event.
issues.desired_state: A cooperation event kind 'step' (session, step kind, branch, commit, pull request, outcome, at) written by the post-commit and pre-push hooks, by finish, and by the landing and release paths, through the shared server when one serves the checkout and to the local journal otherwise, never blocking the step it reports. The board, the monitor and /ui/mesh read it; a seat whose last step is older than its claims' work reads stale there.
acceptance_criteria: A commit in a fixture checkout with a shared server publishes one step event naming the session, the branch and the commit, and majordomus monitor prints it
A push and an opened pull request each publish their step, and /ui/mesh shows the seat's last step and its age
With no shared server the step is written to the local journal and the commit or push still succeeds, unchanged in time beyond its bound
Negative: a failed commit or a refused push publishes a step whose outcome says refused, never success

issues.title: A page written by hand is never resolved as derived: the merge=derived globs name only what a generator writes
non_scope: Changing how scripts/merge-derived resolves a path that is derived
Moving the generated pages out of site/content
issues.objective: Make the merge=derived attribute true of every path it covers: each path .gitattributes resolves with scripts/merge-derived is one that scripts/derive or majordomus generate writes, and a page a person writes is merged as text, so a merge never drops one side of a hand edit.
issues.why: Found on 2026-10-21 while splitting the campaign records into source and derived paths. site/content/roadmap.md is written by hand (no generator writes it and site/content-src holds no copy), yet the glob site/content/*.md marks it merge=derived. scripts/merge-derived resolves such a path to ours and only warns that it is stale, so a merge of two branches that both edit the roadmap prose keeps one side and drops the other without a conflict, and the next derive does not restore it because nothing derives it.
issues.current_state: The .gitattributes line site/content/*.md merge=derived covers every top-level page. Most come from site/content-src through scripts/generate-site-data and _index.md is written by the generator, but site/content/roadmap.md has no source anywhere, and changelog.md, getting-started.md, limitations.md and policy.md have no site/content-src counterpart and are not yet traced. No gate compares the merge=derived set with the set a derive writes.
issues.desired_state: Each merge=derived pattern matches only paths a derive writes, and a gate refuses a tracked path the attribute resolves as derived when a derive does not write it, naming the path. issues.title: A session's mesh claims outlive a lease takeover of the server it made them on
non_scope: Fencing an exclusive claim against a returning holder, which is I3174
The bridge's replay of board announcements after a re-attach, which is I3609
issues.objective: Keep a session's claims live across a lease takeover of the shared server: a claim stays held while any instance of the same node and runtime beats and its session re-opens on that runtime within the busy grace plus one expiry, keeping its original acquisition order; it expires at that bound when the session never comes back, and an instance of another runtime never keeps it alive. Implemented by f8, who holds mesh-journal-converges and found the cause (claim c-f1818acaf75b; its first key c-b50ea7240ad4 was itself dropped by a takeover, the bug demonstrated a fifth time).
issues.why: On 2026-10-20 the shared server of the primary checkout restarted at about 20:34Z, and 9c had to tell every worker to re-claim (d3's milestone:M004 among them); it was then taken over four more times (22:10, 22:25, 22:27 and 22:36Z, each a 'superseded lease' in the server log), after a rebuilt target/debug/majordomus or a newer release won the lease. The old server hands its MCP sessions on (I2127) and stops; its mesh stream <node>-<runtime>-<instance> stops beating, and the fold expires every claim on it, although the mesh session id and the runtime id are the same on the successor and only the instance changed. Every exclusive milestone claim of the sessions it served lapsed while they went on working (session d3 re-claimed its four twice by hand; 9c had to tell every worker), and an exclusive claim that silently lapses is the lock it exists to be until the next worker takes the same milestone.
issues.current_state: A claim belongs to the stream of the runtime instance that accepted it; when that stream expires, its claims expire with it. A lease takeover changes the instance and keeps the node, the runtime and the session ids, so every claim it carried is dropped while its session is attached to the successor. Compaction then removes the dead instance's stream entirely: claims c-b50ea7240ad4, c-bc52b94b7b8f and c-fc1d262e7914 were absent from the state on 2026-10-21, not merely expired.
issues.desired_state: The fold keeps a claim held while an instance of its node and runtime beats and its session re-opens on that runtime within busy grace + one expiry; the claim keeps its acquisition order, so a later claim from another runtime still conflicts with it; it expires at the bound when its session never re-attaches; no new event kind is introduced; it is independent of I3174's fencing epochs. A session re-opens on the successor without its client doing anything: the server that takes the lease reads its predecessor instances' active sessions and re-opens, on its own stream, each one whose client process (I3810) still exists on this machine; a session that only holds claims and says nothing is therefore carried, and one whose client has ended is not.
acceptance_criteria: A claim survives a lease takeover once its session re-attaches to the successor, and a later claim from another runtime conflicts with it
A claim expires at busy grace + one expiry when its session never re-attaches
An instance of a different runtime does not keep the claim alive
Compaction keeps a dead instance's stream while a claim on it is carried by a live instance of the same runtime, and drops it once that claim ends

issues.title: A mesh session whose client process has ended is closed by the runtime that holds it
non_scope: A claim surviving a lease takeover, which is I3798
Review requests that never lapse, which is I3608
Sessions of the board projection (board-pN), which already close when their peer detaches
issues.objective: A mesh session names the client process it belongs to (its process id and start time, read by the hook that opens it on the same machine), and the runtime that holds the session closes it (SessionClosed, once) when that process no longer exists, so the session's claims end by the fold's existing rule (\"its session closed\") instead of being held for as long as the runtime beats. Implemented by f8 (779cc015), holder of mesh-journal-converges, under claim c-7fcc9fbf8956.
issues.why: On 2026-10-21 dev-03 found exclusive claim c-e75ccd4c731d (node 5d81b5c9, I2720 scope, refs/heads/feature/self-update-wraps-the-installer) reading held, and nobody could release it: other runtimes are refused not_own and the holder is not reachable. The fold showed its stream live (beat 5 s before) and its session claude-code-9ab8a13c active, although its client had gone. A provider session joins the mesh once, in its start hook (lib/capture.sh mj_capture_mesh_join), and leaves in its end hook; a client that crashes or is killed never runs the end hook, and nothing else ties the session to its client: connection episodes are attached under a client-chosen id with provider `generic` and never under the mesh session's id, so a reaped episode cannot say which mesh session it carried. On a long-lived runtime such a session is active for ever, and its exclusive claims block every other worker.
issues.current_state: mesh.session.open records the session's client, branch, head, task and intent, and nothing about the process it belongs to. The session ends only by an explicit `mesh session close` or when its runtime stops beating.
issues.desired_state: The start hook passes the client process's id and start time to `mesh session open`, and the session carries them (optional fields, so a session opened without them behaves as today). The runtime holding a session checks, on its own machine and its own clock, whether that process still exists with that start time, and appends SessionClosed once when it does not; a process id reused by another process is not mistaken for the client. The fold, admission and other runtimes are unchanged. I3798 reads the same fields to re-open a predecessor's live sessions after a takeover.
acceptance_criteria: A session whose recorded client process has ended is closed once by its runtime, and its exclusive claim then reads expired (its session closed) on every runtime
A session whose client process is alive stays open, and so do its claims
A process id reused by a different process (another start time) does not keep the session open
A session opened without a client process behaves exactly as before

issues.objective: majordomus prs service install, run by the owner, writes a user service (launchd on macOS, systemd --user on Linux) through the one unit writer I2722 owns, running prs drain --continuous for this checkout; prs service status and uninstall manage it. The unit restarts the executor after an exit that is a crash or an outage, and never after a halt (an unverified landing) or a refusal, which keeps the halt of ADR 0101 D7 and the outage bound (CONTINUOUS_TRANSIENT_LIMIT, drain.rs:1886) in force. It logs under the local half and is never written without the owner running the command.
issues.why: The landing loop of 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-22 lived inside an agent session, so it died with the session and the machine, and every landing a session attempted met the auto-mode classifier. A service outside agent sessions answers both; a review of this plan found that a service restarting without limit would undo the halt.
issues.current_state: No launchd or systemd unit for the executor exists; prs drain runs only on demand; I2722 plans the user-unit writer for the hub.
issues.desired_state: After install the executor runs and lands the next green head; killing it restarts it; a halt or a refusal leaves it stopped and status says why; uninstall leaves nothing behind.
acceptance_criteria: install writes one unit naming this checkout through I2722's writer; a second install changes nothing
A killed executor is restarted; an exit by halt or refusal is not (case a_halted_executor_is_not_restarted, proven without a service manager)
status reports running or not, the last decision and its time; uninstall removes the unit

issues.title: A combined top is composed by a typed command from members declared in a tracked train manifest
issues.objective: majordomus prs compose builds a combined top from a tracked train manifest under .ai/repo/integration/trains/ that lists its members (a branch head or a source patch, with its seat, its issue and its order constraints) and its base. It composes them in order on a scratch index, names each member that does not apply, and only then runs one derive and opens or updates the train pull request. Two machines composing the same manifest produce the same member list and the same tree before the derive; the derived output is the derive's, which ADR 0101 does not hold deterministic per tree.
issues.why: Trains 3a, 3b and 4 were composed by shell scripts under ~/.cache/mj-e7 and ~/.cache/mj-a3; when the seats holding them died on 2026-10-22 the next seat had to reconstruct the order from a ledger, and each train needed two or three fix commits for reds the composition could have found.

issues.desired_state: A seat composes a train with one command from its manifest; another seat on another machine composes the same pre-derive tree from the same manifest.
acceptance_criteria: compose applies the manifest's members in order on a scratch index and names each member that does not apply
Two compositions of one manifest give the same member list and the same pre-derive tree (case a_train_manifest_composes_one_tree)
No member order is read from a session cache

Committing the record from CI; refreshing it stays a reviewed change

On 2026-10-22 the record held 410 of 602 cases, an unrecorded case weighed a guessed 300 s against a median of 9, and run 39762797718's shards ran 87, 52, 82 and 43 minutes. issues.title: The rustdoc composition case proves its composition on a small site, not on the whole one
non_scope: scripts/site-build and scripts/site-check, whose behaviour the case measures and does not change

issues.title: Every pull request carries its metadata, projected from the trunk's records: labels, milestone, assignee and Refs links, never a closing keyword
non_scope: Auto-merge or any landing; the integration executor lands

issues.objective: A pull request's metadata is a projection of the trunk's records, applied by scripts/github-sync --prs locally and by a separate workflow file (not github.yml) on pull_request_target opened, edited, synchronize and labeled, which checks out the base branch only, never the head, and holds pull-requests: write and issues: read with GITHUB_TOKEN, in a concurrency group per pull request. The rule the-projection-is-applied-at-landing moves to version 2 and .ai/repo/ci/github.yaml's forbidden list is amended: the issue projection still never runs for a pull request, while the pull request projection writes only the pull request's own labels, milestone, assignee and managed region, read from the trunk; case 1097 holds the new workflow to its model. The issues a pull request serves are the ones its title and head branch name, resolved by the executable through delivery's named_by (plan/delivery.rs:428-450, wrapping issues_named in ui/prs.rs:174) exposed as a typed subcommand github-sync calls, never a second shell pattern. It projects: a type label from the conventional type of its title, from the commit types I3979 declares (feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, chore, ci, style, build); an area label from the commit scope only when the scope is declared there; the highest priority label of the served issues; train for an integration/train-* head; records when every changed path is under .ai/repo/project; hold and collision:accepted stay a person's. The milestone is the GitHub milestone github-sync already projects for the served issue's milestone; the author is assignee when none is set; a managed region between majordomus:begin and majordomus:end markers lists Refs #<n> for each served issue that has a GitHub issue, and the record id in plain text, with no priority or milestone, for one whose record exists only in the head. GitHub issue numbers come from a record-to-number map the trunk run of github.yml publishes, so a pull request event makes a bounded number of API calls and never lists every issue. No projected text carries a closing keyword (close, fix or resolve followed by an issue number). A second run changes nothing; a region whose hash no longer matches what was written is left alone and reported; a pull request whose token cannot write is reported and passes. Starts after train 4 lands its github-sync listing rewrite (the I3920 record, on chore/landing-survives-any-session), which then becomes a dependency.
issues.why: The owner asked on 2026-10-22 for every pull request to carry its metadata, kept current automatically and offloaded to GitHub, as prismatic-platform does. Today the label set of a pull request is what its author typed: hold, collision:accepted and ci:yielded are read by code (integration/classify.rs, scripts/ci/collision-gate) and set by hand, and no pull request names the GitHub issue its record is projected to. A full listing per pull request event would repeat the truncation of 2026-10-22 and hit the rate limit (github.yaml measured 111 s for one read of 271 issues; there are now about 1384).

issues.title: An exclusive mesh claim lives by its holder's progress: a session stuck on a dialog, hung or crashed stops refusing others while its server beats on
non_scope: Adding session_ttl_seconds to .ai/repo/mesh/majordomus.yaml: an older executable refuses a key it does not know
A new EVENT_VERSION: an older runtime stores and relays session_beat opaque and keeps the stream rule
Closing a silent session: an idle session holding nothing is healthy
Take-over or fencing of a suspended claim's resumed holder: waits for the epoch of I3174
The integration lease: I3991
A monitor signal for a suspension: it is a reading of time, not a journal event; mesh.state and the board show it
issues.objective: Add a second layer of mesh liveness under the stream beat: a session that does real work (an MCP request other than ping and notifications/*, an announcement, a claim, or an explicit mesh.beat with the phase a long-running process is in) has a session_beat written for it carrying cooperation.session_ttl_seconds (default 600); every runtime ages the newest beat on its own clock and reads a held exclusive claim of a session silent past its ttl (plus the expiry on any runtime but the holder's) as suspended, refusing nobody, until the session beats again. Sessions are never closed for silence, advisory claims are untouched, and nothing is taken over or fenced (that waits for I3174's epoch). A session that never beat keeps the stream rule.
issues.why: The owner ordered on 2026-10-22 that no work may stall because a peer waits on a permission dialog, crashed or hung. That day the executor of seat 5d held the integration lease, an exclusive mesh claim, for hours and never answered; the claim stayed live because a claim lived while its runtime beat, and the runtime beat on while the worker behind it waited on nobody. The stdio bridge pings every 20 s whatever its client is doing, so nothing a stalled client sends could tell the mesh it had stopped. The design — suspend claims, never close sessions; a typed beat with a phase for long-running processes; one rule for every transport; advisory-first — is the approved mesh review fc/p7 of 2026-10-23.
issues.current_state: mesh::state::fold expires a claim only when it is released, its session closes, or its stream stops beating (ADR 0067 decisions 7 and 8, rule project.mesh-cooperation-is-authenticated version 1). A session's last MCP message, ping included, refreshes its place on the board and nothing else.
issues.desired_state: An exclusive claim of a session whose worker stops making progress reads suspended within cooperation.session_ttl_seconds on its holder's runtime and within that ttl plus the expiry everywhere else, while its runtime keeps beating; the scope is admitted to the next claimant; mesh.state, mesh.peers (with each session's progress age and phase), the Cockpit and /ui/mesh say so; a process waiting on CI keeps its claim with majordomus mesh beat --phase; a command-line claim that never beats and a claim of an older runtime are judged exactly as before.
acceptance_criteria: A held exclusive claim of a session whose newest session beat is older than its ttl (plus the expiry on a foreign runtime) reads suspended while its runtime beats, its advisory claim and the session stay as they were, and admission no longer refuses on it (mesh::state tests a_silent_exclusive_claim_is_suspended_while_its_runtime_beats, a_silent_exclusive_claim_refuses_nobody)

A beat within its ttl holds the claim, a session that never beat keeps the stream rule, and the digest of one silence is the same on every read (a_beat_within_its_ttl_holds_the_claim, a_session_that_never_beat_keeps_the_stream_rule, silence_reads_the_same_digest_twice)

issues.title: A task started before the first commit finishes: an unborn recorded head is an ancestor of every commit
non_scope: mj_git_touched with a base of NONE, which counts only uncommitted paths for the scope doctrine; a separate issue if the scope of such a task must see its commits
A task whose branch changes between start and finish, which stays different_context
issues.objective: mj_git_label (lib/common.sh) labels a recorded head of NONE, which mj_git_head writes when start runs on an unborn branch, as advanced once the branch has commits, so the state doctrine passes and check and a completed finish are no longer refused for a history that was never rewritten. start's refusal of a second task names the commands that release the first: finish, or handover --close.
issues.why: On 2026-10-23 an adopter of a new repository (majordomus-reel, task t-20261023002255-4d5b) ran majordomus start --scope . before the first commit. start recorded head NONE; after the first commits mj_git_label asked git merge-base --is-ancestor NONE HEAD, which fails for a name that is not a revision, and fell through to diverged. mj_validate_state turned that into a refusal, and state is in verification.finish_requires, so every check and every finish was refused for good and the task could not be closed. The refusal of a second start told the user to run majordomus handover, which does not release the task without --close. A supported release for the stuck task already existed, majordomus handover --close (lib/handover.sh), and the first diagnosis (a handover does not release a task, so there is no supported way out) missed that flag; the adopter was released with it, and the state doctrine is fixed so that no adopter needs it.
issues.current_state: lib/common.sh mj_git_label returns diverged for a recorded head of NONE once HEAD exists; lib/start.sh names majordomus handover as a way out of an active task.
issues.desired_state: A task started on an unborn branch reads advanced after its commits, check passes the state doctrine and a completed finish succeeds; the start refusal names finish and handover --close.
acceptance_criteria: In a fresh repository, start --scope . before the first commit, two commits, then check passes with state advanced and finish --outcome completed succeeds
With the NONE line of mj_git_label removed, the case fails at check with state diverged

issues.title: A node's provisioning secret is read on mc's standard input, never from a command line
non_scope: A gate and rule that refuse a secret on any command line the repository runs (I4224, train 8)
Rotating identities: none was ever created through the argv form
issues.objective: mesh build-cache provision creates a node's MinIO identity with `mc admin user add <alias> <access key>` and passes the secret on the command's standard input. That is mc's own documented form (minio/mc cmd/admin-user-add.go, fetchUserKeys), so the secret is in no process's argv.
issues.why: Found in review of I2674 (#2402) on 2026-10-23, and on master since train 6 (b62848cb6f5): apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cache_provision.rs appended each node's generated secret to the argv of `mc admin user add`. Every user of the provider host can read an argv in ps and /proc/<pid>/cmdline for as long as the call runs. The intent this milestone serves says no credential appears in a process's environment, a log or an answer, and an argument is all three at once. Only `mesh build-cache provision --apply` on a provider host runs the call, and none has been run (lundra, the intended host, has not been provisioned), so no secret has been exposed and none needs rotating.
issues.current_state: Measured at master b62848cb6f5 on 2026-10-25: run_steps builds `mc --quiet admin user add <alias> mesh-cache-<node>`, pushes the secret onto that argv (cache_provision.rs:908-909), and the runner gives the child no standard input.
issues.desired_state: The identity step's argv ends at the access key. The runner writes the secret, followed by a newline, to the child's standard input and closes it. Every other command gets a null standard input. The step's printed line names where the secret goes, never the secret itself.
acceptance_criteria: With a recording runner, no argv of any command the apply runs contains any node's secret, and each node's secret, followed by a newline, is the standard input of exactly its own admin user add
The real runner gives a stand-in mc the input on its standard input and nothing on its command line; a command given no input reads an empty, closed standard input

issues.title: A client that re-attaches and repeats its named claim keeps one departed row, not one per reconnect

issues.objective: An announce of a named claim drops the departed slots of the same worker (same client name and address) whose every claim it now holds under the same name, so a client that re-attaches on a timer no longer fills the board's departed retention and evicts the sessions that really left.
issues.why: On 2026-10-25 at 12:20Z the primary checkout's shared server (port 57351) listed 41 peers: 9 attached and 32 departed, and all 32 departed rows (p200-p232, last seen 0.5-5.6 h earlier) were one codex-chatgpt-mesh-coordinator bridge that re-attaches every ~10 minutes and announces the same claim chatgpt-bridge. The board keeps RETAINED = 32 departed slots (apps/majordomus-cli/src/peers.rs), dropping the oldest past that, so every real session that departed had its retained announcement evicted within one reconnect: the very thing retention exists to keep.

issues.desired_state: PeerBoard::announce_claim, for a named claim, removes departed slots with the announcer's client name and address (both absent counts as equal) whose claims are all named claims the announcer holds under the same names. A departed slot of the same client name at a different address is kept
issues.risk: A departed row is dropped only when a newer row of the same client and address holds every claim it held under the same names, so nothing it said is lost; the newer row carries the current text of those claims.

issues.title: A CI runner's home stays under its cap during a job, not only between jobs
non_scope: disk-guard's runner homes and the runner units' drop-ins (I4352)
Reclaiming outside cargo's lock on a developer machine (I4354)
issues.objective: Bound a self-hosted runner's build directory inside a job, not only around it. The build host policy gives each runner home's build directory a filesystem of its own size, a loop-mounted ext4 image or an XFS project quota the provision creates from the policy's per-home cap, so a job that outgrows it fails with ENOSPC inside its own home while the root filesystem keeps its floor. Around that hard bound: on runner.environment == 'self-hosted', .github/actions/setup-rust runs the build directory bound (mj_rust_bound_build_dir) before cargo and again in a post step; scripts/rust-coverage removes llvm-cov-target on a self-hosted runner once its report is exported; and every job that builds on a self-hosted runner samples its build directory every 30 s and writes the job summary facts `build-dir size` and `build-dir peak`.
issues.why: Incident 1 of 2026-10-28: lundra's root filesystem reached 100% under the runners' cargo build directories, /home/ghrunner/home-2 and home-3/.cargo/build-shared (74.6 and 39.9 GiB, as measured for I4352), and runners lundra-1..3 went offline during run 40680986818. Three hand-provisioned runner homes each keep an unbounded build directory. I4352 (fix/lundra-provisions-its-runners, not landed) renders the homes and the runner drop-ins and makes disk-guard reclaim a runner build directory over its cap once it is idle; it sets no quota, and a coverage job that fills tens of GiB inside one run never becomes idle. A bound applied before and after cargo is also only a bound between invocations. I3959's bound runs only where lib/rust_bin.sh is the entry, and #2567 never reaches CI.

issues.desired_state: A runner home's build directory cannot outgrow its cap during a job: the job fails with ENOSPC in its own home and the root filesystem keeps its floor; around the hard bound a self-hosted job evicts idle units before cargo and after it, a coverage run leaves no llvm-cov-target behind, and each job's summary carries the peak it reached. issues.title: Every sweep that deletes asks one liveness predicate, and it fails closed
non_scope: Keeping an executable of a reclaimed worktree's generation (the review's N22, not filed in this block)
Which homes disk-guard sweeps (I4352)
issues.objective: scripts/reap-orphans --targets, `majordomus worktree cleanup` and the build host's disk-guard decide liveness through one typed capability, worktree.liveness (`majordomus worktree liveness <path>`, declared in the worktree module and implemented in apps/majordomus-cli/src/worktree/liveness.rs), which answers keep or reclaim with its reason. worktree cleanup calls it in process; reap-orphans and disk-guard call the executable, disk-guard through the path disk-guard.service hands it, and keep everything when that executable is absent. A tree or build directory is live if a mesh or board claim names it, an open majordomus task exists in it, the derive lock's owner names it, a queue pid file or a running runner job names it, another process's CARGO_*_DIR or MAJORDOMUS_BIN points into it, or its index, HEAD or reflog changed within the idle window; an unreadable claim source or stat counts as live. No new shell unit is added.
issues.why: Incident 11 of 2026-10-28: at 21:43 reap-orphans deleted a live worktree's target, which held the only copy of the executable its hooks require under ADR 0224, and every hook then refused with exit 12. reap-orphans decides liveness from cwd and argv only, which a session working through absolute paths never shows, and each deleting sweep defines liveness its own way. I3832 (the worktree sweep) is not on master and would add a third definition; I4324 widens the risk; once I4352 lands, disk-guard sweeps the runner homes too, so a wrong answer there takes a running CI job's build directory. ADR 0069 makes new automation a typed or scripted capability, which is why the predicate is a capability and not a shell file beside disk-guard. It sits in development-runtime with I3959 (the shared build directory's bound) and I3836 (the delivery.json half of incident 11), not in the-runtime-supervises-itself, which derives as blocked behind failure-is-visible and runtime-lifecycle and would hold the lundra 24/7 chain (I4345 depends on this issue).

issues.desired_state: One capability answers keep or reclaim with its reason for every deleting sweep; a declared mesh whose claims cannot be read removes nothing and exits non-zero; disk-guard without the executable removes no build directory; reclaim-only-what-you-own v2 is blocking and names the capability. Enforced by cases 611 and 276, blocking, a unit test of the predicate, and the rule.

issues.objective: An exclusive claim for a session nobody opened is refused with session_unknown, naming `mesh session open --client-pid auto`, instead of opening the session implicitly; `mesh claim` sends client_pid and client_started, accepted only when the serving runtime is on the caller's machine; claim() reads the fold back and returns an error carrying the state when the claim is not Held; a claim sent to a runtime that holds only a closed record of a session live elsewhere is refused or forwarded; an exclusive claim also excludes by its issue field; mj_mesh_task_claim stops ignoring the answer. No beat-only suspension is introduced until CLI holders have an automatic beat source.
issues.why: Incidents 6 and 9 of 2026-10-28. The exclusive release/seat claim c-56b837289bb0 stayed live for more than 14 hours on the launchd hub: claim() silently opened an unknown session name (a hand-shortened id, run from another repository), so the session had no client_pid and the I3810 reaper never saw it, and the hub never dies (KeepAlive, --idle 0); I3990 applies only to board sessions, and I3810, I3174, #2410 and #2380 do not cover it. In the id collisions (I4251, #2601 against #2605), a claim made through a stale runtime's closed session returned Written and expired at once. A beat-only TTL would suspend a 4.5-hour release mid-cut, so the remedy is binding, not a shorter lease.
issues.current_state: Measured at 81ef931a3e1: claim() in apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs (line 4184) opens an unknown session on demand; lib/common.sh's mj_mesh_task_claim (line 2063) runs the claim and does not read its answer; rule project.an-exclusive-claim-lives-by-its-holders-progress is v1.
issues.desired_state: No exclusive claim exists without a known session bound to a live process on its runtime's machine, and a caller is never told Written for a claim that is not Held. Enforced by the admission refusals, the Rust tests, case 3990 and the rule at v2.

Rust test: a claim whose folded state is not Held makes claim() return an error carrying the state, not Written
Rust test: with s1 live on runtime A and a closed s1 record on runtime B, a claim through B does not answer Written
Rust test: the same issue claimed exclusively under two different scopes is refused, naming the holder

issues.title: Issue, ADR and case numbers are reserved atomically at origin and checked at landing
non_scope: Renumbering ids that already collided
issues.objective: `next --kind issue|adr|case --reserve` reserves a number by creating refs/ids/<kind>/<n> on the forge (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs -f ref=refs/ids/<kind>/<n> -f sha=<commit>`), which fails atomically with 422 when the ref exists and runs no local hook, and takes the next number on that refusal; .githooks/pre-push skips refs/ids/* as it skips refs/majordomus/*, so a reservation that does reach origin through git does no hook work; a required landing check refuses an id that is already on master or reserved under different content; the identifier gates (collision-check, adr-collision, case-numbers) run in a job that needs only plan, is exempt from the first-red cancel and checks out blobless.
issues.why: Incident 6 of 2026-10-28: I4251 was taken by both #2601 and #2605, and I4296 by both #2633 and the deployed-stage worker. Ids come from one global sequence and nothing reserves a number atomically: the mechanisms are advisory (the board; `--advisory` claims followed by `|| true`), eventually consistent (one admission mutex per runtime), or detect too late (the collision gate runs behind the build and is lost when the run cancels itself). I3974 plans a survey allocator, and ADR 0168 collided even with a survey; on 2026-10-29 the block I4340-I4359 claimed on the mesh was found already used by I4340, I4350 and I4352 in uncommitted work of three other worktrees.
issues.current_state: Measured at 81ef931a3e1: lib/adr.sh and scripts/case-numbers survey this tree, the sibling worktrees, the refs and the board; nothing pushes a reservation to origin; scripts/ci/collision-gate runs inside the validate jobs that build; .githooks/pre-push skips only refs/majordomus/* and delete-only pushes, so any other ref push runs `finish --check`, case-numbers and run-plan (its own comment records a rescue-ref push spending 3490 s in run-plan).
issues.desired_state: Two concurrent reservations of one number give one success and one next number; a pull request adding an id already on master or reserved under other content is refused without a build; the identifier half of rule project.work-is-claimed-before-it-is-built is blocking. Enforced by cases 560, 566 and 4357, the landing check and the rule.
acceptance_criteria: Case 4357 against a stub forge answering 201 once and 422 after: two concurrent reservations of n give one success and one n+1
Case 4357: a reservation runs no hook work: no `finish --check`, case-numbers or run-plan is invoked, and a push of only refs/ids/* through .githooks/pre-push exits 0 without them
Case 4357: a replay of #2605 (a second I4251.yaml) exits 11 from the identifier job, with no build job run
Case 566: the identifier job's needs are a subset of {plan} and it carries no first-red self-cancel
Case 560 passes, and the rule's identifier half is class blocking
I3974 records that its survey approach is superseded by this reservation

issues.title: A seat is taken by `start --seat` under its provider session, kept between that session's tasks and lost with it, and an unbound seat is named by the doctor
non_scope: Binding a claim to its holder's process (I4356)
Recording and replicating the provider_session digest, and refusing the seat's finish while a release is overdue (I3072)
A beat-only TTL, which would suspend a 4.5-hour release mid-cut
issues.objective: `majordomus start --seat release|landing|repair` takes, or keeps, the seat's exclusive claim under the mesh session that carries the task's provider_session digest, so I3072's derived join (a task is the seat's when release/seat is held by a mesh session whose provider_session equals the one start recorded) finds the seat's task with nothing declared; a start with no observable provider session is refused the seat. finish and abandon do not drop the claim at once: they shorten its expiry to a grace, and a `start --seat` of the same provider session inside the grace keeps it, so the seat never reads vacant between one session's tasks (I3072's reason) while a session that has stopped loses it within the grace. A mesh doctor check, unbound_exclusive_claims, fails on an exclusive claim whose provider session has no open task past the grace, naming the claim's runtime URL and the exact release command; the scope seat/release is refused as scope_not_a_seat; the hub's served version is checked against the newest tag. The cooperation rule says seats are taken this way, at v3.
issues.why: Incident 9 of 2026-10-28: the exclusive release/seat claim c-56b837289bb0 stayed live for more than 14 hours on the launchd hub, held by a session that had stopped, and nothing named it; it is still held until the owner releases it on :8791. A seat is taken today by a bare mesh claim (majordomus_mesh_claim), so its lifetime is tied to the stream of the runtime that served it rather than to any task or session, and no finish ever gives it back. I3072 (open, p1) owns the join between a task and the release seat and decided that the join is derived from the provider session, never declared, and that a seat held by each release task would read vacant between tasks and invite a second session; this issue takes the seat through that join instead of a CLI session task-<id>, and keeps it across one session's tasks.
issues.current_state: Measured at 81ef931a3e1: lib/start.sh and lib/finish.sh take and give back no seat; no task record names its provider session (I3072); apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/doctor.rs has no check of exclusive claims without a task; the cooperation rule is v2, and cases 3150 and 3824 hold its file name, `version: 2` and the 'Work moves through seats' paragraph of the provider templates and the generated bootstraps.
issues.desired_state: A seat lives as long as the provider session that took it keeps working, plus a grace; the doctor fails while an exclusive claim outlives that grace without a task, naming how to release it; the hub serving a version older than the newest tag past its bound is a finding; the rule, the provider templates and the bootstraps say seats are taken with `start --seat`. Enforced by case 4358, the doctor check, case 3472 (I3072's join) and the cooperation rule at v3 with cases 3150 and 3824.
acceptance_criteria: Case 4358: `start --seat release` with a provider session takes release/seat under the mesh session carrying that session's digest, and I3072's join names the task as the seat's; without an observable provider session it is refused, naming why

Case 4358: finish shortens the seat claim's expiry to the grace; a `start --seat release` of the same provider session inside the grace keeps the claim, and none leaves it Expired after the grace; abandon does the same
Case 4358: a `start --seat release` of another provider session while the claim is held is refused with claim_conflict, naming the holder
Case 4358: the doctor fails on a fixture exclusive claim whose provider session has no open task past the grace, naming its runtime URL and the release command
Case 4358: the scope seat/release is refused as scope_not_a_seat

Cases 3150 and 3824 pass on v3: the rule file is the-cooperation-model-is-the-owners-word.v3.md with `version: 3`, and the 'Work moves through seats' paragraph in each provider template and in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md, regenerated by `majordomus update`, says a seat is taken with `start --seat`
docs/RELEASE.md and docs/MESH.md name `start --seat release` as how the release seat is taken, and neither tells a session to take release/seat with a bare mesh claim
